report.title: "Roll Tide, and I Mean That as a Threat": MK Strickland Hosts Homecoming
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Roll Tide, darling, and I mean that as a greeting. Mostly. I'm Mary-Kathryn Strickland, but everyone from the Quad to the press box calls me MK. I rode for the Tide equestrian team, I read blitz pickups the way some girls read Southern Living, and I can quote a legendary coaching maxim for every situation, perfectly, usually at dinner. My family has asked me to stop. I will not stop. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little belle-of-the-ball polish. When we win, you'll hear "Roll Tide" in seventeen different tones, each more satisfied than the last. When we lose, I'll say "We will not speak of it," and I will not speak of it. This week, I'll make an exception. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Alabama claims 18 national championships, 13 of them wire-service titles from the poll era [S7]. Paul "Bear" Bryant won six from 1958 to 1982, and Nick Saban won six more between 2007 and 2023 [S7]. The Tide's Heisman winners are Mark Ingram II (2009), Derrick Henry (2015), DeVonta Smith (2020) and Bryce Young (2021) [S7]. Alabama has 30 SEC championships, an NCAA-record 79 bowl appearances and 46 bowl wins, also a record [S7], plus a record 16 straight 10-win seasons from 2008 through 2023 [S7]. Bryant-Denny Stadium seats 101,821 and opened in 1929 [S3]. Coach Bryant has a maxim for this, and I'll save it for dinner.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kalen DeBoer was hired Jan. 12, 2024 [S3], and his first two Tide teams went 9-4 and 11-4 [S3]. This season's offense started like a debutante's waltz: 48, 45, 50, 49 and 56 points in the first five wins [S3]. Then came 17 against Georgia and 10 at Tennessee [S3]. Overall, Alabama scores 39.3 points a game (12th) and throws for 252.7 yards (48th) [S5]. The defense allows 107 rushing yards a game (30th) and is plus-5 in turnovers (15th), with 16 takeaways [S5][S3]. The weak spots are pass defense, 230.9 yards allowed (101st), and red zone defense, where opponents score 95.7% of the time (134th) [S5]. Every ball gown has a loose thread, darling. We sew.

4. Players to Know

• QB Keelon Russell: 129 of 191, 1,746 yards, 12 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. At Tennessee he was 19 of 29 for 147 yards with two interceptions and scored on a 19-yard run [S11].
• RB Trae'shawn Brown: 313 yards on 57 carries, 5 TD [S4][S5].
• WR Ryan Coleman-Williams: 23 catches, 415 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. He missed Tennessee with several injuries, including a concussion, per AP [S11], and an aggregator lists him out with a knee injury as of Oct. 17 . Status for Saturday: not official.
• LB Caleb Woodson: a team-high 53 tackles [S4]. LB Yhonzae Pierre: 3.5 sacks [S4]. DB Bray Hubbard: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Alabama is 5-2 and 3-2 in the SEC, 3-1 at home [S3], and No. 13 in both polls [S3]. The losses were 20-17 to Georgia and 26-10 at Tennessee [S3]. We have lost back-to-back regular-season games for the first time since 2007 [S11]. After this game comes an open date, then a Nov. 7 trip to LSU [S9][S5]. Homecoming against an SEC visitor is precisely the right occasion to straighten our pearls [S9].

6. This Week: Texas A&M (4-3) at No. 13 Alabama (5-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bryant-Denny Stadium · ABC [S1][S5][S8]. Homecoming [S9].
Last week: we lost 26-10 at Tennessee with 201 yards, 54 rushing, and four turnovers [S11]. "The key was they were able to run the football," Coach DeBoer said [S11]. Texas A&M beat The Citadel 41-0 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: the Aggies are good on defense, 17.1 points allowed (27th), 164.1 passing yards allowed (10th) and 29.8% on third down (11th) [S5]. Their pass rush has just 5 sacks [S2], which should give Russell time.
Their offense vs. our defense: Texas A&M averages 356.9 yards (97th) and 195.7 passing (103rd) [S5]. In two SEC road games, it scored 6 points each time [S2]. Marcel Reed has 7 touchdowns and 6 interceptions [S5]. Our run defense, 30th, wants to make him throw [S5].
Series: Alabama leads 13-3 [S9][S10] and is 7-1 against the Aggies from 2016 through 2025 [S3]. The last meeting was a 26-20 win in College Station in 2023 [S9]. The only Aggie win in Tuscaloosa came in 2012, and we've won five straight at home since [S9].
Availability: per an aggregator dated Oct. 17, Coleman-Williams (knee) and WR A.J. Walker are out and TE Jay Ford is questionable (arm) . For A&M, WRs Mario Craver and A.J. Bethel-Roman are questionable . The SEC's first official report comes Oct. 21 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Ball security: four turnovers at Tennessee can't happen twice [S11]. (2) Red zone defense, our weakest number [S5]. (3) Whether our receivers are healthy enough to stretch a top-10 pass defense [S5].
And Colt Wendeborn, Texas A&M's insider: Howdy right back, sugar. Bryant-Denny is lovely this time of year. Roll Tide.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Tuscaloosa for homecoming? Brown's Corner on University Boulevard is a nice place for brunch before the parade.

report.title: "Pedigree Tells": Rhett Abernathy-Coyle Welcomes the Commodores to Kroger Field
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Pedigree tells. Good evening, friends, I'm Rhett Abernathy-Coyle. I grew up on a horse farm out past Keeneland, mucking stalls before school and watching yearlings run in the morning mist. I learned early that you can tell a great deal about a horse from its bloodlines, and I grade football players the same way a Derby breeder grades a foal. I travel with the Wildcats and I live with the Wildcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a Southern gentleman's flourish. When we win, you'll hear my best Derby announcer: "And down the stretch they come!" When we lose, I'll say, "Even the best horses stumble," and adjust my hat. Now, pull up a chair, and let's talk bloodlines. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Wildcats represent the University of Kentucky in the SEC [S7]. Home is Kroger Field in Lexington [S7], opened in 1973 and listed at 61,000 seats [S3]. The last five seasons: a fine 10-3 in 2021, then 7-6, 7-6, 4-8 and 5-7 [S3]. So friends, this 6-1 start is a horse that broke slow last year and is now running at the front of the field.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Will Stein is our first-year head coach [S7]; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 1, 2025 [S3]. And what a debut. This team wins by taking care of the ball and taking it away. We've lost only 5 turnovers and taken away 16 [S3], good for a plus-11 margin, 3rd in FBS [S5]. That's a thoroughbred that never breaks stride. We score 32.7 points a game (46th) and run for 166.1 (56th) [S5]. We play clean, 44.4 penalty yards a game (23rd) [S5]. We have 18 sacks [S3]. Now, every horse has a flaw: we convert just 29.1% of third downs, last in FBS [S5], and our pass defense allows 249.7 yards a game (116th) [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Kenny Minchey: 141 of 206 for 1,552 yards, 13 TD and just one interception [S4][S5]. At Oklahoma he went 21 of 28 for 158 yards and two scores [S5]. Pure pedigree.
• RB C.J. Baxter: 484 yards on 87 carries and 8 TD [S4][S5]. Against Oklahoma, Jason Patterson led our backs with 38 yards on 12 carries [S5], and I haven't seen an official report on Baxter's status this week [S10].
• WR Kenny Darby: 34 catches, 436 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5]. WR Nic Anderson: five catches for 48 yards at Oklahoma [S5].
• LB Grant Godfrey: team-high 67 tackles [S4]. DL Mi'Quise Humphrey-Grace: 4 sacks [S4]. DB Jordan Castell: 4 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Kentucky is 6-1 and 4-1 in the SEC, ranked No. 12 by both the AP and the coaches [S3][S5]. We beat Youngstown State 45-13, won at Texas A&M 31-21, beat South Alabama 45-21, won at South Carolina 35-34, beat LSU 35-34 and won at Oklahoma 21-13 [S3]. The one loss: Alabama, 45-17 [S3]. We're 3-0 on the road [S3]. After Vanderbilt, we have a week off, then go to No. 11 Tennessee on Nov. 7 [S5]. I won't do standings math, friends. I'll only say this horse is in the race.
Down the stretch: two one-point wins in a row, at South Carolina and against LSU [S3]. That's a photo finish twice. Champions win those.
Bloodlines, friends: a first-year coach, a quarterback with one interception in seven games and a defense that keeps taking the ball away [S3][S4][S5]. When I see a yearling with that kind of balance, I call the farm manager and say, keep an eye on that one. The Alabama loss? Even the best young horses get beat in their first big race [S3]. What matters is how they run the next one, and this team has won five straight since [S3]. Three of those wins came on the road, in hostile barns [S3].

6. This Week: Vanderbilt (3-4) at No. 12 Kentucky (6-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kroger Field, Lexington · SEC Network [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we won 21-13 at Oklahoma [S5]. Vanderbilt lost 31-21 to Arkansas [S9].
The history: CFBD shows Kentucky won seven of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025 [S2][S3].
Their offense vs. our defense: Vanderbilt throws for 235.1 yards a game (63rd) [S5], and receiver Junior Sherrill has 628 receiving yards [S5]. Our 116th-ranked pass defense must keep him in front [S5]. But Vanderbilt has thrown 7 interceptions [S4], and Jordan Castell has 4 of ours [S4]. That's a fine matchup for a ball hawk.
Our offense vs. their defense: Vanderbilt's run defense allowed 196 yards to Ole Miss and 170 to Arkansas [S9]. That's an open lane on the rail.
Third downs: our weak spot, last in FBS [S5]. Vanderbilt's defense has allowed 29.7 points a game (115th) [S5].
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Our turnover habit, plus-11 [S5]. (2) Running the ball at a defense that's struggled to stop it [S9]. (3) Keeping Sherrill in check.
To Pippa Ashcroft, Vanderbilt's insider: a song about every game? Charming. Write me one about a horse, and I'll come to the show.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Lexington for the game? Joe Bologna's on West Maxwell Street is a longtime family pizza spot.

report.title: "Ring It If You Mean It": Wade Pettus Welcomes the Sooners to Starkville
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Ring it if you mean it. (ding.) Howdy, Bulldog people. I'm Wade Pettus, poultry-science graduate, and I chart Air Raid concepts on the back of feed-store receipts. I have a drawer full of them. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I will tell you plainly that my cowbell has better football sense than most of the analysts on television. It has never once been wrong about a third down. Every week I'll bring you the players, the matchup, the history and a little gentle Starkville deadpan. When we win, I ring the cowbell exactly once for every point we scored, no matter how long it takes. When we lose, the cowbell goes in a sock, out of respect. I believe football is best explained slowly, the way you'd explain a good hen house. I'm glad you're here. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Mississippi State plays in the SEC and won the league championship in 1941, plus a division title in 1998 [S7]. The Bulldogs have made 27 bowl appearances and produced 38 All-Americans, 171 All-SEC selections and 124 NFL players, 11 of them first-round draft choices [S7]. Our home, Davis Wade Stadium at Scott Field, is the second-oldest stadium in FBS [S7]; CFBD dates it to 1914 and lists capacity at 61,337 [S3]. The last few years have been lean, 2-10 in 2024 and 5-8 in 2025 [S3], and that makes this 4-2 start feel like the first warm morning in March. I wrote that on a receipt, too. The Bulldogs have never played Oklahoma before this week, so every snap Saturday is a first for the record books [S9].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jeff Lebby was hired Nov. 26, 2023 [S3]. He came from Oklahoma, where he was offensive coordinator for Brent Venables's first two seasons, 2022 and 2023 . His first two years in Starkville went 7-18 . This offseason he brought back Zach Arnett as defensive coordinator, Arnett's second stint in that job here . The 2026 numbers show an offense that can move: 454.3 yards a game (22nd), 277.8 passing (22nd) and 176.5 rushing (50th), for 32.5 points a game [S5]. The run game averages 4.6 yards a carry, 1,059 yards on 229 tries [S3]. The defense is better against the run (114.7 a game, 36th) than the pass (264.8, 127th) [S5]. Penalties need cleaning up: 70.7 yards a game ranks 118th [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Kamario Taylor: 102 of 154, 1,450 yards, 17 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. A foot injury slowed him against Missouri and Alabama, and he did not play at LSU [S9][S10]. No official status for Saturday as of Oct. 18 [S11].
• RB Da'Marion "Fluff" Bothwell: 403 yards on 74 carries, 3 TD [S4][S5]. He was also unavailable at LSU [S10].
• WR Anthony Evans III: 47 catches, 614 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5].
• LB Tyler Lockhart: a team-high 38 tackles [S4]. DL Will Whitson: 2 sacks [S4]. LB Jalen Smith: an interception [S4].
• QB Puckett: made his first career start at LSU, 16 of 26 for 121 yards [S5][S10]. AP lists him as Parker Puckett and SI as Billy Puckett, so I'm showing you both until the school confirms [S5][S10].

5. The Conference Picture

Mississippi State is 4-2 overall and 2-2 in the SEC [S3]. Wins: UL Monroe 62-13, at Minnesota 38-13, at South Carolina 41-34 and Missouri 31-24 [S3]. Losses: Alabama 56-23 and at LSU 31-0 [S3]. That's two SEC wins through four league games, already the most of Lebby's tenure in conference play [S9]. We are unranked [S3]. Next up after this is a trip to Texas on Oct. 31 [S5].

6. This Week: Oklahoma (3-3) at Mississippi State (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Davis Wade Stadium · SEC Network [S1][S5][S8]. First meeting ever [S9].
Last week: we lost 31-0 at LSU, with turnovers and failed fourth-down tries hurting the offense [S5][S10]. Oklahoma lost 21-13 at home to Kentucky; Mateer threw three interceptions [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the hard part. Oklahoma allows 260.7 yards a game (5th), 151.3 passing yards (6th) and just 25.6% on third down (2nd) [S5]. Its red zone defense is 6th [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: Oklahoma's offense ranks 126th in yards and 136th in rushing [S5], and the Sooners are minus-8 in turnover margin [S5]. Our run defense, 36th, gets a chance to make them one-dimensional [S5].
The storyline: Coach Lebby against the program where he called plays two seasons ago . My cowbell has thoughts. It's keeping them to itself.
Availability: Taylor (foot) and Bothwell both missed LSU; neither has an official status for Saturday [S10][S11]. For Oklahoma, Venables said left tackle Michael Fasusi was close to returning [S9]. No SEC availability report as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Whether Taylor plays, and how well he moves. (2) Turnovers: Oklahoma has 14 giveaways this season [S2]. (3) Whether our pass offense, 22nd in FBS, can find room against the nation's 6th-best pass defense [S5].
And to Savannah Redbird-Lowe, Oklahoma's very gracious insider: welcome to Starkville. I'll ring once for you. Politely.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Starkville for the game? Thai Siam on Martin Luther King Jr. Drive East makes a good, quiet supper after all that ringing.

report.title: "Boomer! (You Say Sooner.)": Savannah Redbird-Lowe Rides Into Starkville
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Boomer! (You say Sooner.) Louder, Norman, I can't hear you over the Schooner wheels. I'm Savannah Redbird-Lowe, former Oklahoma rodeo princess, and I read a defense the way I used to read a barrel pattern: clean turn, tight pocket, no tipped barrels. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I will make you do the "Boomer!" "Sooner!" call-and-response at least once in every single report. That is my one rule, and I'm sweet about it. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the storylines and the history, told straight with a little Plains-state sass. When we win, you'll hear me holler "Boomer!" and wait for you. When we lose, I'll lift my chin and tell you we'll roll the Schooner again. Saddle up, y'all. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Oklahoma football started in 1895 [S6]. The program claims seven national championships (1950, 1955, 1956, 1974, 1975, 1985 and 2000), 50 conference titles and seven Heisman Trophy winners [S6]. Its 963 wins and .723 winning percentage both rank sixth all-time [S6]. The Sooners also hold the Division I record for consecutive wins, 47 straight, and Oklahoma is the only program where four different coaches have won more than 100 games [S6]. Home is Gaylord Family Oklahoma Memorial Stadium in Norman [S6], listed at 86,112 seats in the CFBD venue file [S2]. These days we're an SEC program; the move came for the 2024 season, after 2021-2023 in the Big 12 [S2]. Last season the Sooners went 10-3 [S2]. That is a lot of trophies to dust, and I do it in boots.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Brent Venables is the head coach; the CFBD coaches file dates his hire to Dec. 5, 2021, and he has led the program since 2022 [S2][S6]. The 2026 numbers tell you exactly who this team is. The defense is the barrel racer that never knocks one over: 260.7 yards allowed a game, 5th in FBS, 151.3 passing yards allowed, 6th, and 18.2 points allowed, 30th [S5]. Opponents convert only 25.6% of their third downs, 2nd-best in the country, and our red zone defense ranks 6th [S5]. The defense has 18 sacks in six games [S2]. The offense is still finding its gait. Oklahoma averages 311.5 yards (126th) and 92.5 rushing yards a game (136th) [S5], on 555 rushing yards across 197 carries [S2]. The turnover column is the sore spot: 14 giveaways and a minus-8 margin that ranks 134th [S2][S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB John Mateer: 114 of 175, 1,308 yards, 9 TD, 7 INT, a 65.1% completion rate [S4][S5]. Against Kentucky he threw for 270 yards with one touchdown and three interceptions [S5]. (One outlet lists his yardage at 1,038; AP and ESPN both say 1,308, and I'm using theirs [S10][S4][S5].)
• RB Lloyd Avant: 267 yards on 60 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5].
• WR Isaiah Sategna III: 33 catches, 414 yards, 2 TD [S4][S5]. Manny Choice had five catches for 98 yards last week [S5].
• LB Owen Heinecke: a team-high 44 tackles [S4]. DL Jake Kreul: a team-high 3 sacks [S4]. DB Peyton Bowen: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Oklahoma is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the SEC, and 0-2 in true road games [S2]. We are not in this week's AP or Coaches poll [S2]. The calendar has been a rodeo: wins over UTEP 51-0, New Mexico 14-6 and Texas 27-24 at the Cotton Bowl, and losses at Michigan 17-10, at Georgia 41-13 and at home to Kentucky 21-13 [S2]. After this trip, South Carolina comes to Norman on Oct. 31 [S5]. A road SEC win here would put us back to .500 in league play [S2].

6. This Week: Oklahoma (3-3) at Mississippi State (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Davis Wade Stadium, Starkville · SEC Network [S1][S5][S8]. This is the first meeting ever between these two programs [S9].
Last week: Kentucky beat us 21-13 in Norman [S5]. Reporting from the week says Oklahoma controlled much of that game before the offense came apart late, while dealing with a long list of injuries up front [S9]. Mississippi State lost 31-0 at LSU, with Puckett starting at quarterback and throwing for 121 yards [S5][S10].
Our offense vs. their defense: Mississippi State allows 264.8 passing yards a game (127th) but just 114.7 on the ground (36th), and 28.5 points (111th) [S5]. That says Mateer has room to throw if he protects the ball.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the barrel race I want to watch. The Bulldogs average 454.3 yards (22nd) and 277.8 passing yards (22nd) [S5]. Our pass defense is 6th [S5]. Something has to give.

The SEC had not posted a week 8 availability report as of Oct. 18 [S11]. Status for Saturday: unknown.
"We've got to get off the mat and got to go to Starkville," Venables said, per Fanrecap. "It's a very unforgiving league." [S9]
What decides it: (1) Whether Mateer takes care of the football. (2) Whether Taylor plays for the Bulldogs. (3) Whether our run game can get anything going against a front allowing 114.7 rushing yards a game [S5].
And Wade Pettus, my very kind Bulldogs counterpart: I hear that cowbell is smart. Mine's a Schooner. We'll compare notes, sweetly.

report.title: "Hotty Toddy, and Pass the Footnotes": Langston Fairbanks Writes His Way to Austin
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hotty Toddy, and pass the footnotes. Good evening, gentle readers. I am Langston Fairbanks, a man of seersucker and sweet tea, a student of literature who has read every word Mr. Faulkner wrote and every snap the Rebels have played this season, often on the same afternoon in the Grove. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I will bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Be warned: my takes tend to run three paragraphs. I can't help it. Football, like a good novel, deserves a proper beginning, middle and end. But I always land on a hard number. When we win, I recite a celebratory monologue under the nearest chandelier. When we lose, I murmur, "The past is never dead," and sip my sweet tea in silence. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Rebels represent the University of Mississippi, which everyone calls Ole Miss, and play in the SEC [S6]. The program was founded in 1893 and has won six SEC titles: 1947, 1954, 1955, 1960, 1962 and 1963 [S6]. Ole Miss has been recognized as national champion three times by major selectors [S6]. Home is Vaught-Hemingway Stadium on campus [S6], opened in 1915 and listed at 64,038 seats [S2]. And the recent chapters read like an epic: 10-3, 8-5, 11-2, 10-3, and last year a 13-2 season [S2] that AP describes as a playoff team [S9]. Since 2023, the Rebels are 25-1 at home [S9].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Pete Golding is the head coach in his first full season; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 30, 2025 [S2]. Under him, the offense writes in long, flowing sentences: 290.7 passing yards a game (13th), 444.5 total yards (36th) and 37.5 points (20th) [S5]. And here is the hard number I promised: we have scored on 100% of our red zone trips, first in FBS [S5]. The defense is the chapter still being revised: 390 yards allowed (108th), 236.5 passing yards allowed (104th) [S5]. Opponents convert 44% of third downs (118th) [S5]. But last week the defense held Missouri to 39 rushing yards on 26 carries [S9]. Defensive tackle Will Echoles said, "Stopping the run has been an issue for us at times this year, but it's gotten better" [S9].

4. Players to Know

• QB Trinidad Chambliss: 142 of 210 for 1,676 yards, 14 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. Against Missouri he threw three touchdowns and ran for another [S9]. Coach Golding: "He wasn't perfect either, but I'm glad he's on our side" [S9].
• RB Kewan Lacy: 352 yards on 62 carries, 5 TD; 122 yards on 16 carries last week [S4][S9]. Makhi Frazier added 101 yards on 15 carries [S9].
• WR Deuce Alexander: 35 catches, 523 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5]. Caleb Odom, Horatio Fields and Caleb Cunningham each caught a touchdown against Missouri [S9].
• DT Will Echoles: five tackles, two pass breakups and a sack against Missouri [S9]. DE Blake Purchase: 3.5 sacks [S4]. LB Luke Ferrelli: team-high 39 tackles [S4]. S Nick Cull: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Ole Miss is 5-1, 3-1 in the SEC, and ranked No. 7 by both the AP and coaches [S2][S5]. We beat Louisville 41-38 at a neutral site, Charlotte 41-9, LSU 32-24, Vanderbilt 52-17 on the road and Missouri 31-3 [S2]. The lone blemish: a 52-28 loss at Florida [S2]. After Austin, Auburn comes to Oxford on Oct. 31 [S5]. AP notes we still face No. 1 Georgia, and four of our last five games are at home [S9]. I shall not do arithmetic upon the standings tonight. I shall only say the plot thickens beautifully. And the Florida chapter? Every great Southern novel has a tragedy in its second act. What matters is that the protagonist rises again, and since Gainesville, we have won twice by a combined 83-20 [S2].

6. This Week: No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1) at No. 19 Texas (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin · ABC [S1][S5][S8]. Kickoff forecast: 85 degrees, partly cloudy [S10]. Seersucker weather.
The history: officially, Texas leads the series 6-1; as played, 6-2 in eight meetings [S10]. The most recent: Ole Miss won 44-23 in 2013, a year after Texas won 66-31 [S10]. And there was a Sugar Bowl win, 39-7, after the 1957 season [S10].
Last week: we beat Missouri 31-3 [S9]. Texas lost 27-24 to Florida [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: now this is the central conflict of the novel. Texas allows 272.5 yards a game (12th), 166.2 passing yards (12th) and 17.8 points (29th) [S5]. Texas' Colin Simmons has 10.5 sacks [S4]. Chambliss against that pass rush is the scene I'll reread for years.
Their offense vs. our defense: Texas averages 361.3 yards (93rd) and 134.5 rushing yards (103rd) [S5]. Arch Manning has 11 touchdown passes [S5].
Availability: no official SEC availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Protecting Chambliss from Simmons. (2) Our perfect red zone record against Texas' 57th-ranked red zone defense [S5]. (3) Getting off the field on third down.
To Caroline Whitfield, Texas' insider: you price your players like assets? Madam, I prefer to read them like poetry. Let us meet in the fourth quarter.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in Oxford? City Grocery and Ajax Diner, both on Courthouse Square, are as much a part of the Oxford story as any novel.

report.title: "Cue the Music": Beau Cheraw Makes His Entrance as the Vols Come to Columbia
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

(Lights down. Music up. A single spotlight. Smoke machine, family-sized.) Cue the music. Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, Gamecock Nation: I'm Beaumont Cheraw, but you can call me Beau, and I live for the entrance. I time my podcast intro to dramatic music. I have timed my breakfast to dramatic music. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines every week, with the volume where it belongs. When we win, I'll bounce like the whole of Williams-Brice when the music hits. When we lose, I'll turn the music down, just for a minute, and remind you that the band plays again next Saturday. I'm electric, I'm theatrical, and I will always be kind to the visitors, because a great show needs a great guest star. And I promise: every number I give you comes with a receipt, right there in brackets. Forever to thee. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

South Carolina plays in the SEC and has since 1992 [S7]. Before that, the Gamecocks were in the ACC from 1953 through 1970, winning the 1969 conference title, and then a major independent from 1971 through 1991 [S7]. The independent years gave us George Rogers, our 1980 Heisman Trophy winner and the No. 1 overall selection in the 1981 draft [S7]. Jadeveon Clowney went No. 1 overall in 2014 [S7]. We won the SEC East in 2010 [S7]. Lou Holtz and Steve Spurrier are both in the College Football Hall of Fame, and Shane Beamer was the 2024 SEC coach of the year [S7]. Home is Williams-Brice Stadium, listed at 80,250 seats [S3]. When that stadium starts bouncing, you understand. The Gamecocks finished in the final AP top 25 in 1984 and 1987 as an independent, and have posted eight final top-25 finishes in the SEC era [S7].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Beamer was hired Dec. 6, 2020, and this is his sixth season [S3][S10]. His teams went 9-4 in 2024 and 4-8 in 2025 [S3]. The 2026 Gamecocks bring the noise on offense: 474.7 yards a game (13th in FBS), 232.3 rushing yards (10th) and 37.7 points (18th) [S5]. CFBD has 1,394 rushing yards on 233 carries, just about 6 yards a carry [S3]. The defense is sturdy against the run, 103.7 yards allowed a game (25th), and leakier through the air, 237.2 passing yards allowed (107th) [S5]. The red zone defense, 93.8% scoring allowed, ranks 122nd [S5]. That's the one part of the show we're still rehearsing.

4. Players to Know

• QB LaNorris Sellers: 115 of 187, 1,338 yards, 12 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. Against Florida he threw for 279 yards and four touchdowns, and ran one in [S5].
• RB Matthew Fuller: 485 yards on 81 carries, 5 TD [S4][S5].
• WR Nyck Harbor: 17 catches, 278 yards, 2 TD [S4][S5], including four for 83 and a score against Florida [S5].
• LB Justin Okoronkwo: a team-high 43 tackles [S4]. DE Anthony Addison: 3 sacks [S4]. DB Peyton Williams: an interception [S4].
• Freshman Julian Walker: two starts and a sack, per the school's injury rundown [S11].

5. The Conference Picture

South Carolina is 3-3 and 1-3 in the SEC [S3]. The three SEC losses were by 7 to Mississippi State, by 31 at Alabama and by 1 in overtime to Kentucky, 35-34 [S3][S4]. The win at Florida, 38-19, came right before the bye [S3][S5]. We're unranked [S3]. Next up is a trip to Oklahoma on Oct. 31 [S5]. Knocking off the No. 11 team in the country at home would be one fine entrance into November [S2].

6. This Week: No. 11 Tennessee (6-1) at South Carolina (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Williams-Brice Stadium · ESPN [S1][S5][S9].
Last game: we beat Florida 38-19 on Oct. 10, then had the bye [S5]. Tennessee beat Alabama 26-10 last Saturday behind 159 rushing yards from DeSean Bishop [S12].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the main event. Tennessee allows 14.7 points (9th), 280.6 yards (15th) and 159.3 passing yards (8th) [S5]. It has 29 sacks [S2]. Our run game, 10th in FBS, against their run defense, 42nd, is where I'd put the spotlight [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: Tennessee runs for 217.1 yards a game (19th) and scores on 95.7% of red zone trips (6th) [S5]. We allow 103.7 rushing yards a game (25th), so that's strength against strength [S5]. Their quarterback spot is a work in progress, per AP [S12].
Series: UT's game notes list the all-time series at Tennessee 29, South Carolina 11, with 2 ties [S9]. From 2016 through 2025 it's even, 4-4 [S3].
Availability: Beamer, after the Florida game: "Everybody that missed the game yesterday or left the game, like Judge Collier did, we all expect to be back against Tennessee. The only one that we would be most concerned about ... is QuaySheed Scott." [S10] That group included DT Gabriel Brownlow-Dindy, Walker and center Carter Miller [S11]. The first SEC availability report comes Wednesday [S10]. For Tennessee, aggregators list three players out, including LB J. Harmon (ACL) .
What decides it: (1) Whether Sellers can find room against the 8th-ranked pass defense. (2) Red zone: our defense has to get stops there. (3) Whether the bye week gets our injured guys back to full speed [S10].
And Rocky Top Haskew, Tennessee's insider, I hear you brought a banjo. Bring it on in. We'll give you a proper entrance.

report.title: "Cue the Banjo": Rocky Top Haskew Takes the Vols to Columbia
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

(banjo: plink-a-plink-plink.) Cue the banjo. Howdy, Big Orange Country, I'm Earl Haskew, but everybody on Cumberland Avenue calls me Rocky Top. I was a long snapper for the Vols, which means I spent four years looking at the world upside down and backward, and honestly it gave me a great perspective on defensive fronts. I travel with this team and live with this team, and before every stat I play a little banjo intro. Sometimes the banjo's out of tune on purpose. You'll know when. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and a few checkerboard metaphors from a fella who loves the end zones at Neyland more than his own front porch. When we win, I play "Rocky Top" until somebody stops me, and nobody ever does. When we lose, I play it slow and sad. Pull up a rocking chair. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

(plink.) Tennessee started playing football in 1891 [S6]. The Vols claim six national titles, including two from the wire-service polls in 1951 and 1998, and 16 conference championships [S6]. We rank fifth all-time in bowl appearances, 55 of them, with four Sugar Bowls, three Cotton Bowls, two Orange Bowls, a Fiesta and a Peach among the wins [S6]. Neyland Stadium is the cathedral, and the Vols have won 485 games there, the most any program has won in its current home [S6]. Capacity is listed at 101,915 by one source and 102,455 by CFBD, so I'll just say "a whole lot of orange" and show you both [S6][S2]. Josh Heupel's teams have gone 11-2, 9-4, 10-3 and 8-5 since 2022 [S2].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Heupel was hired Jan. 27, 2021 [S2]. This year's Vols win the old-fashioned way, and my banjo approves. Tennessee runs for 217.1 yards a game, 19th in FBS, and has 1,520 rushing yards on 302 carries, a little over 5 yards a pop [S5][S2]. The passing game is more modest, 188.0 yards a game (110th) [S5]. The defense is the headliner: 280.6 yards allowed (15th), 159.3 passing yards allowed (8th) and 14.7 points allowed (9th) [S5]. It has 29 sacks and 13 takeaways through seven games [S2], and it holds opponents to 30.8% on third down, 15th in FBS [S5]. The red zone offense scores on 95.7% of trips, 6th [S5]. That's checkerboard football: square by square, all the way down the field.

4. Players to Know

• RB DeSean Bishop: 837 yards on 139 carries, 10 TD [S4][S5]. He ran for 159 yards and two scores against Alabama, 95 of them after halftime [S12]. Heupel called him "a special back. Smart, tough, physical, great vision." [S12]
• The quarterbacks: Faizon Brandon leads the team at 697 yards, 7 TD and 1 INT on 61 of 101 [S4][S5]. George MacIntyre started against Alabama and went 21 of 31 for 197 yards [S12]. AP called the position "still very much a work in progress" [S12].
• WR Mike Matthews: 29 catches, 481 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5], including seven for 85 against Alabama [S5].
• DL Tyree Weathersby: a team-high 6.5 sacks [S4]. LB Amare Campbell: 46 tackles [S4]. DB Dejuan Lane: 3 interceptions [S4].
(Note: ESPN's public game page showed slightly different sack and tackle leaders on Oct. 18. I'm using its season-leaders feed [S4].)

5. The Conference Picture

Tennessee is 6-1 and 3-1 in the SEC, 2-0 on the road [S2], and No. 11 in both the AP and Coaches polls this week [S2]. The only loss was 20-17 to Texas [S2]. The Vols have won three straight: Auburn 24-14, at Arkansas 24-17 and Alabama 26-10 [S2]. Tennessee has now won three of its last five against Alabama, all three at home [S12]. After the field-storming, the SEC fined Tennessee $500,000, payable to Alabama under league policy [S13]. After this trip, the next game listed is a Nov. 7 home date with No. 12 Kentucky [S5].

6. This Week: No. 11 Tennessee (6-1) at South Carolina (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Williams-Brice Stadium, Columbia · ESPN [S1][S5][S9].
Last week: we beat Alabama 26-10. Alabama had 201 yards, 54 on the ground, and four turnovers, and went 2 for 13 on third down [S12]. A fourth-quarter drive took 9 minutes, 32 seconds and ended with Bishop's 5-yard touchdown [S12]. South Carolina was off after beating Florida 38-19 on Oct. 10 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: South Carolina stops the run well, 103.7 yards allowed a game (25th), but gives up 237.2 passing yards (107th) and lets opponents score on 93.8% of red zone trips (122nd) [S5]. That last number makes my banjo hum.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the heavyweight bout. South Carolina averages 474.7 yards (13th), 232.3 rushing (10th) and 37.7 points (18th) [S5]. LaNorris Sellers has 12 touchdown passes and four interceptions [S5]. Our defense is 9th in scoring [S5].
Series: UT's game notes list Tennessee 29 wins, South Carolina 11 and 2 ties [S9]. In the CFBD window from 2016 through 2025, the teams split eight meetings, 4-4 [S2].
Availability: aggregator reports list LB J. Harmon out for the season with a torn ACL, OG Wendell Moe Jr. out for the season and LS B. Brady out with an undisclosed injury, as of Oct. 17 . That's not an official SEC report, and the first one comes Wednesday [S10]. For South Carolina, Beamer expected everyone who missed the Florida game back except possibly nickel Quay'Sheed Scott, pending tests [S10][S11].
What decides it: (1) Bishop and the run game against South Carolina's 25th-ranked run defense. (2) Who plays quarterback for us, and how cleanly. (3) Whether our defense can slow an offense that is 10th in rushing [S5].
And Beau Cheraw, South Carolina's insider: I hear you've got an entrance planned. I've got a banjo. Let's make it a duet.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching from Knoxville? Calhoun's on the River on Neyland Drive is a fine spot to listen for the banjo.

report.title: "Darling, That's a Premium Asset": Caro Whitfield Welcomes the Rebels to Austin
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Darling, that's a premium asset. Well, hello, y'all, I'm Caroline Whitfield, Caro to my friends. I was a rodeo queen in a former life, I spent a few years in consulting after that, and now I bring both to the Forty Acres: big-hat polish and a very organized brain. I travel with the Longhorns and I live with the Longhorns, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I size up every opponent's roster in imaginary Caro Bucks, and I'll tell you exactly what each player is worth to me. Darling, I don't do rebuilds. I do acquisitions. When we win, I raise a single eyebrow and say, "As forecast." When we lose, I call an emergency board meeting with myself. Hypothetically, heads roll. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Texas Longhorns began playing in 1893 and compete in the SEC [S7]. We claim four consensus national championships: 1963, 1969, 1970 and 2005 [S7], and the program has been led by three Hall of Fame coaches [S7]. Home is DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium in Austin, opened in 1924 and listed at 100,119 seats [S3]. The last five seasons: 5-7, 8-5, then 12-2, 13-3 and 10-3 [S3]. That, darling, is a blue-chip portfolio.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Steve Sarkisian has been our head coach since CFBD's hire date of Jan. 2, 2021 [S3]. CollegeFootballDigest notes he's two wins from 100 as a head coach, with 98 so far [S10]. Now, the holdings. The defense is the crown jewel: 272.5 yards allowed a game (12th in FBS), 166.2 passing yards allowed (12th), 106.3 rushing (28th) and 17.8 points (29th) [S5]. We have 19 sacks [S3]. The offense, I'll admit, is underperforming its valuation: 361.3 yards a game (93rd) and 134.5 rushing yards (103rd) [S5]. We've allowed 17 sacks [S3]. A smart investor knows which assets to hold and which need attention.

4. Players to Know

• QB Arch Manning: 106 of 166 for about 1,295 yards (1,298 per AP), 11 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. Against Florida he went 14 of 20 for 173 yards and a touchdown [S5].
• RB Smothers: 289 yards on 65 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5]. ESPN lists him as Hollywood Smothers; AP says Daylan [S4][S5].
• WR Ryan Wingo: 26 catches, 345 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5]. Emmett Mosley V: two catches for 76 yards against Florida [S5].
• DE Colin Simmons: 10.5 sacks [S4]. In seven figures of Caro Bucks, darling, that is a premium asset.
• LB Rasheem Biles: team-high 48 tackles and 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Texas is 4-2 and 1-2 in the SEC, ranked No. 19 by the AP and No. 18 by the coaches [S3][S5]. We beat Texas State 59-7, Ohio State 24-23, UTSA 30-6 and Tennessee 20-17 on the road [S3]. Then two three-point losses: 27-24 to Oklahoma at a neutral site and 27-24 to Florida [S3]. After Ole Miss, Mississippi State visits on Oct. 31 [S5]. I don't do standings math in public, darling. I'll just say two losses by three points apiece is a market correction, not a crash.
The portfolio review: the Ohio State win, 24-23, is still the holding I treasure most this year [S3]. Beating Tennessee on the road, 20-17, was a fine acquisition too [S3]. In those two big wins, the defense allowed 40 points combined [S3]. That is how this team wins, darling: suffocate people. The losses to Oklahoma and Florida were decided by a field goal each, and both opponents scored 27 [S3]. A few plays here and there, and we're having a very different conversation. I've seen bigger swings in the oil patch. And unlike oil, I know this defense will keep holding up in October.

6. This Week: No. 7 Ole Miss (5-1) at No. 19 Texas (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 Central) · DKR-Texas Memorial Stadium, Austin · ABC [S1][S5][S8]. Kickoff forecast: 85 degrees, partly cloudy [S10].
The history: officially, Texas leads the series 6-1; as played, 6-2 [S10]. We won 66-31 in 2012; Ole Miss won 44-23 in 2013, the most recent meeting [S10].
Their offense vs. our defense: this is the merger of the season. Ole Miss throws for 290.7 yards a game (13th) and scores 37.5 points (20th) [S5]. Trinidad Chambliss has 14 touchdown passes [S5]. And the Rebels have scored on every one of their red zone trips, first in FBS [S5]. Our pass defense ranks 12th [S5]. Something has to give, y'all.
Our offense vs. their defense: Ole Miss allows 390 yards a game (108th), 236.5 passing yards (104th) and lets opponents convert 44% of third downs (118th) [S5]. Manning should find room.
Possession: Ole Miss averages 26:59, 131st in FBS [S5]. They score fast and they leave the field fast.
Availability: no official SEC availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Simmons and our pass rush against Chambliss. (2) Manning against a 104th-ranked pass defense. (3) Red zone defense; ours ranks 57th [S5].
To Langston Fairbanks, Ole Miss' insider: poetry is lovely, darling. I prefer a balance sheet. See you in the fourth quarter.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Austin for the game? Kerbey Lane Cafe on Kerbey Lane is a classic for pancakes before a night kickoff.

report.title: "Howdy, and Let Me Yell This": Colt Wendeborn Brings the 12th Man to Tuscaloosa
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

HOWDY! Howdy, and let me yell this: welcome to The Cover Window, Aggies! I'm Colt Wendeborn, petroleum engineering graduate, and I report on football practice the way the Yell Leaders lead Midnight Yell, with my whole chest. I travel with this team and I live with this team. My one weakness is that I explain everything with an Aggie tradition, and then I explain the tradition, and then sometimes I explain the explanation. You'll learn a lot. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, delivered with the straight-arrow earnestness of a man who irons his maroon. When we win, I yell. Just yell. Joyfully. When we lose, I go practice silent yell drills in a closet until I feel better. Gig 'em, and thank you for reading. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Texas A&M competes in the SEC and claims three national titles and 18 conference championships [S6]. Home is Kyle Field, an outdoor stadium on campus that seats 102,733 [S6][S2]. CFBD dates it to 1927 [S2]. (A tradition explained: the student section stands the entire game because the 12th Man is ready to go in. That's why I'm standing while I write this.) The last five seasons have run 8-4, 5-7, 7-6, 8-5 and then a big 11-2 in 2025, Mike Elko's second year [S2]. Kyle Field and Bryant-Denny both hold more than 100,000 people [S2][S3], so Saturday is two of the biggest rooms in the sport shaking hands.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Elko was hired Nov. 27, 2023 [S2]. The 2026 identity is defense first, and I will yell about it. The Aggies allow 17.1 points a game (27th), 306.6 yards (29th) and just 164.1 passing yards (10th) [S5]. Opponents convert only 29.8% of third downs, 11th in FBS [S5]. The team is careful, too: 41.7 penalty yards a game is 14th-best in the country [S5]. The offense is still searching. It averages 356.9 yards (97th) and 195.7 passing yards (103rd) [S5], and the pass rush has only 5 sacks in seven games [S2]. In the two SEC road losses, at LSU and at Missouri, the Aggies scored 6 points each time [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Marcel Reed: 112 of 201, 1,227 yards, 7 TD, 6 INT [S4][S5]. At Missouri he went 19 of 39 for 189 yards and two interceptions; a week later against The Citadel he was 8 of 13 for 130 and a touchdown [S9][S5].
• RB K.J. Edwards: 317 yards on 47 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5], including 116 yards on 13 carries last week [S5].
• WR Isaiah Horton: 20 catches, 280 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5]. Aaron Gregory caught six passes for 94 yards and two touchdowns against The Citadel [S5].
• LB Ray Coney: a team-high 36 tackles [S4]. DE Marco Jones: 2 sacks [S4]. CB Julio Humphrey: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Texas A&M is 4-3 and 1-3 in the SEC, 0-2 on the road [S2]. The wins: Missouri State 50-0, Arizona State 48-20, Arkansas 34-7 and The Citadel 41-0 [S2]. The losses: Kentucky 31-21, at LSU 35-6 and at Missouri 27-6 [S2]. We're unranked [S2]. Next is a Nov. 7 trip to South Carolina [S5]. A win in Tuscaloosa would be the kind of thing you tell your grandchildren about at Silver Taps (that's a solemn tradition, and I won't joke about it).

6. This Week: Texas A&M (4-3) at No. 13 Alabama (5-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:30 p.m. ET · Bryant-Denny Stadium, Tuscaloosa · ABC [S1][S5][S8]. It's Alabama's homecoming [S9].
Last week: we beat The Citadel 41-0 [S5]. Alabama lost 26-10 at Tennessee, managed 201 yards, turned it over four times and went 2 for 13 on third down [S11]. It was the Tide's second straight loss, the first time that's happened in the regular season since 2007 [S11].
Our offense vs. their defense: Alabama allows 107 rushing yards a game (30th) but 230.9 passing (101st) [S5]. Its red zone defense allows a score on 95.7% of trips, 134th [S5]. If Reed can get us inside the 20, the door is open.
Their offense vs. our defense: Alabama scores 39.3 points a game (12th) [S5]. Keelon Russell has 1,746 yards, 12 TD and 4 INT [S5]. Our pass defense ranks 10th [S5], and Russell said after Tennessee, "It was just a lack of a plan that I had. Just wasn't playing my game today." [S11] Expect him to have one this week.
Series: Alabama leads 13-3 [S9][S10]. The last meeting was a 26-20 Alabama win in College Station on Oct. 7, 2023, and the teams did not play in 2024 or 2025 [S9]. Our last win in Tuscaloosa was 29-24 in 2012 [S9].
Availability: aggregator listings dated Oct. 17 have WRs Mario Craver and A.J. Bethel-Roman questionable, and OG Blake Ivy, WRs Terry Bussey and Madden Williams and RB T.J. Riden Jr. out . For Alabama, WRs Ryan Coleman-Williams (knee) and A.J. Walker are listed out and TE Jay Ford questionable . None of that is an official SEC report; the first comes Oct. 21 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Whether Reed can protect the ball on the road. (2) Our pass defense against Russell. (3) Red zone trips: Alabama has struggled to stop them [S5].
And Mary-Kathryn Strickland, Alabama's very gracious insider: Howdy! I've brought you a tradition explained. It's long.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In College Station? Nam Cafe on Nagle Street is a quiet bowl of pho before a long yell.

report.title: "That's a Hit Single, Y'all": Pippa Ashcroft Takes Her Guitar to Lexington
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

That's a hit single, y'all. Hey there, I'm Penelope Ashcroft, but everyone on West End calls me Pippa. I study economics at Vanderbilt by day, and by night I write country songs on a beat-up guitar, and every single one of them is about a football game. I travel with the Commodores and I live with the Commodores, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little Music City wordplay and a chorus or two. Got an interception return in my heart and a third-down stop on my mind. That's my sound. When we win, I sing a big country chorus, key change and all. When we lose, I write a sad breakup ballad to the turnover that did us in. I've got a whole album of those this month. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Commodores represent Vanderbilt University in the SEC [S6]. Home is FirstBank Stadium, right on our Nashville campus [S6], opened in 1922 and listed at 40,351 seats [S2]. Now here's a song with a happy ending: the last five seasons went 2-10, 5-7, 2-10, then 7-6 in 2024 and a 10-3 smash hit in 2025 [S2]. Ten wins at Vanderbilt. Y'all, that one went platinum. This season is the follow-up album, and follow-up albums are hard.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Clark Lea is the head coach [S6]; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 14, 2020 [S2]. He's the producer behind that 10-3 record [S2]. This year's offense throws it, 235.1 passing yards a game (63rd), with 23.6 points a game (98th) [S5]. The run game is quiet, 119.3 a game (118th) [S5]. The defense has 15 sacks [S2], but it's allowing 146.3 rushing yards (79th) and 29.7 points (115th) [S5]. AP noted the defense came in highly touted but gave up 196 rushing yards to Ole Miss and 170 to Arkansas [S9]. And our turnover margin is minus-6, 126th [S5]. Coach Lea said it plainly last week: "We're actively in pursuit of a better performance" [S9].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jared Curtis: 101 of 161 for 1,242 yards, 6 TD, 7 INT [S4][S5]. Against Arkansas he threw for 274 yards [S9].
• WR Junior Sherrill: 41 catches, 628 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. Eight catches for 99 yards and a touchdown last week [S5]. That boy is a hit single, y'all.
• RB Sedrick Alexander: 270 yards on 61 carries, 5 TD; a touchdown run against Arkansas [S4][S9]. Makhilyn Young also ran for a score [S9].
• S CJ Heard: team-high 51 tackles [S4]. LB Nick Rinaldi: 3.5 sacks [S4]. Miles Capers: 1 interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Vanderbilt is 3-4 and 0-4 in the SEC [S2]. We opened 3-0 with wins over Austin Peay 28-9, Delaware 35-26 and NC State 35-31 [S2]. Then the SEC tour: a 21-15 loss at Auburn, 38-14 at Georgia, 52-17 to Ole Miss and 31-21 to Arkansas [S2]. After Lexington, we have a week off, then visit Mississippi State on Nov. 7 [S5]. I won't do standings math, y'all. I'll write a song about turning it around.
The breakup ballad of the week: with 3:46 left against Arkansas, Curtis drove us to their 29, and an interception ended it [S9]. Verse one, chorus, heartbreak. But the Auburn game was within one score [S2], and that tells me the band can still play.
Season so far, as an album: track one, two and three were upbeat, three straight wins at home, including a 35-31 thriller over NC State [S2]. Then came the slow songs. That's how every great record goes, y'all. You put the ballads in the middle, and you save the anthem for the end. There are still five games of this album left to write.

6. This Week: Vanderbilt (3-4) at No. 12 Kentucky (6-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kroger Field, Lexington · SEC Network [S1][S5][S8].
The history: CFBD shows Kentucky won seven of the 10 meetings from 2016 through 2025 [S2][S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Kentucky's pass defense allows 249.7 yards a game, 116th in FBS [S5]. Curtis and Sherrill can write a hit against that. Kentucky's overall defense is 95th [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: Kentucky QB Kenny Minchey has 13 touchdown passes and only one interception [S5]. C.J. Baxter has 484 rushing yards and 8 TD [S5]. Their run game, 166.1 a game (56th), meets our run defense, which has struggled the last two weeks [S5][S9].
Their big weakness: Kentucky converts just 29.1% of third downs, last in FBS [S5]. Get them to third down, and we've got a shot.
Turnovers: Kentucky is plus-11, 3rd in FBS; we're minus-6 [S5]. That's the whole song right there.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Protecting the football. (2) Stopping the run. (3) Winning third downs against the worst third-down offense in FBS [S5].
To Rhett Abernathy-Coyle, Kentucky's insider: you grade bloodlines? Sugar, I grade hooks. And your team's got a catchy one this year. I'll give you that.

Why I Love This Team

I love that a school that went 2-10 twice in three years just won 10 games [S2]. I love Sherrill's hands [S4]. I love that Coach Lea talks straight [S9]. And I love writing these songs, even the sad ones. Especially the sad ones. They're the best ones on the album.

report.title: "Bless Your Yards-Per-Play": Mallory Penhallow Takes the Hoosiers to the Big House
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well hello, Hoosier Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Mallory Penhallow, former Miss Monroe County runner-up, and these days I run a 40-tab efficiency model on everything this football team does. I travel with the team, I live with the numbers, and yes, the clicker is rhinestone. My pageant answer to every question is the same: "It's the explosives, darling." Each week I give one opponent my honorary Miss Congeniality sash. It goes to whoever I roast the hardest, and I always do it with love. When we win, you get the full pageant wave. When we lose, it's "grace in defeat"... and then I quietly open tab 41. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Before Curt Cignetti showed up, Indiana had the most losses of any program in college football, 713 of them over 130-plus years [S14]. It had won three bowl games in its whole history, and the last one came in 1991 [S16]. Then 2025 happened. The Hoosiers went 16-0 and beat Miami 27-21 at Hard Rock Stadium on Jan. 19, 2026, to win their first national championship [S14]. The last team to win 16 games without a loss was Yale in 1894 [S14]. Quarterback Fernando Mendoza won the Heisman, and he scored the deciding touchdown himself on a 12-yard run on fourth-and-4 [S14][S15]. Cignetti's quote still sounds like an acceptance speech to me: "We won the national championship at Indiana University. It can be done." [S14]

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Cignetti was hired on Nov. 30, 2023 [S5]. Part of his rebuild came from bringing 13 transfers with him from his old school, James Madison [S16]. The 2026 numbers show what this team is. On offense, Indiana averages 36.6 points and 449.3 yards a game [S8]. It runs for 5.67 yards a carry [S3], and Josh Hoover has 18 touchdown passes with no interceptions [S4]. On defense, the Hoosiers allow 12.9 points a game, which ranks 4th in FBS [S8]. Opponents gain only 2.28 yards a carry [S3], and Indiana has 24 sacks against 10 allowed [S3]. The team has lost just three turnovers all season [S3] and gives up 30.7 penalty yards a game, 3rd-fewest in FBS [S8]. Clean football is my love language.

4. Players to Know

• QB Josh Hoover: 1,660 yards, 18 TD, 0 INT, 63.9% completions [S4][S8]. Against Ohio State he landed on his right shoulder, missed one play and came back [S12][S13]. I found no official status for Saturday as of Oct. 18 [S13].
• RB Turbo Richard: 643 yards on 87 carries, 6 TD [S4]. RB Lee Beebe: 575 yards on 107 carries, 4 TD [S4].
• WR Charlie Becker: 39 catches, 694 yards, 8 TD [S4], including 9 for 165 against Ohio State [S11]. WR Nick Marsh: 32 catches, 585 yards, 7 TD [S4].
• Tobi Osunsanmi (sack leader): 7 sacks, 11.5 tackles for loss [S4]. Isaiah Jones: a team-high 51 tackles [S4]. Amare Ferrell: team-high 2 INT [S4], with an interception against Ohio State [S11].

5. The Conference Picture

Indiana is 6-1 overall and 3-1 in the Big Ten, and 2-0 on the road [S2]. The Hoosiers dropped from No. 5 to No. 6 in the AP poll after losing 19-15 to Ohio State, which ended a 22-game winning streak and Cignetti's 19-game unbeaten run at home [S7][S11][S12]. In Cignetti's words: "We can accomplish anything we want, all of our goals, except going undefeated." [S11]

6. This Week: No. 6 Indiana (6-1) at Michigan (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Michigan Stadium, Ann Arbor · FOX [S1][S8][S22]. The game is sold out, and it's Michigan's Block Cancer Game and Parents Weekend [S22].
Last week: Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State. On the last play, Marsh caught a fourth-and-4 pass but couldn't get his left foot down inbounds [S11][S10]. The defense held the Buckeyes to 313 yards, only 78 of them on the ground [S10]. Michigan beat Penn State 21-18 after true freshman Tommy Carr replaced Bryce Underwood at halftime [S9][S8].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is a real test. Michigan allows 256.5 yards a game, 3rd in FBS, and 89.7 rushing yards a game, 13th [S8]. Indiana has also been held under 75 rushing yards in each of its last two games [S12].
Their offense vs. our defense: Michigan averages 22.7 points a game (105th) and 165.7 passing yards (125th) [S8]. The Wolverines have lost 11 turnovers [S3] and are minus-3 in turnover margin, while Indiana is plus-3 [S8].
Series: Michigan leads 62-11 [S6]. Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in Bloomington in 2024 [S6], and the teams did not play in 2025 [S10].
Availability: Hoover's shoulder (above). I found no other official report for this game as of Oct. 18 [S13].
What decides it: (1) How healthy Hoover is and how well he throws. (2) Whether Indiana's run game can do anything against Michigan's front. (3) Who plays quarterback for Michigan, which Kyle Whittingham may not announce before kickoff [S9].
And yes, Gus Hartwell, Michigan's very charming insider, I'm holding the Miss Congeniality sash for you. With love.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching from Bloomington? Mother Bear's Pizza on East 3rd Street is a home-game tradition in our house.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 26, Michigan Wolverines 17.

report.title: "Hail to the Spreadsheet": Gus Hartwell Welcomes the Champs to Ann Arbor
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Greetings, Wolverines, and welcome to The Cover Window. I am Augustin Hartwell, but everybody calls me Gus. You'll know me by the maize sweater, the engineering-school pin and the coffee mug that says VICTORS. I travel with this team, and I label my data with fight-song lyrics. "Champions of the West" is a perfectly good column header, and I expect Dr. Ingrid Solvang, our Big Ten expert, to accept it. My motto is "Hail to the spreadsheet." When we win, I belt out "Hail to the Victors," off-key and proud. When we lose: "Victors... valiant... later." Then I head to the library. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Michigan played its first game on May 30, 1879 [S19], and it has more wins than any other program in college football [S21]. The Wolverines claim 12 national championships, most recently in 2023 [S18][S19]. That 2023 team went 15-0, won the program's 45th Big Ten title, and beat Washington 34-13 for the national title [S18]. Three Wolverines have won the Heisman: Tom Harmon (1940), Desmond Howard (1991) and Charles Woodson (1997) [S21]. Michigan Stadium has been home since 1927 and set the stadium's attendance record of 115,109 against Notre Dame on Sept. 7, 2013 [S19]. Official sources list two different capacities, 107,601 and 109,901, so we note both [S20][S19].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kyle Whittingham was named Michigan's 22nd head coach on Dec. 26, 2025, with a five-year contract that runs through 2030 [S17]. He spent 21 seasons as Utah's head coach, went 177-88 there, and had eight seasons with 10 or more wins [S17]. That makes him the 22nd head coach in a program history spanning 146 years [S17], and he took over after Michigan fired Sherrone Moore [S23]. The standard he inherits is enormous: Michigan has more all-time wins than any program in college football [S21], and the record crowd at Michigan Stadium is 115,109, set against Notre Dame on Sept. 7, 2013 [S19]. The 2026 numbers say defense comes first. Michigan allows 256.5 yards a game (3rd in FBS) and 16.2 points (21st) [S8], and opponents gain only 2.68 yards a carry [S3]. The offense runs first, with 211 carries against 135 pass attempts [S3], but it's still finding its footing at 313.3 yards a game (125th) [S8]. Two things to clean up: 11 turnovers lost [S3] and 65.8 penalty yards a game, 104th in FBS [S8].

4. Players to Know

• QB Bryce Underwood (sophomore): 924 yards, 5 TD, 6 INT, 58.1% completions [S4][S8][S9]. He was benched at halftime against Penn State after throwing two interceptions [S9].
• QB Tommy Carr (true freshman): 5 of 7 for 47 yards against Penn State, plus 4 carries for 36 yards and a touchdown [S8][S9]. Whittingham has not named a starter and may not announce one before the game [S9].
• RB Jordan Marshall: 293 yards on 69 carries, 4 TD [S4]. RB Savion Hiter: 223 yards [S4], including 78 on 11 carries against Penn State [S8].
• WR JJ Buchanan: 27 catches, 482 yards, 4 TD [S4]. WR Andrew Marsh: 28 catches, 289 yards [S4].
• Troy Bowles: a team-high 50 tackles [S4]. John Henry Daley: 3.5 sacks, 6 tackles for loss [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Michigan is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big Ten, and 4-1 at home [S2]. The Wolverines are not ranked in the AP or Coaches poll this week [S7]. Their losses came against Iowa (20-19) and at Minnesota (20-14) [S1]. Beating the defending national champions at home would be a résumé entry worth framing.

6. This Week: No. 6 Indiana (6-1) at Michigan (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · Noon ET · Michigan Stadium · FOX · Sold out · Block Cancer Game and Parents Weekend [S1][S8][S22].
Last week: Michigan trailed Penn State 3-0 at halftime, then scored 21 points in the second half and won 21-18 [S10][S9]. Indiana lost 19-15 to Ohio State. It was the Hoosiers' first loss in 23 games [S12].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the hard part. Indiana allows 12.9 points a game (4th in FBS) and 75.4 rushing yards a game (4th) [S8]. It has 24 sacks [S3], seven of them by Tobi Osunsanmi [S4].
Their offense vs. our defense: Indiana scores 36.6 points a game, and Josh Hoover hasn't thrown an interception [S8][S4]. Michigan's pass defense ranks 14th [S8]. Hoover hurt his right shoulder against Ohio State. He missed one play and finished the game [S12]. I found no official update as of Oct. 18 [S13].
Series: Michigan leads 62-11 [S6], but Indiana won the last meeting, 20-15 in 2024 [S6]. The teams did not play in 2025 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Who plays quarterback, and whether Michigan can stop losing the ball. (2) Michigan's red-zone defense, which has allowed scores on 92.9% of opponent trips (118th) [S8]. (3) Whether Michigan's run defense can keep Indiana's ground game quiet for a third straight week [S12].
Mallory, I hear you're holding a sash for me. In Ann Arbor, we call that a participation ribbon. Kindly meant.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Game day starts with breakfast at Fleetwood Diner on South Ashley Street, a downtown Ann Arbor classic.

My call: Indiana Hoosiers 26, Michigan Wolverines 17.

report.title: "In a World...": Sterling Ashworth-Vance Premieres the Trojans in Madison
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

In a world... where one team plays every Saturday like it's opening night... Good evening, I'm Sterling Ashworth-Vance, film buff, football historian and your guide to the Trojans. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, polished and presented in glorious widescreen. I treat every game like a premiere, because at USC, every game is one. The Coliseum is the grandest movie set in sports, and every fall our Trojans play the lead. Traveler gallops, the band strikes up, and Los Angeles remembers why it loves this team. When we win, the music swells and I say, "Roll credits." When we lose, I call it a second-act setback, because the best films always have one. Fight On! (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Trojans were formed in 1888 [S6]. The program has more than 860 wins and claims 11 national championships, seven of them from the AP and/or Coaches polls [S6]. USC has had 13 undefeated seasons, eight of them perfect [S6]. We now play in the Big Ten, at the 77,500-seat Los Angeles Memorial Coliseum in Exposition Park, right next to campus [S6]. CFBD dates the Coliseum to 1923 [S2]. The last five seasons: 4-8, 11-3, 8-5, 7-6 in our first Big Ten year, and 9-4 [S2]. A classic comeback arc.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Lincoln Riley is the director's chair; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2021 [S2]. His offense is a blockbuster: 310.1 passing yards a game (7th in FBS), 462.4 total yards (17th) and 36.4 points (27th) [S5]. We convert 51.2% of third downs, 14th [S5], and hold the ball 32:50 a game (21st) [S5]. The defense stops the run, 111 yards allowed (32nd) [S5], with 15 sacks [S2]. The plot hole: the pass defense allows 239 yards a game, 109th [S5], and opponents score on 84.6% of red zone trips (76th) [S5]. Every great film needs some tension.

4. Players to Know

• QB Jayden Maiava: 152 of 224 for 2,045 yards, 18 TD, 3 INT [S4][S5]. CollegeFootballDigest says he's No. 2 in FBS in passing yards [S9]. At Penn State he went 21 of 33 for 301 yards and three scores [S5]. Leading-man material.
• RB King Miller: 595 yards on 114 carries, 4 TD; 102 yards and a touchdown at Penn State [S4][S5].
• WR Kayden Dixon-Wyatt: 27 catches, 400 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. Trent Mosley: nine catches for 111 yards and a touchdown at Penn State [S5].
• S Christian Pierce: team-leading tackler [S4][S9]. S Kennedy Urlacher: 3 sacks [S4]. CB Prophet Brown: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

USC is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Big Ten, ranked No. 16 by the AP and No. 15 in the coaches poll [S2][S5]. The wins: San José State 42-26, Fresno State 39-0, Louisiana 49-30, at Rutgers 42-35, Washington 25-21 and at Penn State 31-23 [S2]. The one loss: Oregon, 41-27 [S2]. We had last week off [S2]. After Madison comes a true blockbuster: No. 3 Ohio State at the Coliseum on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math tonight. I'll only say the sequel is lining up beautifully.
The road so far: two road games, two wins [S2]. Our heroes travel well.
The one dark scene: Oregon came to the Coliseum and won 41-27 [S2]. Every great franchise has an episode like that. What matters is what came next: a 25-21 win over Washington and that statement night at Penn State [S2]. That's a hero who gets knocked down in act two and gets back up for the finale.

6. This Week: No. 16 USC (6-1) at Wisconsin (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC [S1][S5][S8]. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph [S9].
The backstory: USC leads the series 7-1 [S9]. The meetings include the Rose Bowl after the 1962 season, a 42-37 USC win, and a Holiday Bowl after 2015 that Wisconsin won 23-21 [S9]. The last meeting, in 2024, went to USC 38-21 [S9]. A rich film library.
Last time out: we beat Penn State 31-23 on Oct. 10 [S5]. Wisconsin lost 17-7 at UCLA on Oct. 17 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is the main event. Wisconsin's defense is excellent: 286.7 yards allowed (17th), 171.2 passing yards allowed (20th) and 16.7 points (24th) [S5]. Maiava against that secondary is the scene everyone will remember.
Their offense vs. our defense: Wisconsin averages 351.8 yards (103rd) [S5], but quarterback Colton Joseph is also its leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD [S5]. And Wisconsin scores on 94.1% of red zone trips, 14th [S5].
Availability: no availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Maiava against a top-20 pass defense. (2) Containing Joseph's legs. (3) Our red zone defense.
To Lars "Brat" Ellefson, Wisconsin's insider: a cheese wedge at every game? Magnificent costume design. I'd cast you in a heartbeat.

Why I Love This Team

I love an offense that plays like a summer blockbuster [S5]. I love a quarterback with 18 touchdowns and three interceptions [S4]. I love that the Trojans have won on the road twice already [S2]. And I love the history: 11 national championships and a Rose Bowl win over this very opponent [S6][S9]. Roll credits.

report.title: "Pass the Curds": Brat Ellefson Welcomes the Trojans to Camp Randall
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Pass the curds. (Polka accordion: oom-pah, oom-pah.) Hiya, folks, I'm Lars Ellefson, but everybody calls me Brat. I was a fullback for the Badgers back in my day, and I still carry a cheese wedge to every game. Every single one. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, wholesome as a glass of cold milk. You'll notice I play a little polka before I share a stat. My doctor says it's good for my heart. When we win, I jump around, literally, and pass out cheese curds. When we lose, I eat a brat in thoughtful silence. Then I eat another one. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

(Oom-pah.) The Badgers have played in the Big Ten since it formed in 1896 [S7]. Wisconsin is one of 26 programs to win 700 or more games [S7]. Home is Camp Randall Stadium, the fourth-oldest stadium in college football [S7], opened in 1917 and listed at 80,321 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were 9-4, 7-6, 7-6, 5-7 and 4-8 [S3]. So this 4-2 start? That's a fresh batch of squeaky curds, folks. Squeaky fresh.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Luke Fickell is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 27, 2022 [S3]. (Oom-pah.) This team is built on defense, the way a good barn is built on a stone foundation. We allow 286.7 yards a game (17th in FBS), 171.2 passing yards (20th), 115.5 rushing yards (37th) and 16.7 points (24th) [S5]. Now, the offense. I love it like family, and family is honest: 351.8 yards a game (103rd) and 199.7 passing yards (100th) [S5]. But in the red zone, we score on 94.1% of trips, 14th in the country [S5]. Get us close, and we'll punch it in. Spoken like a fullback.

4. Players to Know

• QB Colton Joseph: 87 of 159 for 1,198 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT, and he's also our leading rusher, 333 yards and 4 TD on 69 carries [S4][S5]. At UCLA he ran 18 times for 71 yards and a touchdown [S5]. That's my kind of quarterback. Fullback heart.
• WR Tyrell Henry: 27 catches, 343 yards, 1 TD [S4][S5].
• RB Abu Sama III: six carries for 34 yards at UCLA [S5]. WR Jaylon Domingeaux: two catches for 26 yards [S5].
• LB Cooper Catalano: team-high 50 tackles [S4][S9]. LB Sebastian Cheeks: 2.5 sacks [S4]. S Marvin Burks Jr.: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

(Oom-pah.) Wisconsin is 4-2 and 2-1 in the Big Ten, 3-0 at home [S3]. We opened with a 41-13 loss to Notre Dame at a neutral site, then beat Western Illinois 36-9, Eastern Michigan 54-10, Penn State 24-20 on the road and Michigan State 31-3 [S3]. Last week, UCLA beat us 17-7 [S3]. After USC, we head to No. 15 Iowa on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math. I'm just saying a win over a ranked team at Camp Randall would make the whole state jump.
The Penn State win is the one I'll keep telling my grandkids about: on the road, 24-20 [S3]. That's a cheese wedge held high.
Season so far, by the polka: the Notre Dame game was a slow waltz we didn't want to dance [S3]. Then came three home wins and that road win at Penn State, a real toe-tapper [S3]. Michigan State managed just 3 points against our defense [S3]. UCLA held us to 7, and Joseph completed 6 of 16 passes [S5]. That's a sour note, folks. But we had a week off before UCLA, and the band's been practicing ever since [S3]. (Oom-pah.) I've seen this defense all year. It's the real deal, and it'll keep us in this one.
A fullback's note on Joseph: 69 carries through six games [S4]. That young man runs like he's carrying the cheese wedge himself.

6. This Week: No. 16 USC (6-1) at Wisconsin (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 Central) · Camp Randall Stadium, Madison · NBC [S1][S5][S8]. Forecast at kickoff: 65 degrees, mostly cloudy, south wind 10 mph [S9]. Perfect brat weather.
The history: USC leads the series 7-1 [S9]. Our one win came in the Holiday Bowl after the 2015 season, 23-21 [S9]. The last meeting, in 2024, went to USC 38-21 [S9]. Time to even things up a little, eh?
Their offense vs. our defense: here's the big one. USC throws for 310.1 yards a game (7th) [S5], and Jayden Maiava has 18 touchdown passes [S5]. Our pass defense is 20th [S5]. That's a heavyweight bout at the county fair.
Our offense vs. their defense: USC's pass defense ranks 109th [S5], so Joseph should have chances. And USC allows opponents to score on 84.6% of red zone trips [S5]. Get us inside the 20, folks.
Availability: no availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Our pass defense against Maiava. (2) Joseph's legs and our red zone finishing. (3) Third downs; USC converts 51.2% (14th) [S5].
To Sterling Ashworth-Vance, USC's insider: I'd be honored to be in your movie, as long as I get to play the fullback.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Madison for the game? State Street Brats on State Street. A brat before the game is tradition in my house.

report.title: "Hydrate and Dominate": Skylar Vanterpool Welcomes the Wildcats to Tempe
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hi, Sun Devil Nation, and welcome to The Cover Window! I'm Skylar Vanterpool. Yes, I'm the girl by the pool in the giant maroon sunhat, and yes, I also have a master's degree in sports science, so I will talk your ear off about recovery windows and sweat rates. I travel with this team and live with this team. Fair warning: about every 90 seconds I'm going to remind you to drink some water. It's not a bit. Okay, it's a little bit a bit. My motto is simple: "Hydrate and dominate." When we win, I cannonball into a kiddie pool on set. When we lose, it's "Hydrate, reflect, recover," and then a well-earned nap. Every week I'll bring you the players, the coaches and the matchup, with plenty of sunshine and zero sunburn. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Sun Devil football has a Rose Bowl ring to it. On Jan. 1, 1987, quarterback Jeff Van Raaphorst led a comeback as Arizona State beat Michigan 22-15 in Pasadena [S15]. More recently, the Sun Devils won the 2024 Big 12 championship, beating Iowa State 45-19 in the title game [S14]. Home is Mountain America Stadium in Tempe, listed at a capacity of 65,870 [S2][S18]. This team also gets around: in Week 3 it beat Kansas 24-17 at Wembley Stadium in London, England, in the Union Jack Classic [S18]. Sip of water. Okay, moving on.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kenny Dillingham became Arizona State's 26th head coach on Nov. 27, 2022, and took the Sun Devils to the Big 12 title in his second season [S14]. The 2026 numbers say this offense lives through the air. ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game and has 15 passing touchdowns, against 7 on the ground [S2]. It averages 31.3 points and 420.3 yards a game, and runs on about 48% of its plays at 4.42 yards a carry [S2]. The defense is where we need some shade and electrolytes: ASU allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. Two more things to fix are 15 sacks allowed and 10 turnovers lost against 6 forced [S2]. After last week, Dillingham said, "We almost gotta double down on that, because we're doing a lot well." [S9]

4. Players to Know

• QB Cutter Boley (junior, Kentucky transfer): the season starter. One preview lists him at 1,229 yards, 12 TD and 3 INT, though that snapshot may not include the most recent game [S16]. At Texas Tech he went 5 of 10 for 124 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions before he was benched at halftime [S8][S10].
• QB Mikey Keene (sixth-year): 25 of 34 for 256 yards and two touchdowns in the second half at Texas Tech [S8]. He's on the Pat Tillman Leadership Council and has played at UCF, Fresno State and Michigan [S9].
• WR Reed Harris (senior): 34 catches, 590 yards and 7 TD in the same preview snapshot [S16].
• WR Raiden Vines-Bright: caught a 74-yard touchdown at Texas Tech [S8][S10]. WR Derek Eusebio: led the team with seven catches for 89 yards last week after an injury-slowed start [S10].
• RB Cardae Mack (freshman): seven carries for 27 yards and a touchdown catch at Texas Tech [S10].
I could not find current, dated season defensive leaders, so I'm leaving them out rather than guessing.

5. The Conference Picture

Arizona State is 3-3 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 2-1 at home and 0-2 on the road, plus the Wembley win at a neutral site [S2][S18]. The Sun Devils are not ranked this week [S2]. The league losses were 55-19 at home to Baylor and 53-25 at Texas Tech [S18]. The top two Big 12 teams meet in the championship game [S4], and both teams in this one are 1-2, so this is a big afternoon in the desert.

6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 12:45 p.m. MST (3:45 p.m. ET) · Mountain America Stadium · ESPN2 [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first visit to Tempe since 1989 [S17].
Last week: ASU trailed Texas Tech 43-10 at halftime and lost 53-25 [S10]. Kansas State came from behind to beat Kansas 35-24, with 568 yards of offense and 359 on the ground [S6].
Our offense vs. their defense: K-State allows only 136.3 passing yards a game and has 13 sacks [S2]. Our pass protection gave up a season-high six sacks last week, even with center Tana Alo-Tupuola and guard Wade Helton back from missed time [S9][S10].
Their offense vs. our defense: the Wildcats run the ball well, at 6.23 yards a carry [S2]. Quarterback Avery Johnson has 462 rushing yards to go with 1,301 passing [S5], and running back Joe Jackson ran for 159 yards against Kansas [S6]. Our run defense allows 4.80 a carry [S2], so tackling is the whole story. Arizona Sports pointed to tackling as a problem at Texas Tech [S10].
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1 and won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5].
Availability: I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham said he would "assess all personnel" after watching the tape and has not named a starting quarterback [S8]. Johnson was shaken up against Kansas but said he only had the wind knocked out of him [S7].
What decides it: (1) Boley or Keene, and how quickly that quarterback gets settled. (2) Whether our front can win at the point of attack against K-State's run game. (3) Protection. Six sacks can't happen again.
And to Hattie Brandvold, K-State's insider: welcome to Tempe, sweetie! I left a cold water bottle at your seat. It's a dry heat, but your crops will still wilt.
