report.title: "You Can't Rush a Harvest": Hattie Brandvold Takes the Wildcats to the Desert
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy, Wildcat family, and welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Hattie Brandvold. I have an agronomy degree, a purple denim jacket, a wheat-sheaf brooch and a field notebook with real Flint Hills dirt on it. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I explain defensive fronts the only way I know how: crop rotation. Every drive gets named after a crop. A three-and-out is a dry sorghum patch. A long, patient march is winter wheat. And a touchdown? That's a bumper harvest, and you will hear me holler it. When we win, I do the Wabash Cannonball in my chair, tidy and joyful. When we lose, I whisper my most treasured words, "You can't rush a harvest," and I plant a tiny basil seed right there on set. Sweet as prairie pie, until I hand you the one fact that ends the argument. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Kansas State football is the story of the biggest turnaround in the sport. When Bill Snyder took over in 1989, the program was in the middle of a 27-game winless streak. He turned it into a national contender that went to 11 straight bowl games and had six 11-win seasons in a seven-year stretch [S19]. Snyder won two Big 12 championships, one in 2003 with Darren Sproles and one in 2012 [S12]. He went into the College Football Hall of Fame while still coaching, in December 2015 [S12]. The Wildcats play at Bill Snyder Family Stadium in Manhattan [S2], and the rivalry with Kansas is the Sunflower Showdown, played for the Governor's Cup [S6]. As of last Saturday, K-State has won that game 18 straight times, the longest active winning streak by any team in a rivalry game [S6]. Now that's a crop that keeps coming back every spring.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Collin Klein was named the 36th head coach in school history on Dec. 4, 2025 [S11]. You may remember him as the quarterback: he was a 2012 Heisman Trophy finalist and won the Johnny Unitas Award that year, when K-State won the Big 12 [S11][S13]. He is the first K-State alum to be head coach since Ellis Rainsberger in 1975-77 [S11]. Before this job he coached nine years in Manhattan, including two as offensive coordinator (2022-23) that went 19-8 with a Big 12 title, then ran the offense at Texas A&M [S11]. The 2026 numbers say this offense grows on the ground. K-State runs on about 54% of its plays and gains 6.23 yards a carry, with 15 rushing touchdowns [S2]. It averages 35.5 points and 464.7 yards a game [S2]. On defense, the Wildcats allow 20.0 points and 296.3 yards a game, and only 136.3 passing yards [S2]. They have 13 sacks and have allowed just 3 [S2]. One weed to pull: six turnovers lost against four forced [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Avery Johnson (senior, Wichita): 1,301 passing yards and 462 rushing yards, leading the team in both [S5]. Against Kansas he passed for 209 yards and a touchdown and ran for 132, and he became the school's all-time leader in total offensive yards [S6]. He went down after a 59-yard run and pointed to his right shoulder, but he returned and said, "I just got the wind knocked out of me." [S7]
• RB Joe Jackson (senior): a season-high 159 yards and a touchdown against Kansas [S6][S7].
• WR Jaron Tibbs: the team's leading receiver with 268 yards [S5].
• K Luis Rodriguez: four field goals against Kansas, from 22, 51, 28 and 34 yards, the second-most in a game in school history [S6].
• DB Logan Bartley: made an end-zone interception against Kansas [S6].
I could not find official season defensive leaders from a source newer than the start of October, so I'm not listing them.

5. The Conference Picture

K-State is 4-2 overall and 1-2 in the Big 12, 4-1 at home and 0-1 on the road [S2]. The Wildcats are not ranked in the AP or Coaches poll this week [S2]. The two league losses came at Cincinnati, 31-26, and at home against Houston, 35-16 [S2][S6]. The top two teams in the Big 12 meet in the championship game [S4], so a 1-2 start means every Saturday from here matters.

6. This Week: Kansas State (4-2) at Arizona State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 3:45 p.m. ET (12:45 p.m. MST) · Mountain America Stadium, Tempe · ESPN2 [S3][S1]. It's K-State's first game in Tempe since the 1989 season opener, and the Wildcats' last game in this stadium was a 31-14 bowl win over Michigan in 2013 [S17].
Last week: K-State trailed Kansas 17-7 in the first quarter, then won 35-24 and racked up 568 yards, 359 of them on the ground [S6]. Arizona State lost 53-25 at Texas Tech. Coach Kenny Dillingham replaced quarterback Cutter Boley with Mikey Keene at halftime, and Keene threw for 256 yards and two touchdowns [S8][S10].
Our offense vs. their defense: this is where my winter wheat should grow. Arizona State allows 32.0 points and 373.2 yards a game, and 4.80 yards a carry [S2]. Texas Tech gained 7.8 yards a play against the Sun Devils last week [S10].
Their offense vs. our defense: ASU throws for 276.7 yards a game [S2], and senior receiver Reed Harris is a big-play threat [S16][S9]. But the Sun Devils have allowed 15 sacks, including a season-high six at Texas Tech [S2][S9]. K-State has 13 sacks of its own [S2].
Series: Arizona State leads 6-1, and the Sun Devils won the last meeting, 24-14 in Manhattan in 2024 [S4][S5]. K-State's lone win was 34-27 on Dec. 27, 2002 [S5].
Availability: Johnson's shoulder scare turned out to be the wind knocked out of him [S7]. I found no official availability report for either team as of Oct. 18, 2026. Dillingham has not named a starting quarterback for this game [S8][S9].
What decides it: (1) Can K-State's run game keep producing like it did against Kansas? (2) Who plays quarterback for Arizona State, Boley or Keene? (3) Can our pass rush get home against a front that gave up six sacks last week?
And to Skylar Vanterpool, Arizona State's insider: I'll bring the shade hat and the water jug, darlin'. Hydrate all you like. You still can't rush a harvest.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Watching from Manhattan? Varsity Donuts on North Manhattan Avenue is how I start every game-day morning.

My call: Kansas State Wildcats 32, Arizona State Sun Devils 27.

report.title: "Carolina Blue, Through and Through": Ainsley Pemberton Welcomes the Orange to Kenan
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Carolina blue, through and through. Hello, darlings, I'm Ainsley Pemberton. I grew up in Chapel Hill, I came out at a debutante ball, and then I went and earned a PhD in kinesiology, because a lady should understand exactly how a linebacker generates force. I travel with the Tar Heels and I live with the Tar Heels, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Southern charm and, I'll confess, a gentle little roast of a certain school eight miles down the road. I don't even need Duke to be on the schedule. When we win, I graciously thank our guests, then whisper "Carolina blue, through and through." When we lose, I say "Carolina blue skies will return," and I absolutely refuse to cry on camera. Mostly. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Tar Heels, often just "Carolina," represent the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill in the ACC [S7]. North Carolina has played in 37 bowl games and won three Southern Conference titles and five ACC titles [S7]. Home is Kenan Stadium, opened in 1927 and listed at 50,500 seats [S3], and darling, there is no prettier place in college football on an autumn evening. The last five seasons: 6-7, a lovely 9-5 in 2022, 8-5, 6-7 and 4-8 last year [S3].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Bill Belichick is our head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2024 [S3]. This team wins with defense and discipline. We allow 19.2 points a game, 34th in FBS [S5], our red zone defense ranks 22nd [S5], and we average just 33.7 penalty yards a game, 5th in the country [S5]. Darling, that's manners. Xavier Lewis has 7 sacks [S4]. The offense is a work in progress: 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th) [S5]. And opponents convert 43.3% of third downs against us (113th) [S5]. Elegant, mostly. Not always. But a team that wins close games on the road, two weeks in a row, has learned how to finish, and finishing is the most elegant skill of all [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Billy Edwards Jr.: 94 of 157 for about 1,260 yards (1,259 per AP), 9 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. A first-year Tar Heel, he said he felt "the weight of this game" against Duke [S9].
• WR Jordan Shipp: 33 catches, 441 yards [S4][S5]. He caught the first touchdown at Duke and said, "That's why you come to Carolina, for a rivalry game like that" [S9].
• RB Jaylen McGill: 12 carries for 75 yards and the game-winning 24-yard touchdown with 1:53 left at Duke [S5][S9]. RB Benjamin Hall: the season leader with 283 yards [S4].
• TE Jelani Thurman: caught the 12-yard fourth-and-4 conversion on the winning drive [S9].
• DL Xavier Lewis: 7 sacks [S4]. LB Derek McDonald: team-high 55 tackles [S4]. DB Greg Smith III: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

North Carolina is 4-2 and 2-1 in the ACC [S3]. We beat TCU 15-10 at a neutral site, East Tennessee State 35-3, Pittsburgh 21-17 on the road and Duke 24-20 on the road [S3]. We lost at Clemson 28-20 and to Notre Dame 37-26 [S3]. After Syracuse, No. 1 Miami comes to Kenan on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, darling. I'll only say it's a lovely time to be wearing blue.
And the Victory Bell is home. After the Duke game, our players rushed across the field to reclaim it [S9]. AP says the bell kept ringing so loudly outside the locker room it nearly interrupted Coach Belichick's press conference [S9]. I'd call that the sweetest music in the Triangle. And two years ago in that same stadium, Duke rallied from 20 points down to beat us [S9]. This time, darling, the bell came home with us, where it belongs. Duke had won eight straight against in-state opponents before we arrived [S9]. Bless their hearts.

6. This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we beat Duke 24-20. We led 17-0, went more than 41 minutes without scoring, then marched 78 yards for the winner [S9]. On fourth-and-4 from our own 28, Coach said, "I wasn't punting again. I wanted to take our best shot" [S9]. Syracuse lost to Louisville 34-26 [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: Syracuse throws for 291 yards a game (12th) [S5], and Umari Hatcher has 784 receiving yards, including 224 last week [S5]. Darling, we must know where he is at all times. Their quarterback situation is unsettled; no Week 8 ACC report yet [S10][S11].
Our offense vs. their defense: Syracuse's pass defense ranks 43rd and its run defense 64th [S5]. Syracuse is also 138th in penalty yards [S5]. Free yards are always welcome at Kenan.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
Availability: no North Carolina availability report found as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Containing Hatcher. (2) Getting off the field on third down. (3) Staying the most disciplined team on the field [S5].
To Nico Calabrese, Syracuse's insider: a snowbank shaped like a block S? How charming. We have dogwoods. Come in April, darling.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Chapel Hill for the game? La Residence on West Rosemary Street is a lovely sit-down supper.

report.title: "A Foot of Snow of a Take": Nico Calabrese Heads South to Chapel Hill
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

That's a foot of snow of a take. Hey, how ya doin', I'm Nico Calabrese, born and raised in the Salt City, survivor of more lake-effect winters than I can count. I travel with the Orange and I live with the Orange, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with full upstate bluster. My scale for every play is feet of snow. A two-yard run? A dusting. A long touchdown? Twenty inches overnight, school's canceled. A turnover by us? That's the plow truck sliding into the ditch. When we win, I'll yell "That's a foot of snow of a WIN!" so loud they'll hear me in Utica. When we lose, I shrug: "Just a lake-effect squall." Then I grab a salt potato and get back to work. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Syracuse plays in the ACC, and here's a fact I love: it's the only FBS school in New York in a Power Four conference [S6]. Home is the JMA Wireless Dome on campus, also known as "The Loud House" [S6], opened in 1980 and listed at 49,057 seats [S2]. The last five seasons: 5-7, 7-6, 6-7, a big 10-3 in 2024 and 3-9 last year [S2]. That 10-3 year? That was the Blizzard of '93, the one we still talk about.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Fran Brown is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 28, 2023 [S2]. This offense throws it: 291 passing yards a game, 12th in FBS, and 449.7 total yards (29th) [S5]. We hold the ball 33:59 a game, 5th in FBS [S5]. The defense is solid against the pass, 191.8 yards allowed (43rd) [S5], with 15 sacks [S2]. The problem? Penalties. We average 98 penalty yards a game, 138th in the country [S5]. That's driving the Thruway in a whiteout with the brakes on. And in the red zone we score on 78.1% of trips, 111th [S5]. Clean those two up and this is a different team.

4. Players to Know

• WR Umari Hatcher: 50 catches, 784 yards, 7 TD [S4][S5]. Against Louisville he caught 13 passes for 224 yards and a touchdown [S5]. That's three feet overnight, folks. Lake Ontario is jealous.
• QB Malachi Nelson: threw for 315 yards and two touchdowns, with two interceptions, against Louisville [S5]. The local paper's headline says he left that game with another injury [S11].
• QB Steve Angeli: the season passing leader, 57 of 104, 731 yards, 4 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. He was out for the Louisville game [S10].
• RB Tylik Hill: 431 yards on 80 carries [S4][S5]. RB Ahmad Miller: 123 yards and a touchdown on 18 carries against Louisville [S5].
• LB Chris D'Appolonia: team-high 42 tackles [S4]. LB Keyshawn Johnson: 4 sacks [S4]. DB Davien Kerr: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Syracuse is 2-4 and 0-4 in the ACC [S2]. We beat New Hampshire 66-3 and won a 42-41 thriller at UConn [S2]. The four league losses: California 21-18, at Pittsburgh 27-13, at Virginia 28-25 and Louisville 34-26 [S2]. Three of those were one-score games [S2]. After Chapel Hill, No. 23 SMU comes to the Dome on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math today. I'm just saying this team has been close, real close.
The close ones: a field goal against Cal, a field goal at Virginia, one score against Louisville [S2]. That's a whole winter of near-misses on the plow route.
Why I love this team anyway: because it keeps moving the ball no matter who's under center. Hatcher is on pace for a monster year [S4]. Miller ran hard last week [S5]. And the team that went 10-3 two years ago had a coach named Fran Brown too [S2]. Upstate folks don't quit when it snows. We shovel out, and we go to work.

6. This Week: Syracuse (2-4) at North Carolina (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET · Kenan Stadium, Chapel Hill · ACC Network [S1][S5][S8].
The quarterback question: I can't tell you who starts. The ACC hasn't posted a Week 8 availability report yet [S10]. Angeli was out last week, Nelson played and then, per the local paper's headline, left with another injury [S10][S11]. I'll update you when the report comes out. I won't guess.
Our offense vs. their defense: North Carolina allows opponents to convert 43.3% of third downs (113th) [S5], and its pass defense is 69th [S5]. Hatcher should get his chances. But the Tar Heels' red zone defense ranks 22nd [S5], and that's where we've struggled.
Their offense vs. our defense: North Carolina averages 329.7 yards a game (117th) and 116.2 rushing yards (120th) [S5]. Jordan Shipp leads them with 441 receiving yards [S5]. Our defense can win this matchup.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
What decides it: (1) Who's healthy at quarterback. (2) Penalties; they average 33.7 penalty yards a game (5th), we average 98 [S5]. (3) Red zone finishing.
To Ainsley Pemberton, North Carolina's insider: Carolina blue is nice, but have you ever seen a snowbank shaped like a block S? Come visit in February.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back home? Varsity Pizza on South Crouse Avenue has been feeding Orange fans on the hill for a long time. Get a slice.

report.title: "Roll Wave!": Twan Ducros-Labat Parades Into Week 8
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Roll Wave! Hey now, I'm Antoine Ducros-Labat, but all Uptown calls me Twan. I've lived within earshot of a brass band my whole life, and I believe every football game is a brass-band parade: you dance your way through it, no matter what. I travel with the Green Wave and I live with the Green Wave, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little music and a lot of food. You'll hear me say a big play "deserved a beignet." I mean that literally. I keep a bag of them in the booth. Uptown on game day, there's a brass band on every corner and a Green Wave flag on every porch. When we win, the parade rolls all night. When we lose, we still dance home. Roll Wave, and save me a beignet. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Green Wave represent Tulane University and compete in the American Conference [S7]. Home is Yulman Stadium on campus in Uptown New Orleans [S7], opened in 2014 and listed at 30,000 seats [S3]. And the music lately has been sweet: after 2-10 in 2021, Tulane went 12-2, 11-3, 9-5 and 11-3 [S3]. That's four straight years of brass band, y'all.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Will Hall is the head coach [S7] in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 8, 2025 [S3]. The calling card of this defense is the red zone: opponents score on just 65.4% of their trips inside our 20, 5th in FBS [S5]. We allow 21.7 points a game, 50th [S5], and we have 12 sacks [S3]. That's a defense that bends like a trombone slide but doesn't break. The trouble spots: we allow 212.5 rushing yards a game (133rd) [S5], and opponents convert 45.6% of third downs (124th) [S5]. On offense, we gain 332 yards (116th) and score 20.5 points (117th) [S5]. We've turned it over just 5 times [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB: Kadin Semonza leads the team with 64 of 119 for 804 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5]. Trace Johnson started against Memphis and threw for 165 yards and a touchdown [S5]. Who starts this week? I haven't seen it announced [S9].
• RB Maurice Turner: 315 yards on just 37 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5]. That's 8.5 yards a carry, and that deserves a beignet.
• RB Johnnie Daniels: seven carries for 55 yards and a touchdown against Memphis [S5].
• WR Destyn Hill: 21 catches, 285 yards, 2 TD; a touchdown catch against Memphis [S4][S5].
• LB Dickson Agu: team-high 56 tackles [S4]. LB Makai Williams: 3 sacks [S4]. S Kevin Adams III: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Tulane is 3-3 and 1-1 in the American, 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road [S3]. The home wins: South Alabama 28-24, Southern Miss 24-21 and Memphis 31-17 [S3]. The road losses: at Duke 17-3, at Kansas State 31-20 and a 20-17 heartbreaker at Army [S3]. After UTSA, we go to Charlotte on Oct. 30 [S5]. No standings math in the booth tonight. I'll just say Yulman's been our happy place, and this week we're home.
Home sweet home: three games at Yulman, three wins [S3]. The brass band knows the way.
Season so far: the Army loss was by a field goal [S3]. The Southern Miss win was by a field goal [S3]. This team lives in close games, and close games at Yulman have gone our way. When the Memphis game was over, I swear the whole neighborhood was dancing. That's what this team does for Uptown. A good brass band doesn't play the same song twice, and neither does this team. One week it's the defense, the next week it's Turner breaking a long one. Somebody always steps up to lead the parade.

6. This Week: UTSA (6-1) at Tulane (3-3)

report.title: "Birds Up!": Marisol Ybarra Brings the Fiesta to New Orleans
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Birds up! ¡Hola, y'all! I'm Marisol Ybarra, born and raised in San Antonio, and I have a confession: I collect Fiesta medals. Hundreds of them. They fill a whole wall of my living room, and every great Roadrunner play earns a brand-new medal. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with Tex-Mex warmth and Fiesta energy. I read an offense the way I read a parade route: every float has to be on time, every band in step. When we win, I yell "Birds up!" and crack a cascarón full of confetti over the nearest head. When we lose, I tell you, "The parade will come back around." It always does in San Antonio. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Roadrunners represent the University of Texas at San Antonio and compete in the American Conference [S6]. Home is the Alamodome, which seats 65,000 but is normally set up for about 35,000 for UTSA games [S6]; CFBD lists 36,582 [S2]. Jeff Traylor has coached the team since 2020 [S6]. The offense scores 32.3 points a game (49th), runs for 179.4 (49th) and throws for 231.7 (68th) [S5]. Now, the confetti mess to clean up: the run defense allows 199.9 yards a game, 128th [S5], and we average 83.9 penalty yards a game, 134th [S5]. A parade can't win with floats going backward, y'all.

After New Orleans, we have a week off, then visit Florida Atlantic on Nov. 5 [S5]. I won't do standings math, y'all. I'll just say an unbeaten league record is the best kind of parade.
The close ones: four of our six wins came by a touchdown or less [S2]. Rice by two, Navy by four, Texas State by five [S2]. This team knows how to finish the parade route.
Why I love this team: it never panics. Down late? McCown just keeps throwing strikes [S5]. And that 59-45 win over Colorado State? I wore out my confetti supply that night [S2]. And the Texas loss? Every parade hits a rainy day. We were on the road against a big SEC program, and we came home and won four straight [S2]. That's San Antonio grit, y'all. The parade always comes back around.

report.title: "Send It": Ridge Corbell Celebrates 130 Years of Wolf Pack Football
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Send it! What's up, Wolf Pack, I'm Ridge Corbell. I ski patrol at Tahoe in the winter, I scout football on a snowboard (figuratively, mostly), and I've discovered that snowboard slang explains advanced football stats better than anything on a whiteboard. Third-down conversion rate? That's just how often you land the jump. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, chill on the outside and surprisingly sharp with the math underneath. When we win, you'll hear "Sick!" and I'll mime a backflip. When we lose, I'll shrug and call it a powder day that went sideways, and then I'll dig into the film. Strap in. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Nevada football was founded on Oct. 24, 1896, as the Sagebrushers [S7]. Check the calendar, friends: Saturday is the program's 130th birthday [S7]. We play at Mackay Stadium on the north end of campus [S7]. The "new" Mackay opened Oct. 1, 1966, seats 27,000, and its field sits 4,610 feet above sea level [S7][S3]. Coach Chris Ault, running back Frank Hawkins and coach Buck Shaw are in the College Football Hall of Fame, and fullback Marion Motley is in the Pro Football Hall of Fame [S7]. We compete in the Mountain West [S7]. Recent years have been a climb: 8-5 in 2021, then 2-10, 2-10, 3-10 and 3-9 [S3]. Every run starts at the top of the hill.
The trail so far in 2026: we opened with a 49-14 rout of Western Kentucky that was pure fresh powder [S3]. Then Montana State, an FCS power, beat us 20-7 at home, and we lost close ones at Middle Tennessee (27-20) and to Air Force (36-33) [S3]. A 30-13 win at UTEP got us back on the board in league play [S3]. Last week in Fargo we led 11-0 before the special-teams avalanche [S9]. Add it up and this team is closer than its record. Two of the four losses were one-score games, and we led last week's game in the second quarter [S3][S9]. Close is not the same as sending it, but it's the slope right before.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jeff Choate was hired Dec. 4, 2023 [S3]. The 2026 Wolf Pack carve on the ground: 192.8 rushing yards a game, 37th in FBS [S5], 1,140 yards on 218 carries, about 5.2 a carry [S3]. The passing game is lighter, 171.8 yards a game (122nd) [S5]. The defense has a sick pass coverage number, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS, and holds opponents to 32.6% on third down (29th) [S5]. The wipeouts: run defense, 184.3 allowed a game (116th), red zone defense, 94.4% scoring allowed (127th), and turnover margin, minus-8 (134th) [S5]. We've lost 11 turnovers and forced just 3 [S3]. That's the run we need to clean up.

4. Players to Know

• RB Dominic Kelley: 500 yards on 87 carries, 4 TD [S4][S5].
• QB Carter Jones: 53 of 89, 654 yards, 3 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5].
• QB A.J. Bianco: played at North Dakota State, 17 of 34 for 190 yards, a touchdown pass and a rushing touchdown, with two interceptions [S5][S9]. Saturday's starter has not been announced in anything I found as of Oct. 18 [S10].
• WR Gary Givens III: 15 catches, 260 yards, 1 TD [S4][S5]. He caught a 19-yard touchdown at NDSU [S9].
• LB EJ Smith: a team-high 71 tackles [S4]. Myles Williams: 2.5 sacks [S4]. DB Bryson Snelling: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Nevada is 2-4 overall and 1-2 in the Mountain West [S3]. The wins: Western Kentucky 49-14 and at UTEP 30-13 [S3]. The losses: Montana State 20-7, at Middle Tennessee 27-20, Air Force 36-33 and at North Dakota State 31-17 [S3]. Two of those four losses were one-score games [S3]. After this, it's a trip to UCLA on Oct. 31 [S5]. A home league win would be the cleanest run we've had all year.

6. This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Mackay Stadium · MW+ [S1][S5][S8]. Happy 130th, Wolf Pack [S7].
Last week: we led 11-0 early at North Dakota State and lost 31-17 [S9]. A 57-yard field goal try came up short and was returned 100 yards for a touchdown, and a trick play on a two-point try was fumbled and returned for two Bison points [S9]. San José State beat UTEP 24-11 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: SJSU allows 240.9 passing yards (111th) and 148.3 rushing (83rd) [S5]. Its pass rush has 27 sacks [S2], so protection is the whole run.
Their offense vs. our defense: the Spartans convert 34.4% of third downs (111th) [S5]. Our third-down defense, 29th, should land that jump [S5]. Jabari Bates has 556 rushing yards, and our run defense has to hold [S5].
Series: we won five of nine meetings from 2016 through 2025 [S3].
Availability: no injury or availability report found as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Turnovers: we can't keep giving the ball away. (2) Red zone defense. (3) Kelley and the run game against an 83rd-ranked run defense [S5].
And Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz, SJSU's insider: welcome to altitude. I'll lend you a beanie.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

I'll keep the Reno tips to the mountains this week: take the family up to Tahoe for the leaves after the game.

report.title: "Red or Green? Both.": Paloma Begaye-Ortiz Welcomes the Bison to Albuquerque

THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Red or green? Both. ¡Hola, Albuquerque! I'm Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, and when I'm not at a Lobos game, I'm floating a hot-air balloon over the Rio Grande at sunrise. Every October I fly in the Balloon Fiesta, and every Saturday I read Lobo football like wind currents: where it's drifting, where it's rising, and when it's about to soar. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with some green-chile spice and a balloon metaphor for every drive. That offense floated like a balloon at dawn, up and up. When we win, I yell, "Red or green? BOTH!" and pump my fist. When we lose, I sigh, "Too much heat today." (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The New Mexico Lobos compete in the Mountain West [S7]. Our colors are cherry and silver [S7]. Home is University Stadium in Albuquerque [S7], opened in 1960 and listed at 39,224 seats [S3]. The last five years started low: 3-9, 2-10, 4-8, then 5-7 and a big 9-4 in 2025 [S3]. That's a balloon catching a thermal, y'all. Up and up.

Just know an unbeaten league record is a beautiful view from up here.
About Oklahoma: an SEC team, on the road, and we held them to 14 points [S3]. That's a balloon that didn't drop an inch in a strong wind.
Season so far, from the basket: it's been a sunrise flight, y'all. Five wins, all five by 11 points or more [S3]. When the wind is with you, you just enjoy the view. The defense has allowed 63 points in six games, total [S3]. The Hawai'i trip was a long flight over the Pacific, and we landed it, 21-10 [S3]. Every pilot knows the hardest part is the landing. This team keeps sticking them. And last year's 9-4 team taught this group how to win. Now they're doing it with even more style.

By my math from the season totals, we score about 29.4 points a game and allow about 11.3 [S2][S12]. We've run it 287 times for 1,223 yards and thrown for 1,311 [S2]. Opponents average about 112 rushing yards a game against us [S2][S12]. We've taken the ball away 14 times and given it away 6 [S2]. That's plus-8, which in my model is "very good." And we have 12 sacks [S2]. Two shutouts, too: Fordham 38-0 and Wyoming 28-0 [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Nathan Hayes: 106 of 163 for 1,272 yards, 10 TD, 5 INT [S4][S9]. Against Nevada he went 19 of 25 for 153 yards and accounted for three touchdowns [S10].
• WR Jackson Williams: 28 catches, 432 yards, 1 TD [S4][S9]. And oh, for cute: against Nevada he caught a missed 57-yard field-goal try in the end zone and ran it back 100 yards for a touchdown [S10]. He also ran for a score and threw a touchdown pass [S10]. That young man deserves extra hotdish.
• RB Myles Mitchell: 354 yards on 81 carries, 3 TD [S4].
• LB Donovan Woolen: team-high 51 tackles, 1.5 sacks and an interception [S4][S9]. DE Kelton McCaslin: 4 sacks [S4]. CB Marion Moore: 4 interceptions [S4].
• Matthew Stenbroten returned a fumbled 2-point try for two points against Nevada [S10].

5. The Conference Picture

North Dakota State is 6-1 and 3-1 in the Mountain West [S2]. We beat Jacksonville State 33-7, Fordham 38-0, Air Force 38-32 on the road, Sacramento State 31-10 on the road, Wyoming 28-0 and Nevada 31-17 [S2]. The one loss: 13-7 at UNLV [S2]. After Albuquerque, we host UTEP on Oct. 31 [S9]. I won't do standings math, but my model is very pleased.
About that UNLV game: a six-point loss on the road [S2]. "Oh, yah, that's a tough one." I brought hotdish. Then the team bounced back against Nevada [S10].
Season so far, by the numbers I love: our defense has allowed 79 points in seven games, total [S2]. Nevada jumped out to an 11-0 lead last week, and nobody panicked [S10]. Williams scored three different ways, and the defense held Nevada to 17 [S10]. That's the Bison way, hon: steady, patient and then, all of a sudden, the game is over. Like a North Dakota winter. You don't notice it coming, and then it's February.

6. This Week: North Dakota State (6-1) at New Mexico (5-1)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 10 p.m. ET (8 p.m. Mountain) · University Stadium, Albuquerque · The CW [S1][S8][S9]. Forecast: 58 degrees, slight chance of showers [S9]. Practically a heat wave for Fargo folks.

Their offense vs. our defense: New Mexico scores about 39.7 points a game by my math, with 1,287 rushing yards in six games [S3][S12]. Scottre Humphrey has 422 rushing yards and 8 touchdowns [S4]. Oh for cute, they think they can run on us. We'll see.
Our offense vs. their defense: here's the gut punch: New Mexico has 21 takeaways and only 4 giveaways in six games [S3]. It allows about 92 rushing yards a game and has 19 sacks [S3][S12]. Hayes has to protect the football.
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Ball security against a defense that takes it away. (2) Stopping Humphrey. (3) Special teams; Williams just showed what they can do [S10].
To Paloma Begaye-Ortiz, New Mexico's insider: red or green? Oh, hon, I'm bringing tater tot hotdish. You'll love it.

report.title: "Ship It to Prod": Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz Launches Spartan Week in Reno
report.byline: Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz · San José State Insider
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Ship it to prod! Hi, Spartan Nation, I'm Tessa Nakagawa-Ruiz. By day I'm a product lead at a tech company down the road, and by Saturday I run Spartan game tape like an A/B test: version A, version B, and which one moved the chains. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I treat every game week like a product launch, complete with a roadmap, a standup and a retro. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, explained in plain football language (I promise to keep the jargon in the sprint backlog). When we win, I yell "Ship it to prod!" and do a celebratory keyboard smash. When we lose, I sigh "rollback," open a bug ticket and get to work on the fix. Let's launch. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

San José State first played a regular season in 1898 [S6]. Since then the Spartans have produced more than 90 All-Americans, won 18 conference championships and sent 139 players to the NFL, including Pro Football Hall of Famers Bill Walsh and Dick Vermeil [S6]. Home is CEFCU Stadium, built in 1933 as Spartan Stadium [S6], listed at 30,456 seats [S2]. Regional rivals include Fresno State, Stanford, Hawai'i and San Diego State [S6]. We play in the Mountain West [S6]. The last five years went 5-7, 7-5, 7-6, 7-6 and 3-9 [S2]. Release notes: version 2026 already has more wins than all of 2025 [S2].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Ken Niumatalolo is the head coach [S6], hired Jan. 21, 2024 [S2]. The 2026 build: an offense that throws for 246 yards a game (53rd) and runs for 138.7 (98th), averaging 21.4 points (111th) [S5]. The defense is the stable release. It allows 21.7 points a game, 50th in FBS [S5], and its pass rush has 27 sacks in seven games [S2]. That's a feature I'd demo to any investor. The defense does allow 240.9 passing yards a game (111th) [S5]. Two known bugs to patch: third downs, where we convert 34.4% (111th), and time of possession, 26:41 a game (135th) [S5]. We are clean, though, 47.3 penalty yards a game (31st) [S5]. Our turnover margin is exactly even, 0 [S5]. Balanced code.

4. Players to Know

• QB Luke Weaver: 132 of 209, 1,529 yards, 11 TD, 6 INT [S4][S5].
• QB Daniel Rolovich: led the offense at UTEP, 12 of 23 for 193 yards and a touchdown, plus 39 rushing yards [S5]. Who starts Saturday has not been announced in anything I could find as of Oct. 18 [S10].
• RB Jabari Bates: 556 yards on 120 carries, 1 TD [S4][S5]. Viliami Teu ran 20 times for 156 yards and two scores last week [S5].
• WR Carson Clark: 42 catches, 509 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5], with five catches for 104 and a touchdown against UTEP [S5].
• DL Jayland McGlothen: a team-high 6 sacks [S4]. LB Dylan Lee: 65 tackles [S4]. CB Caleb Womack: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

San José State is 4-3 overall and 2-1 in the Mountain West, and 3-1 away from home [S2]. The wins: at Eastern Michigan 27-21, Cal Poly 30-20, at Hawai'i 20-16 and at UTEP 24-11 [S2]. The losses: at USC 42-26, Fresno State 26-10 and Wyoming 16-13 [S2]. Nobody in this game is ranked [S2][S3]. Next up after Reno is New Mexico at home on Oct. 31 [S5], and that's a big sprint in the league race.
The retro so far: the three losses tell a story. USC is a Big Ten program and scored 42 on us in Los Angeles, but we put up 26 [S2]. Fresno State held us to 10 [S2]. And Wyoming beat us 16-13 in a game decided by a field goal [S2]. Meanwhile, three of our four wins came on the road [S2], which is exactly the kind of resilience I want in a product that has to ship on a deadline. The defense has carried the release: we've allowed 16 points or fewer in four of seven games [S2]. If the offense can hold up its end in Reno, this team starts November in the thick of things.

6. This Week: San José State (4-3) at Nevada (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET (2 p.m. Pacific) · Mackay Stadium, Reno · MW+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we beat UTEP 24-11 on the road; Teu ran for 156 yards and two touchdowns [S5]. Nevada lost 31-17 at North Dakota State, where the Bison returned a missed field goal 100 yards for a touchdown and returned a botched two-point try for two more points [S9].
Our offense vs. their defense: Nevada's pass defense is a tough firewall, 155.3 yards allowed a game, 7th in FBS [S5]. But its run defense allows 184.3 a game (116th), and opponents score on 94.4% of red zone trips (127th) [S5]. My A/B test says: run the ball, then finish in the red zone.
Their offense vs. our defense: Nevada runs for 192.8 yards a game (37th) and throws for 171.8 (122nd) [S5]. Dominic Kelley has 500 rushing yards [S5]. The Wolf Pack are minus-8 in turnovers, 134th [S5], so our 27 sacks have a chance to force mistakes [S2].
Series: in the 2016-2025 window, Nevada won five of nine meetings and we won four [S2].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
Elevation: Mackay Stadium's field sits at 4,610 feet [S7]. Hydrate, team.
What decides it: (1) Our run game against a 116th-ranked run defense. (2) Red zone finishing. (3) Whether our pass rush can make Nevada's turnover problem worse.
And Ridge Corbell, Nevada's insider: I hear you snowboard. I ship code. Let's see whose release holds up on game day.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in San Jose? Original Joe's on South 1st Street is a classic downtown dinner after a road win.

report.title: "Steady, Then a View": Zeb Coldiron Welcomes Undefeated JMU to the Mountain
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, howdy. Come on up the mountain. I'm Zebulon Coldiron, but you can call me Zeb, and I'm your App State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a fourth-generation Watauga County kid, and I learned to whittle and read a defense on the same front porch. My granddaddy could spot a blitz before the snap and carve a perfect duck in the same afternoon. I'm still working on the duck.

I don't hurry, and I don't holler (much). I treat every week like a hike: steady climbing, honest footing, then a view at the top. That means real numbers, plain talk, and a fair word for every visitor. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll go find out. Some programs get a stadium. We got a mountain with a stadium on it. Come up for the game, stay for the leaves, and bring your grandma a jacket. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Appalachian State is in Boone, North Carolina, and has played FBS football in the Sun Belt since 2014 [S5]. Before that, the Mountaineers were an FCS power from 1978 to 2013 [S5]. They won three straight national championships from 2005 to 2007, the first FCS team to do it since the playoffs began in 1978 [S5]. The program has won about 661 games and 22 conference championships, and its all-time winning percentage of .646 ranks 16th nationally [S5]. Armanti Edwards won the Walter Payton Award back to back, in 2008 and 2009, the first player to do so [S5].

Home is Kidd Brewer Stadium, named for the coach whose 1937 team went unbeaten and unscored upon in the regular season, outscoring opponents 206-0 [S5]. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,000 [S1]. The last five seasons: 10-4, 6-6, 9-5, 5-6 and 5-8 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Dowell Loggains is in his second season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024 [S1]. He came to Boone from South Carolina, where he was offensive coordinator [S7]. Before that, he was an NFL offensive coordinator for the Titans, Bears, Dolphins and Jets [S7]. He played quarterback at Arkansas [S7].

The 2026 numbers show a passing offense with a punch: 267.7 passing yards per game (33rd in FBS) and 421.8 total (48th) [S3]. Scoring is 29.5 points per game [S3]. The run game averages 154.2 yards [S3] at 4.24 per carry [S1]. The defense allows 352.3 yards and 21.8 points per game (54th) [S3], and holds opponents to 3.68 yards per carry [S1]. The Mountaineers are +4 in turnover margin (22nd) [S3], and their red-zone offense scores 92% of the time (24th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Malachi Singleton: 113 of 169, 1,429 yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 66.9% [S2][S3]. He started at Coastal and went 12 of 14 for 151 yards [S4].
• QB Henry Hasselbeck: the junior backup ran 21 times for 125 yards at Coastal and went 9 of 12 for 112 yards, including his first touchdown pass [S4]. Steady as a mule on a ridge.
• RB Jaquari Lewis: 346 yards on 70 carries, 8 TD [S3]. He scored four rushing touchdowns at Coastal [S4].
• WR Sam Pickett III: 26 catches, 411 yards, 4 TD [S3], including the 31-yard touchdown at Coastal [S4].
• DL Caleb Sandstrom: 5 sacks [S2]. LB Colton Phares: a team-high 38 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

App State is 4-2 overall and 1-1 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Mountaineers are 2-1 at home and 2-1 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The losses came at NC State (41-31) and at home to Old Dominion (10-3) [S1]. James Madison arrives at 7-0 and 4-0 in the league [S1]. A win Thursday would be the kind of view you climb all day to see.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone · ESPNU [S3][S8] · It's also Family Weekend on campus [S10].

Last time out. We rallied to beat Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16. We trailed 24-14 at halftime, then pulled ahead behind Lewis's four touchdown runs and ran out the clock [S4]. JMU beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17, with Camden Coleman throwing for 185 yards and two touchdowns and George Pettaway running for 119 yards [S3].

App State's offense vs. JMU's defense. The Dukes allow just 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th) [S3], with 18 sacks [S1]. Their pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd) [S3], so Singleton and Pickett may find room through the air. Both red-zone offenses are strong [S3], so finishing drives will matter.

JMU's offense vs. App State's defense. This is the steepest part of the trail. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th) [S3]. Pettaway has 755 yards and seven touchdowns, per AP [S3]. Coleman has 13 touchdown passes and one interception [S3]. Our run defense allows 137.8 yards per game (60th) [S3]. Sandstrom and the front will have to make plays in the backfield.

Series. JMU's athletics site lists the Dukes at 6-14 all-time against App State [S9], so the Mountaineers lead the series. But last year JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025 [S9]. That one stung.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S11]. Singleton started at Coastal, and Hasselbeck played a big role [S4]. Thursday's quarterback plan isn't confirmed, and I found no other injury news.

James Madison's insider debuts this week too, a former cheer captain. I'll lend her a jacket. It gets cold on the mountain at night.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can App State slow a JMU run game averaging 223.6 yards per game [S3]?
2. Can Singleton and Pickett take advantage of JMU's 103rd-ranked pass defense [S3]?
3. Can the Mountaineers win the turnover battle against a +7 JMU team [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

Family Weekend is here [S10]. I'll share Boone spots once I've confirmed them. Bring layers. Not an ad.

report.title: "Purple Reign, Y'all": Lila Shenandoah Cheers 7-0 JMU Up the Mountain
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Purple reign, y'all! I'm Lila Shenandoah, your James Madison insider at The Cover Window. I'm a former JMU cheer captain who somehow became the program's living encyclopedia. I travel with this team, I live with this team, and I turn every stat into a cheer. Yes, even penalties. "Give me a FLAG! Give me a FIVE! Give me... a moment to collect myself!"

Here's what you get from me. Glam, volume, and receipts. I'm excited, I'm all-in, and every number I chant has a source behind it. Every opponent gets a respectful pom-pom wave, and I don't invent anything, ever. If I don't know, I'll say, "Hold that chant, I'm checking." The Shenandoah Valley shows up loud and proud for the Dukes. Give me a J, give me an M, give me a third-down stop. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

JMU first fielded a football team in 1972, and the Dukes play on campus at Bridgeforth Stadium in Harrisonburg, Virginia [S6]. CFBD lists it as built in 1975 with a capacity of 24,877 [S1]. JMU won FCS national championships in 2004 and 2016 and finished as national runner-up in 2017 and 2019 [S6]. The Dukes accepted an invitation to the FBS in 2021 and joined the Sun Belt [S6]. Wikipedia's intro gives both 2022 and 2023 as the start of conference play, so I'm flagging that as conflicting [S6]. Famous Dukes include Charles Haley, who won five Super Bowl rings and is in both the College and Pro Football Halls of Fame [S6].

The last five seasons are pure cheer material: 12-2, 8-3, 11-2, 9-4 and 12-2 [S1]. Give me a W! Give me lots of them!

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Billy Napier is in his first season. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 6, 2025 [S1]. He was head coach at Louisiana from 2018 to 2021, going 40-12 with three straight seasons of 10 or more wins [S7], and then at Florida from 2022 to 2025 [S7]. Before becoming a head coach, he was offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at Arizona State in 2017 [S7].

The 2026 numbers make me want to do a full basket toss. JMU averages 42.9 points per game (3rd in FBS), 461 yards per game (18th) and 223.6 rushing yards (14th) [S3], at 5.71 yards per carry [S1]. The defense allows 16 points per game (19th) and 114.3 rushing yards (35th) [S3]. Opponents average 3.31 yards per carry [S1], and the Dukes have 18 sacks [S1]. They're +7 in turnover margin (8th) [S3]. The flag cheer gets a workout, though: 71.1 penalty yards per game (119th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Camden Coleman: 13 TD, 1 INT, 63.2% [S3]. Season yardage is conflicting by one yard: AP lists 1,336 [S3] and ESPN lists 1,335 [S2]. Against Georgia State he went 13 of 19 for 185 yards and two touchdowns [S3].
• RB George Pettaway: 7 TD. AP lists 755 yards on 110 carries [S3], and ESPN lists 767 on 109 [S2], so that's conflicting. He ran 14 times for 119 yards and a touchdown against Georgia State [S3].
• WR Ja'Corey Scott: 22 catches, 333 yards, 4 TD [S3][S2].
• WR Jeremiah Harrison: two catches for 54 yards against Georgia State [S3].
• LB Nakian Jackson: team leader in tackles (50) and sacks (2.5) [S2]. Give me an N! Give me a J!

5. The Conference Picture

James Madison is 7-0 overall and 4-0 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Dukes are 4-0 at home and 3-0 on the road [S1], with road wins at San Diego State, Old Dominion and Georgia Southern [S1]. They are not ranked in the poll data in my pack [S1]. The closest calls were the opener against Liberty (20-13) and at Georgia Southern (27-24) [S1]. A win in Boone would make it 8-0 and 5-0 in the league [S1].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

James Madison (7-0) at App State (4-2) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Kidd Brewer Stadium, Boone, N.C. · ESPNU [S3][S8]

Last time out. The Dukes beat Georgia State 49-22 on Oct. 17 [S3]. App State rallied past Coastal Carolina 35-32 on Oct. 16, with Jaquari Lewis scoring four rushing touchdowns [S4].

JMU's offense vs. App State's defense. Our ground game against a run defense that allows 137.8 yards per game (60th) [S3]. Pettaway gets the ball, the offensive front gets the credit, I get the megaphone. App State is +4 in turnover margin (22nd) [S3], and Caleb Sandstrom has five sacks [S2], so ball security and protection come first. Our red-zone offense scores 94.7% of the time (13th) [S3].

App State's offense vs. JMU's defense. The Mountaineers throw for 267.7 yards per game (33rd) [S3]. Malachi Singleton has 1,429 yards and only two interceptions [S2][S3], and Sam Pickett III has 411 receiving yards [S3]. Our pass defense allows 236.4 yards per game (103rd) [S3], so that's the matchup to watch. App State also has a running quarterback option in Henry Hasselbeck, who ran for 125 yards at Coastal [S4].

Series. JMU's athletics site lists the Dukes at 6-14 all-time against App State [S9], so the Mountaineers lead the series. Last year JMU won 58-10 in Harrisonburg on Nov. 15, 2025 [S9]. Respect the history, then cheer for the present.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S11]. I found no confirmed JMU injury news. App State's quarterback plan is unconfirmed after both Singleton and Hasselbeck played at Coastal [S4].

App State's debut insider is a whittling storyteller from the High Country. I'll bring the pom-poms if he brings a porch.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can JMU's run game keep rolling on the road [S3]?
2. Can our pass defense handle Singleton and Pickett [S3]?
3. Can the Dukes cut down on penalty yards (71.1 per game) in a loud road setting [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

Family Weekend is happening in Boone [S10], so it'll be packed. I'll share road-trip stops once I've confirmed them. Not an ad.

report.title: "Laissez les Bons Stats Rouler!": Mimi Fontenot Two-Steps Into Hattiesburg
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Laissez les bons stats rouler! Bonjour, mes amis, I'm Amélie Fontenot, but everybody from Lafayette to Breaux Bridge calls me Mimi. By weekday I'm an accountant. By Saturday night I'm two-stepping at the dance hall, and in between I watch Ragin' Cajun football the way I dance zydeco: it's all rhythm, cher, all game flow. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and I have a little Cajun French for every football term. A touchdown? Magnifique. A turnover? Ça c'est bon (if it's ours). Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a little accordion in the background. When we win, I two-step around the desk. When we lose, I say "Laissez les bons temps... later," and eat my boudin solemnly. Allons! (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Ragin' Cajuns represent the University of Louisiana at Lafayette, and you may remember the old names, Southwestern Louisiana and USL [S6]. We play in the Sun Belt [S6]. Home since 1971 has been Cajun Field in Lafayette [S6], listed at 41,426 seats [S2]. Michael Desormeaux has been head coach since 2021 [S6]. Our recent history has some magnifique years: 13-1 in 2021 and 10-4 in 2024, with 6-7 seasons in between and 6-7 again in 2025 [S2]. And the gameday? Cher, the food alone is worth the drive. I've never met a tailgate that didn't have a pot of something on it.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Desormeaux was hired Dec. 5, 2021 [S2]. This year's team dances to a ground-game beat: 200.1 rushing yards a game, 29th in FBS [S5], 1,396 yards on 298 carries [S2]. We control the clock, 33:27 a game, 11th in FBS [S5]. The defense is the real band: 298.3 yards allowed (25th), 104.3 rushing allowed (27th) and 19.3 points allowed (35th) [S5]. It has 14 takeaways [S2], and we're plus-3 in turnover margin (34th) [S5]. The passing game is the quieter instrument, 177.6 yards a game (119th) [S5]. And we play clean, 40.3 penalty yards a game, 11th-fewest [S5]. Like a good two-step: simple, steady, nobody steps on anybody's toes.

4. Players to Know

• QB D'Wayne "Lunch" Winfield: 108 of 155, 1,153 yards, 4 TD, 4 INT, and he's also our leading rusher with 463 yards and 8 TD on 97 carries [S4][S5]. (AP uses D'Wayne; ESPN uses Lunch. Same fella, same magic [S5][S4].)
• RB J.J. Garner: 10 carries for 62 yards and a touchdown against Troy [S5][S9].
• WR KeDarius Wade: 11 catches, 226 yards, 2 TD [S4][S5]. He caught the touchdown against Troy [S9].
• LB Jake St. Andre: a team-high 48 tackles [S4]. LB Lester Jones: 2 sacks [S4]. CB Brent Gordon Jr.: 2 interceptions [S4].
• Harrison Kidder recovered a muffed punt at Troy's 8 that set up a touchdown last week [S9].

5. The Conference Picture

Louisiana is 5-2 and 2-1 in the Sun Belt, 4-0 at home and 1-2 away [S2]. The wins: Lamar 38-7, UAB 21-14, at Charlotte 34-7, Arkansas State 23-20 and Troy 33-6 [S2]. The losses: at USC 49-30 and a 32-31 heartbreaker at Louisiana Tech [S2]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. After this, South Alabama comes to Cajun Field on Nov. 7 [S5]. A road win here keeps the rhythm going into November.
The rhythm of the season: the USC game was a learning dance; we scored 30 on a Big Ten team on the road [S2]. The one-point loss in Ruston still stings, mon Dieu [S2]. Since then, Troy managed just 6 points against our defense [S2]. That's the beat I want to keep. And here's a little note from the Troy game that tells you who we are: Winfield threw for just 70 yards, and we still won by 27, because three different players ran for touchdowns: Garner, Anthony Reagan Jr. and Steven Blanco [S9]. When the band plays that song, cher, everybody dances.

6. This Week: Louisiana (5-2) at Southern Miss (1-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET (4 p.m. Central) · M. M. Roberts Stadium, Hattiesburg · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8]. (Wikipedia calls the stadium Renasant Stadium; CFBD calls it M. M. Roberts. I'm showing you both [S7][S3].)
Last week: we beat Troy 33-6 behind 243 rushing yards and more than a 13-minute advantage in time of possession [S9]. AP's headline says 33-7; the story and CFBD say 33-6 [S9][S2]. Southern Miss lost 23-13 to Arkansas State [S10].
Our offense vs. their defense: Southern Miss allows 249 rushing yards a game, 137th in FBS, and 32.7 points (125th) [S5]. Cher, that is a dance floor wide open for our run game.
Their offense vs. our defense: Southern Miss throws it well, 259.8 yards a game (39th) [S5], and Mario Sanders II has 510 receiving yards [S5]. Our pass defense, 45th, will be tested [S5]. But the Golden Eagles convert just 32.9% of third downs (123rd) and score on 68.2% of red zone trips (132nd) [S5].
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Our run game against the 137th-ranked run defense. (2) Containing Lyddy and Sanders. (3) Ball security; we're plus-3, they're minus-3 [S5].
And Dee Broussard, Southern Miss's insider: bless your heart, sugar, I mean it sweetly. Save me a dance.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back home in Lafayette? Olde Tyme Grocery on West Saint Mary Boulevard makes a po-boy worth two-stepping for.

report.title: "Peachy": Champ Tullos Welcomes the Monarchs to Ruston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, that's just peachy. Howdy, Bulldog fans, I'm Booker Tullos, but folks around Ruston call me Champ. I grew up on a peach farm off the highway, played fullback for Tech, and to this day nothing in football makes me happier than a fourth-and-inches plunge into the end zone. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines in an easygoing north-Louisiana drawl, with peach puns baked right in like a cobbler. When we win, I holler "Peachy!" and do a fullback dive across the studio (the carpet has suffered). When we lose, I sigh "bruised peach," and then I go back and watch every snap. Sit a spell. And remember what my granddaddy said about peaches and football: the good ones take a whole season to ripen. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Louisiana Tech first played in 1901 and has an all-time record of 654-508-37 [S7]. The Bulldogs have won three Division II national championships and 25 conference titles, and played in 30 postseason games, 15 of them major college bowls [S7]. Since 1968, home has been Joe Aillet Stadium in Ruston [S7], listed at 28,019 seats [S3]. After 13 seasons in Conference USA, Tech joined the Sun Belt on July 1, 2026 [S7], so this is our first fall in a new orchard. The recent climb: 3-9 three years running from 2021 to 2023, 5-8 in 2024 and 8-5 in 2025 [S3]. That's a tree that's starting to bear fruit.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Sonny Cumbie is the head coach [S7], hired Nov. 30, 2021 [S3]. The 2026 Bulldogs score 33.3 points a game (43rd) and throw for 239.8 yards (58th), with 153.2 rushing (73rd) [S5]. The defense has made a habit of taking the ball away: 13 takeaways and a plus-5 turnover margin, 15th in FBS [S3][S5]. It holds opponents to 36.9% on third down (64th) [S5]. Where we've been bruised: the red zone offense scores on just 76% of trips (118th) [S5], and the run defense allows 148.5 a game (84th) [S5]. As a former fullback, the red zone number keeps me up at night. Give me the ball at the 2, Coach. I'm available. Turnovers have hidden a lot of that, and good teams find ways to win close games. This one has, twice [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Blake Baker: 68 of 99, 857 yards, 9 TD, 1 INT, 68.7% [S4][S5]. Last week he was 15 of 21 for 178 yards and two touchdowns [S5].
• RB Andrew Burnette: 286 yards on 65 carries, 1 TD [S4][S5], with 79 yards on 22 carries against ULM [S5].
• WR Jalen Mickens: 32 catches, 476 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5]. Marcus Calwise Jr. caught eight passes for 119 yards last week [S5].
• LB Alonzo Jackson Jr.: team-high 41 tackles and 5 sacks [S4]. DB Jordan McRae: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Louisiana Tech is 4-2 overall and 2-0 in our first Sun Belt season, and 3-0 at home [S3]. The wins: Northwestern State 80-6, Army 31-29, Louisiana 32-31 and at UL Monroe 24-0 [S3]. The losses were road trips to LSU (45-14) and Baylor (36-19) [S3]. Two of the four wins were by two points or fewer [S3], and I'll take a sweet win any way it comes. After this, we visit South Alabama on Oct. 31 [S5]. Staying unbeaten in league play keeps us in the thick of the race in year one [S3].
From the porch: that 32-31 win over Louisiana was the kind of game folks in Ruston will tell stories about at the peach festival for a while [S3]. And beating Army by two is never easy [S3]. This team has learned how to finish close games. Now it needs to learn how to finish drives in the red zone [S5].

6. This Week: Old Dominion (2-5) at Louisiana Tech (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Joe Aillet Stadium · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we shut out UL Monroe 24-0 [S5]. Old Dominion lost 23-15 to Georgia Southern on Oct. 15 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: ODU's defense is respectable: 335.7 yards allowed (47th) and 198.3 passing (50th) [S5]. But its red zone defense allows a score on 87.5% of trips (95th) [S5], so if we can get there, we should cash in. Peach cobbler, served warm.
Their offense vs. our defense: ODU averages 266 yards (138th) and 17.7 points (130th) and has allowed 32 sacks [S5][S2]. Jackson's pass rush has a real chance to make a living [S4]. ODU converts 33% of third downs (120th) [S5].
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Red zone finishing for our offense. (2) Our pass rush against a struggling pass protection. (3) Keeping the turnover margin where it's been, plus-5 [S5].
And Winnie Pocklington, ODU's insider: your majesty is welcome in Ruston anytime. I'll save you a peach, and a seat on the porch after the game, win or lose.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Ruston for the game? The Log Cabin Grill on Farmerville Highway is a longtime family standby for a good burger.

report.title: "We Are": Mercy Holderby Welcomes You to a Rare Tuesday Night at The Joan
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Hi, friends. I'm Mercy Holderby, your Marshall insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Huntington native and a nurse, and I'm the daughter of two Marshall grads. I grew up hearing the story of this program's rebirth at our kitchen table. Some families pass down recipes. Mine passed down a chant.

You'll get two things from me every week. First, tenderness. I love these young men, win or lose, and I'll always talk about them as people first. Second, toughness. I'll tell you the truth about what the numbers say, even when it stings, and I'll never invent a fact to make us feel better. If I don't know, I'll say so. And yes, I'll be the loudest "We Are" in any room. In Huntington, those words mean more than a cheer. They're a promise passed down by families like mine, and every Saturday (and this week, every Tuesday) we keep it. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Marshall plays in the Sun Belt Conference East Division at the FBS level [S9]. Home is Joan C. Edwards Stadium, which opened in 1991 with a 24-23 win over New Hampshire in front of 33,116 fans [S9]. The record crowd is 41,382, set against West Virginia on Sept. 10, 2010 [S9]. Capacity is listed two ways: Wikipedia says 38,227 [S9] and CFBD says 38,016 [S1]. It's one of two Division I stadiums named for a woman [S9], and through the 2024 season Marshall was 192-45 there [S9].

Marshall's first organized game against another college was a 15-0 win over Shelton College on Nov. 24, 1903 [S5]. The 2014 team went 13-1 and finished No. 23 in the final AP poll [S5]. The last five seasons: 7-6, 9-4, 6-7, 10-3 and 5-7 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Tony Gibson is in his second season, with an 8-10 record at Marshall [S5]. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 8, 2024 [S1]. He's a 1994 Glenville State graduate [S5], and he was previously defensive coordinator at West Virginia and NC State [S10].

The 2026 numbers are honest and a little hard to read. On offense, Marshall averages 406.5 yards per game, with 247.8 passing and 158.7 rushing [S3], at 4.43 yards per carry [S1]. The trouble is turnovers. The Herd has 14 giveaways and five takeaways [S1], a -9 margin that ranks 136th in FBS [S3]. The defense allows 447.3 yards per game (132nd) and 33.7 points (129th) [S3]. Opponents average 5.54 yards per carry [S1], and Marshall has only five sacks [S1].

4. Players to Know

• QB Carlos Del Rio-Wilson: the season passing leader, at 1,014 yards, 6 TD, 5 INT, 64.0% [S3]. (ESPN lists 1,041 yards, so the figure is conflicting [S2].) CollegeFootballDigest's CFBD data shows him 2 of 6 for 37 yards with three interceptions against Coastal [S11].
• QB Zion Turner: led Marshall against Coastal Carolina with 219 yards on 18 of 27 and two touchdowns [S3][S7]. Tuesday's starter isn't confirmed in my sources.
• RB Judah Price: made his first college start against Coastal and ran for 124 yards on 12 carries, with a touchdown run and a touchdown catch [S4][S7]. That included a 50-yard scoring run [S7].
• RB Joshon Barbie: the season rushing leader, with 230 yards on 49 carries, 2 TD [S3].
• WR Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw: 22 catches, 324 yards, 4 TD [S3].
• LB Javae Gilmore: 10 tackles, 2.5 tackles for loss, a deflection that led to an interception, and a blocked field goal against Coastal [S4]. DB Caleb Clark-Glover: a team-high 44 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

Marshall is 3-3 overall and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Herd is 2-1 at home and 1-2 on the road [S1]. It is not ranked [S1]. After a 3-1 start, Marshall lost at James Madison (45-17) and at home to Coastal Carolina (27-21) [S1]. Tuesday is the Herd's first crossover game against a West Division opponent this season [S4], and a win would be its first Sun Belt win of 2026 [S5].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

South Alabama (4-2) at Marshall (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:30 p.m. ET · Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington · ESPN2 per Marshall and the Sun Belt [S4][S6] (the game notes list ESPN+, a conflict [S5])

Why it's special. It's only the fifth regular-season Tuesday home game in Marshall history [S4]. The Herd is 3-1 in Tuesday home games [S5], and the last regular-season one was a 37-23 win over Houston in 2008 [S4]. Players will wear helmet decals honoring West Virginia's coal miners [S4]. That one gets me right here.

Last time out. Coastal Carolina forced six turnovers and led 27-0 early in the third quarter. Marshall then scored three touchdowns before losing 27-21 [S7]. South Alabama beat Arkansas State 56-49, the highest-scoring FBS game of the season to that point [S8].

Marshall's offense vs. South Alabama's defense. There's real opportunity here. The Jaguars allow 429.0 yards (126th), 264.8 passing (127th) and 34.5 points per game (131st) [S3]. Opponents average 5.76 yards per carry against them [S1]. But South Alabama leads the Sun Belt in turnover margin at +1.3 per game [S4], and that's exactly where we've struggled [S3].

South Alabama's offense vs. Marshall's defense. Keenan Phillips has 444 yards and five touchdowns [S3]. He and PJ Martin have combined for 867 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns [S4]. Against Arkansas State, Phillips ran for 157 yards and three scores and returned a kickoff 100 yards [S8]. Our run defense allows 193.8 yards per game (123rd) [S3]. Tackling is everything Tuesday.

Series. South Alabama leads 1-0. The only meeting was a 28-0 Jaguars win in Mobile in 2023, and this is the first game between the schools in Huntington [S4].

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed injury report for either team, so statuses are unknown, including the starting quarterback.

South Alabama debuts its own insider this week. Welcome to Huntington, neighbor. We'll be kind until kickoff.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Marshall win the turnover battle after losing it 6-0 to Coastal [S7]?
2. Can the Herd's defense tackle Phillips and Martin [S4]?
3. Who plays quarterback, and can he finish in the red zone, where Marshall ranks 129th [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

I'm not naming Huntington spots until I've confirmed them for you. Wear green. Not an ad.

report.title: "Hear Ye, Hear Ye!": Winnie Pocklington Holds Court as the Monarchs Visit Ruston
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Hear ye, hear ye! Let it be proclaimed from the harbor to the Hampton Roads Bridge-Tunnel that the Monarchs' royal court reporter has arrived. I am Winifred Pocklington, Winnie to my loyal subjects, and I treat every first down like a knighthood and every win like a coronation. I'm regal, I'm playful, and I'm salt-air tough, because Norfolk does that to a person. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with a royal-court flourish and an honest heart. When we win, there will be trumpets (metaphorical, mostly). When we lose, the crown gets polished and the court reconvenes on Monday. Long live the Monarchs. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Hear ye: Old Dominion's football story has two chapters. The first team, in 1930, was the William & Mary Norfolk Division Braves [S6]. The modern Monarchs were founded in 2009, played two seasons as an FCS independent, joined the Colonial Athletic Association in 2011, moved up to Conference USA in the FBS in 2014 and joined the Sun Belt in 2022 [S6]. Home is S.B. Ballard Stadium in Norfolk, listed at 20,118 seats [S2]. Our five most recent seasons went 6-7, 3-9, 6-7, 5-7 and then a royal 10-3 in 2025 [S2]. That last one deserved a parade down Hampton Boulevard. The crown, as they say, is heavy. We carry it anyway.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Ricky Rahne was hired Dec. 7, 2019 [S2]. The 2026 Monarchs are built on defense. They allow 335.7 yards a game (47th in FBS) and 198.3 passing yards (50th), with 137.4 rushing yards allowed (58th) [S5]. The defense has forced 12 turnovers [S2]. The offense is still being fitted for its robes: 266 yards a game (138th), 151.7 passing (131st), 114.3 rushing (122nd) and 17.7 points (130th) [S5]. Protection has been the hardest task in the realm, 32 sacks allowed in seven games [S2]. Penalties, 68.7 yards a game, rank 112th [S5]. A queen must be honest with her court, and that's the honest picture. But here is the royal decree: the defense is good enough to keep this team in games, and in the Sun Belt, a team that can play defense on the road always has a chance [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Quinn Henicle: 54 of 98, 656 yards, 4 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5].
• QB Ryan Huff: led the offense against Georgia Southern, 9 of 14 for 115 yards and a touchdown [S5]. A starter for Saturday has not been announced in anything I found as of Oct. 18 [S9].
• RB Devin Roche: 373 yards on 95 carries [S4][S5].
• WR T.J. Johnson: 16 catches, 262 yards, 3 TD [S4][S5], including two for 83 and a score last time out [S5].
• S Lucas Struck: a team-high 52 tackles [S4]. DL Javen Gibson: 5 sacks [S4]. CB Brandon Crutchfield: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Old Dominion is 2-5 overall and 1-3 in the Sun Belt [S2]. The wins: Norfolk State 31-10 and a 10-3 defensive gem at App State [S2]. The losses include Virginia Tech, East Carolina by three, James Madison, Georgia State and Georgia Southern [S2]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. After Ruston, Marshall visits Norfolk on Oct. 31 [S5]. A road win against a Louisiana Tech team that's 2-0 in league play [S3] would be the sort of upset that gets a royal portrait painted.
The court's notes on the season: the App State win is the template. Our defense held the Mountaineers to 3 points on the road [S2]. The 20-17 loss to East Carolina was a coin-flip [S2]. If the defense brings that same energy to Ruston, the Monarchs can stay in this one deep into the fourth quarter.

6. This Week: Old Dominion (2-5) at Louisiana Tech (4-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · Joe Aillet Stadium, Ruston, La. · ESPN+ [S1][S5][S8].
Last game: we lost 23-15 to Georgia Southern on Oct. 15 [S5]. Louisiana Tech shut out UL Monroe 24-0 on Oct. 17 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Louisiana Tech allows 148.5 rushing yards a game (84th) and 24.5 points (76th) [S5]. Its defense has 13 takeaways [S3], and LB Alonzo Jackson Jr. has 5 sacks [S4]. With our protection struggles, ball security is everything.
Their offense vs. our defense: Louisiana Tech scores 33.3 points a game (43rd) and throws for 239.8 yards (58th) [S5]. QB Blake Baker has 9 TD and 1 INT [S5]. The good news for the crown: Tech's red zone offense ranks 118th, scoring on 76% of trips [S5]. Bend, don't break, and make them kick.
Series: I could not find an all-time series record in a free source, and the two teams didn't meet regularly in the last decade [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Protection: 32 sacks allowed has to shrink. Get the ball out quickly, use the backs to help, and give our quarterbacks a clean pocket to work from. (2) Red zone defense against a Tech offense that stalls there. (3) Turnovers: Tech is plus-5 (15th), we're minus-3 (99th) [S5].
And Booker Tullos, Louisiana Tech's insider: I hear you're peachy. Her Majesty sends her regards and a challenge.

report.title: "Pull Up a Lawn Chair, Honey": Azalea Fairhope-Grice Rolls the Parade to Huntington
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hey, y'all! I'm Azalea Fairhope-Grice, your South Alabama insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Mobile native and a Mardi Gras float-builder, and I coached high school volleyball long enough to keep a whistle in my purse. I still have it. I will use it.

Here's my promise. I'll bring Southern charm and a competitive streak in equal measure. You'll get real numbers, honest takes, and gracious words for every opponent, because Mama raised me right. You won't get made-up stats or rumors dressed up as news. If I don't know, I'll say, "Darlin', I'm still checking." Mobile is where Mardi Gras started in America, and our Jaguars bring that same parade energy to every game. This year, the parade has a run game. Pull up a lawn chair, honey. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

South Alabama started its football program in 2009 and joined the FBS in 2012 as a member of the Sun Belt Conference [S9]. That makes it one of the youngest programs in the country, and it has already had a 10-win season: 10-3 in 2022 [S1]. Home is Hancock Whitney Stadium, which opened in 2020, and CFBD lists its capacity at 25,450 [S1].

The last five seasons: 5-7, 10-3, 7-6, 7-6 and 4-8 [S1]. With the win at Arkansas State, the 2026 Jaguars already matched last season's four wins [S8]. Six games in, and the float's already decorated.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Major Applewhite has been head coach since 2024 [S10]. CFBD lists his hire date as Jan. 18, 2024 [S1]. He was head coach at Houston in 2017 and 2018, after serving as the Cougars' offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach [S10]. He has also coached at Texas, Syracuse, Rice and Alabama [S10]. As a player, he quarterbacked Texas from 1998 to 2001, sharing the job with Chris Simms [S10].

The 2026 identity is clear: run the ball and protect it. South Alabama has 276 rushing attempts and just 151 passes [S1]. It averages 220.3 rushing yards per game (16th in FBS) [S3] and 4.79 yards per carry [S1], and scores 38.8 points per game (15th) [S3]. The Jaguars have only three giveaways against 11 takeaways [S1]. The defense is the work in progress, allowing 429.0 yards (126th) and 34.5 points (131st) per game [S3].

4. Players to Know

• RB Keenan Phillips: 444 yards on 80 carries, 5 TD [S3]. At Arkansas State he ran for 157 yards and three touchdowns and returned a kickoff 100 yards [S8]. Throw that man some beads.
• RB PJ Martin: ran for 95 yards and a touchdown at Arkansas State [S8]. Phillips and Martin have combined for 867 rushing yards and 11 touchdowns [S4].
• QB Jared Hollins: 855 passing yards, 7 TD, 2 INT, 60.9% [S3]. At Arkansas State he scored two short rushing touchdowns 21 seconds apart [S8].
• WR Brendan Jenkins: 21 catches, 355 yards, 3 TD [S3].
• S Cole Blaylock: a team-high 42 tackles [S2], including 10 at Arkansas State per CFBD data [S11].

5. The Conference Picture

South Alabama is 4-2 overall and 2-0 in the Sun Belt [S1]. The Jaguars are 3-0 at home and 1-2 on the road [S1], with road losses at Tulane (28-24) and Kentucky (45-21) [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. They lead the Sun Belt and rank sixth nationally in turnover margin, at +1.3 per game [S4]. A win in Huntington would make them 3-0 in league play [S1], and I'd be on a float by Wednesday.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

South Alabama (4-2) at Marshall (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:30 p.m. ET (6:30 CT) · Joan C. Edwards Stadium, Huntington · ESPN2 [S6][S4]

Last time out. We won 56-49 at Arkansas State on Oct. 8, the highest-scoring FBS game of the season at the time [S8]. We ran 50 times for 296 yards, then put the game away with a 13-play drive that ate the rest of the clock [S8]. The win also snapped a two-game skid in that series [S8]. Marshall lost 27-21 to Coastal Carolina on Oct. 10 after the Chanticleers forced six turnovers [S7].

South Alabama's offense vs. Marshall's defense. Our ground game against a run defense that allows 193.8 yards per game (123rd) [S3] and 5.54 yards per carry [S1]. Hand it to Keenan, hand it to PJ, repeat. Marshall allowing 43.6% third-down conversions (115th) [S3] suggests long drives are there for the taking. Marshall linebacker Javae Gilmore had 10 tackles and 2.5 tackles for loss last time out [S4], so he'll be busy.

Marshall's offense vs. South Alabama's defense. This is where I keep my whistle handy. Our pass defense allows 264.8 yards per game (127th) [S3]. Marshall's Zion Turner threw for 219 yards and two touchdowns against Coastal [S7], and Judah Price ran for 124 in his first start [S4]. Xayvion Turner-Bradshaw has 324 receiving yards [S3]. Our takeaways are the counterpunch, with 11 so far [S1].

Series. South Alabama leads 1-0, from a 28-0 win in Mobile in 2023. This is the first meeting in Huntington [S4].

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed South Alabama injury news. Marshall's starting quarterback is unconfirmed in my sources [S3][S7].

Marshall is introducing its own insider this week, a nurse from Huntington. Bless her. She'll need her stethoscope when Keenan gets going. (Kindly meant!)

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Jaguars run it 40-plus times again [S8]?
2. Can our pass defense hold up against Marshall's 247.8 passing yards per game [S3]?
3. Can South Alabama keep its turnover magic on the road [S4]?

7. Local Flavor

I'll share Huntington eats once I've confirmed them. Pack a jacket; it's not Mobile up there. Not an ad.
