report.title: "To the Top, Sugar": Dee Broussard Welcomes the Cajuns to Hattiesburg
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

To the top, sugar! Hey, y'all, I'm Delphine Broussard, but please call me Dee. I was sorority president at Southern Miss, and these days I scout football with the same eye I used to plan a formal: I notice everything, I forget nothing, and I say it all with a smile. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, served with Southern sweetness and a little spice. My one weakness is the gentle Southern burn. I can't help it. When we win, I'll point skyward and holler "To the top, y'all!" When we lose, I'll sigh "Bless it," fix my pearls and get right back to work. Pull up a rocker. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Southern Miss plays in Hattiesburg and competes in the Sun Belt [S7]. Our home stadium has two names depending on who you ask: Wikipedia lists Renasant Stadium, and CFBD lists M. M. Roberts Stadium, opened in 1932 with 36,000 seats [S7][S3]. Either way, sugar, it's ours, and it's loud. The last five seasons have been a roller coaster: 3-9 in 2021, 7-6 in 2022, 3-9, then a hard 1-11 in 2024 and a lovely 7-6 bounce back in 2025 [S3]. That 2025 team proved this program can climb fast, and climbing is what we do. To the top.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Blake Anderson is in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 11, 2025 [S3]. The 2026 Golden Eagles throw it well: 259.8 passing yards a game, 39th in FBS, and 394.3 total yards (65th) [S5]. The run game is lighter, 134.5 a game (103rd) [S5]. Bless it, the defense has had a hard time: 249 rushing yards allowed a game (137th) and 32.7 points (125th) [S5]. Here's a sweet spot, though: our pass defense allows just 193.2 yards a game, 44th in FBS [S5]. And the team has 14 sacks [S3]. The fixes we need are third downs (32.9%, 123rd), red zone offense (68.2%, 132nd) and turnovers (minus-3) [S5].

4. Players to Know

• QB Landry Lyddy: 80 of 132, 1,032 yards, 7 TD, 4 INT [S4]. (AP's preview lists 1,026 yards; feeds update at different times [S5].)
• RB Steven Robinson: 432 yards on 99 carries, 5 TD [S4][S5]. He ran for 84 yards and a touchdown last week [S5].
• WR Mario Sanders II: 34 catches for 492 yards and 5 TD per ESPN, 510 yards per AP [S4][S5]. He had six catches for 106 yards against Arkansas State [S5].
• LB Mathis Haygood: a team-high 55 tackles [S4]. DL Jameer Lewis: 3 sacks [S4]. DB Kobi Albert: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Southern Miss is 1-5 and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S3]. We opened with a 49-3 win over Alcorn State, then lost at Auburn, to UConn, at Tulane by three, at Troy and to Arkansas State [S3]. That 24-21 game at Tulane tells you this team can play with folks [S3]. After Louisiana, we visit UL Monroe on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, sugar. I'll just say a home win over a 5-2 team would make the whole Pine Belt smile.
Honest scouting, with love: the Troy game was a 55-34 shootout, and we scored 34 on the road [S3]. Against Arkansas State, the Red Wolves won time of possession by about 20 minutes and drained the final 7:21 on one drive [S10]. Our defense needs to get off the field. When it does, this offense can make plays [S5]. And look at the turnover story from last week: Lyddy threw two interceptions, and we gave the ball up on downs three times [S10]. Clean that up and this is a different football team, sugar. One more sweet spot: Louisiana's red zone defense ranks 30th, so every trip inside the 20 has to count for us [S5].

6. This Week: Louisiana (5-2) at Southern Miss (1-5)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 5 p.m. ET · M. M. Roberts Stadium (also listed as Renasant Stadium), Hattiesburg · ESPN+ [S1][S3][S5][S7][S8].
Last week: we lost 23-13 to Arkansas State; Lyddy threw for over 200 yards with a touchdown and two interceptions, and we turned it over on downs three times [S10]. Louisiana beat Troy 33-6 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Louisiana's defense is stingy, 298.3 yards allowed (25th) and 104.3 rushing allowed (27th) [S5]. But its pass defense is 45th [S5], and that's where Lyddy and Sanders can do some damage.
Their offense vs. our defense: Louisiana runs for 200.1 yards a game (29th), led by quarterback Winfield's 463 rushing yards [S5]. That's the matchup that worries me, sugar, and I'll say it plainly.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S12].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Stopping Winfield on the ground. (2) Third downs and red zone trips for our offense. (3) Turnovers.
And Mimi Fontenot, Louisiana's insider: you're a doll. I'll save you a seat and a sweet tea. Then we'll see. Folks in Hattiesburg are proud people, and we'll fill those stands for a 5-2 visitor.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Hattiesburg for the game? Depot Kitchen & Market on Buschman Street is a nice spot for a family supper.

report.title: "That's Peanuts, Buddy": Marlo Pickens Welcomes the Warhawks to Troy
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hey there. That's peanuts, buddy, and I mean that as a compliment. I'm Marlo Pickens. I snapped for the Trojans, my daddy farms peanuts down in the Wiregrass, and I have never once in my life finished a segment without a peanut pun. I'm not sure I could if I tried. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll shell out the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, roasted and salted, in a laid-back drawl you can set your porch swing to. When we win, I crack open a bag of boiled peanuts and grin. When we lose, I shrug and say "That's peanuts," and then I stay up all night with the film, because it isn't, really, and we both know it. Pull up a chair. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Troy has played at the FBS level since 2001 and joined the Sun Belt in 2004 [S7]. The Trojans have won 23 conference championships, eight of them in the Sun Belt [S7]. Home is Veterans Memorial Stadium in Troy, Ala., listed at 30,000 seats [S7][S3]. The last five years have had real highs: 12-2 in 2022 and 11-3 in 2023, then 4-8 and a bounce back to 8-6 in 2025 [S3]. That's a program that knows how to win in this league, and I'm nuts about it. (Sorry. Not sorry.) The town is small, the Saturdays are big, and the stadium sits right in the middle of campus, which is how a college football Saturday ought to look. Folks bring the boiled peanuts themselves. I've checked.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Gerad Parker is the head coach [S7], hired Dec. 18, 2023 [S3]. The 2026 Trojans like to run: 1,228 rushing yards on 239 carries, about 5.1 a carry, with 1,188 passing yards [S3]. The defense has allowed 828 rushing yards on 193 carries and has 10 sacks [S3]. Turnovers are even, seven given and seven taken [S3]. The flag count is the shell we haven't cracked yet: 43 penalties for 452 yards [S3]. And home cooking matters here. Troy is 3-0 at Veterans Memorial and 0-3 on the road [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Goose Crowder: 96 of 169, 1,112 yards, 9 TD, 4 INT [S4]. (One stats site lists him as Will Crowder; ESPN and AP use Goose [S9][S4][S10].)
• QB Tucker Kilcrease: shared snaps at Louisiana and scored on a 23-yard run [S10].
• RB Gavin Griffin: 359 yards on 76 carries, 1 TD [S4].
• WR TK Keyes: 13 catches, 282 yards, 3 TD [S4].
• LB Keno Jones: a team-high 40 tackles [S4]. DB Donnie Smith: a team-high 5 sacks, which is a lot of peanuts for a defensive back [S4]. DE Kavion Henderson: an interception [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Troy is 3-3 and 1-1 in the Sun Belt [S3]. Wins: Sam Houston 24-21, Alabama State 34-17 and Southern Miss 55-34 [S3]. Losses: at Missouri 27-17, at Utah State 21-10 and at Louisiana 33-6 [S3]. Neither team is ranked [S2][S3]. Getting back over .500 at home before the November stretch is the plain goal, and I'll keep it plain. Here's the honest scouting from the press box. When this team plays at Veterans Memorial, it has scored 24, 34 and 55 points [S3]. On the road, it has scored 17, 10 and 6 [S3]. That's two different ballclubs, and the home one is a lot of fun to watch. The Southern Miss game was the high-water mark, 55 points [S3], and that's the version of the Trojans I expect to see stroll out of the tunnel Saturday.

6. This Week: UL Monroe (0-6) at Troy (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Veterans Memorial Stadium · ESPN+ [S1][S8][S9].
Last week: we lost 33-6 at Louisiana (AP's headline says 33-7; the story and CFBD say 33-6) [S10][S3]. Crowder and Kilcrease combined to go 14 of 26 for 141 yards, and Louisiana held the ball more than 13 minutes longer [S10]. A muffed punt at our 8 set up a Louisiana touchdown [S10]. ULM lost 24-0 to Louisiana Tech [S11].
Our offense vs. their defense: ULM has allowed 1,378 rushing yards on 255 carries, about 5.4 a carry, and 247 points in six games [S2]. That plays right into what we like to do.
Their offense vs. our defense: ULM's leading rusher is QB Austin Carlisle, 230 yards [S4], and Aidan Armenta has thrown for 974 yards [S4]. Keep Carlisle in the pocket, and our pass rush, led by Smith, can go to work [S4].
Series: Troy leads 11-8 [S9]. We won last year, 37-14, but ULM won 13-9 in 2024 [S9]. So nobody's shelling anybody without a fight.
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Special teams: no more muffed punts [S10]. (2) Our run game against a defense allowing 5.4 a carry [S2]. (3) Who takes the quarterback snaps, and how cleanly. Crowder has the bigger season numbers [S4], and Kilcrease brought some legs at Louisiana [S10]. Either way, the job is the same: hand it to Griffin, keep the chains moving, and keep the home crowd loud. I'd call that a good, honest Saturday plan, and so would my daddy, who has never once in his life called a play.
And Darnell Vidrine, ULM's insider: I admire a fella who keeps faith. I'll save you a bag of boiled peanuts, win or lose.

report.title: "Keep the Faith, Warhawks": Darnell Vidrine Resets the Counter for Troy
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Keep the faith, Warhawks! Good evening, good morning, good whatever-time-it-is, because I'm Darnell Vidrine, and I've hosted overnight sports radio out of the Delta for so long that every hour feels like 2 a.m. and every caller feels like family. I travel with this team and I live with this team. I keep an optimism counter on my desk, and every week, no matter what, I reset it to 100. It has been reset a lot. It still works. Every week you'll get the players, the matchups, the history and the hope, because I believe we are always one play away from greatness. I can FEEL it. When we win, you'll hear "I KNEW IT!" and you may hear a sniffle. When we lose, I'll say "Keep the faith, y'all," and reach for the counter. Thanks for tuning in. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

UL Monroe football dates to 1931 [S6]. We were the Northeast Louisiana Indians for a long stretch and became the Warhawks in 2006 [S6]. The program moved up to Division I-A, now FBS, in 1994 and plays in the Sun Belt [S6]. Our home is Malone Stadium in Monroe, listed at 27,617 seats and opened in 1978 [S2][S6]. Here's the hard truth, said with love: our only FBS bowl game was the 2012 Independence Bowl in Shreveport, a 45-14 loss to Ohio, and the drought since then is the longest in FBS [S6]. The last five seasons went 4-8, 4-8, 2-10, 5-7 and 3-9 [S2]. Long nights make the sunrise sweeter. That's not a stat. That's just Delta truth.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Bryant Vincent was hired Dec. 5, 2023 [S2]. The 2026 numbers are what they are, and I'll read them to you straight, because the faith only means something if you're honest. ULM has 723 rushing yards on 197 carries and 1,325 passing yards in six games [S2]. The defense has given up 1,378 rushing yards on 255 carries, about 5.4 a carry [S2]. We've scored 120 points and allowed 247 [S2]. The bright spots: two of the losses were one-score games, 26-20 at UAB and 38-35 to SE Louisiana, and we put up 35 points at South Alabama [S2]. When this offense gets rolling, it can score in bunches. And our penalties are low, 33 for 295 yards [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Aidan Armenta: 83 of 131, 974 yards, 6 TD, 3 INT [S4]. Against Louisiana Tech he was 14 of 24 for 105 yards with two interceptions [S9].
• QB Austin Carlisle: our leading rusher, 230 yards on 40 carries, 1 TD [S4], and he's thrown for 358 yards and 3 TD [S9].
• WR Marcellus Jackson: 32 catches, 265 yards [S4].
• LB Noah Flemmings: a team-high 51 tackles [S4]. DL Tyrell Brown: 2.5 sacks [S4]. S Carl Fauntroy: an interception [S4].
(The two stat feeds differ slightly on Armenta and Flemmings; I'm using ESPN's season-leaders feed [S4][S9].)

5. The Conference Picture

ULM is 0-6 and 0-2 in the Sun Belt [S2]. The schedule opened with a trip to Mississippi State, a 62-13 loss, and included Florida Atlantic, 45-17, and last week's 24-0 loss to Louisiana Tech [S2][S11]. Nobody is ranked in this game [S2][S3].  I'm not going to do standings math. I'm going to say this: the first one is the hardest, and it's coming. Here's my optimism counter's case, built only on the numbers. Troy is 0-3 away from home but 3-0 at home [S3], so yes, we're walking into its strongest room. But Troy also scored just 6 points last week [S10], and its offense has topped 24 points only twice this season [S3]. Our defense has been on the field a lot, and it's still swinging. If we can hold the Trojans near their road form for four quarters, the counter stays at 100 well past halftime.

6. This Week: UL Monroe (0-6) at Troy (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Veterans Memorial Stadium, Troy, Ala. · ESPN+ [S1][S8][S9].
Last week: Louisiana Tech shut us out 24-0 [S11]. Troy lost 33-6 at Louisiana; the AP headline says 33-7, but the story and the CFBD record say 33-6 [S10][S3].
Our offense vs. their defense: Troy has allowed 828 rushing yards on 193 carries, about 4.3 a carry, and has 10 sacks [S3]. Its secondary has a sack leader, DB Donnie Smith, with 5 [S4], so Armenta has to watch the blitz.
Their offense vs. our defense: Troy runs it, 1,228 yards on 239 carries [S3]. Gavin Griffin leads with 359 yards [S4]. Our run defense has to get off blocks.
Series: Troy leads 11-8 [S9]. The last six meetings split 4-2 for Troy, and our most recent win was 13-9 in 2024 [S9]. So it's been done, and not that long ago.
Availability: I found no injury or availability report for either team as of Oct. 18 [S12].
What decides it: (1) Whether we can keep Troy's run game under its season average. (2) Turnovers: Armenta threw two interceptions against Louisiana Tech [S9]. (3) Whether Carlisle's legs can give us a spark.
And Marlo Pickens, Troy's insider: I hear you love a peanut pun. I love a comeback. Let's see whose story ends better.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back home in Monroe? Warehouse No. 1 Restaurant on Olive Street, down by the river, is where I'd take the family after a win.

report.title: "Gray Turf, Bright Future": Imogen Tremblay Brings Her Spreadsheet to Athens
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Gray turf, bright future! Hi, I'm Imogen Tremblay. I studied education in Ypsilanti, I build spreadsheets for fun, and I have one tab, color-coded, devoted entirely to the "gray turf advantage." My model says it's worth 1.3 points. My heart says 13. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll walk you through the players, the matchups and the history, plus at least one gentle reminder that Ypsilanti is not Ann Arbor's little brother. We are Ann Arbor's cooler cousin with better parking. When we win, I'll show you a spreadsheet with one enormous green cell, and I will squeal. When we lose, I'll update the model, grimly, and come back next week with more columns. Thanks for being here. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Eastern Michigan has played football since 1891, missing only 1944 [S6]. Before we were the Eagles, we were the Normalites (1899-1928) and the Hurons (1929-1990) [S6]. We've had five undefeated seasons: 1906, 1925, 1927, 1943 and 1945, and the 1943 team didn't allow a point [S6]. Our golden age ran from 1925 through 1939 under Elton Rynearson, and our stadium carries his name [S6]. The field inside is Crosby Field at "The Factory," and yes, it's gray [S10]. CFBD lists Rynearson at 30,200 seats [S2]. We compete in the Mid-American Conference [S6]. Spreadsheet note: the all-time record is 490-622-47 [S6]. Honesty is a column too.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Chris Creighton was hired Dec. 11, 2013 [S2], which makes him a fixture in Ypsilanti. His teams went 7-6 and 9-4 in 2021 and 2022 [S2]. The 2026 offense leans on the arm: 215 passing yards a game (86th) and 105 rushing yards (128th), for 21.5 points a game (110th) [S5]. It converts 41.9% of third downs, 56th in FBS, which is a nice green cell [S5]. The defense allows 379.3 yards a game (97th) and 25.9 points (92nd) [S5]. The stat I love most is quieter: EMU averages just 41.8 penalty yards a game, 15th-fewest in the country [S5]. Clean football is my love language, and also my spreadsheet's.

4. Players to Know

• QB Noah Kim: 169 of 285, 1,678 yards, 11 TD, 4 INT [S4][S5]. Against Toledo he threw for 214 yards and two touchdowns [S5].
• RB Amareon Blue: 338 yards on 68 carries, 3 TD [S4][S5].
• TE Joshua Long: a team-high 38 catches for 366 yards and 2 TD [S4][S5], including seven for 84 and a score last week [S5].
• LB Zach Mowchan: a team-high 58 tackles [S4]. DL Quincy Byas: 4 sacks [S4]. DB Caleb Dobbs: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Eastern Michigan is 4-4 overall and 3-1 in the MAC [S2]. The league wins came at Massachusetts 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and against Sacramento State 28-17 to open the year [S2]. The MAC loss was last week, 34-14 to Toledo [S2][S5]. Non-league games at Michigan State and Wisconsin were losses [S2]. After this, Central Michigan is next, on Nov. 4 [S5]. A road win in Athens would keep the Eagles near the top of the MAC standings [S2]. My spreadsheet would need a new color.
The season, cell by cell: we opened by beating Sacramento State 28-17 and lost 27-21 to San José State, then dropped road games at Michigan State (35-7) and Wisconsin (54-10) [S2]. Since then: Lindenwood 29-3, at UMass 38-14, at Akron 25-23 and the Toledo loss [S2]. That's three road wins already, and two of them were MAC games [S2]. On defense, we've forced nine turnovers and committed ten [S2]. The pass rush has 12 sacks and has allowed 14 [S2]. None of those cells are glowing green yet, but none of them are red either. They're gray. Like the turf. Which, as I've explained, is a good sign.

6. This Week: Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Peden Stadium, Athens, Ohio · ESPNU [S1][S5][S9]. It's Ohio's Senior Day and Heroes Day, and the Bobcats' last Saturday home game of 2026 [S9].
Last week: we lost 34-14 to Toledo on homecoming; Kim was 16 of 36 for 214 yards [S5]. Ohio beat Sacramento State 48-7 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Ohio allows 198.4 passing yards (52nd) and 138.7 rushing (62nd) [S5]. But the Bobcats let opponents convert 42.1% of third downs, 106th [S5], and we're 56th at converting them [S5]. That is a column I'm watching.
Their offense vs. our defense: Ohio runs for 207 yards a game, 24th in FBS [S5]. We allow 142.3 on the ground (71st) [S5]. Our run defense is the whole story.
Series: Ohio leads 22-12-1 and has won four straight, including 28-21 in Ypsilanti last year [S9][S10]. Our last win was 27-20 in Athens in 2016 [S10]. Ten years! My model would like a word. Last year's game was a shootout of sorts on our gray turf: Ohio quarterback Parker Navarro threw for a career-high 315 yards, and two Bobcat receivers went over 100 yards [S9]. Keeping their passing game in check this time starts with knowing that Ohio's 2026 offense is built differently, on the ground [S5].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S11].
What decides it: (1) Whether we can slow Ohio's run game. (2) Third downs on both sides. (3) Kim's accuracy; 44.4% last week won't do [S5].
And Penny Trautman, Ohio's lovely insider: I hear you build things brick by brick. I build them cell by cell. Let's compare blueprints.

report.title: "Brick by Brick": Penny Trautman Lays Out Senior Day at Peden
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Brick by brick, friends. I'm Penny Trautman, and I live in Athens, Ohio, where the streets are brick, the hills are green, and the Bobcats run the football like they're laying Court Street, one solid block at a time. I'm a brick-street archivist by hobby (it's a real hobby; I have a binder), and I chart this run game the same way. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines with some hill-country wit and an unreasonable number of brick puns. When we win, I tap a brick for luck and grin. When we lose, I say "brick by brick" and start rebuilding by Monday. Welcome to the porch. One more thing: I'll always be honest with you, even when the mortar's cracked. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Ohio is the senior member of the Mid-American Conference [S7]. The Bobcats have played home games at Peden Stadium since 1929 [S7], and CFBD lists it at 24,000 seats [S3]. The recent run has been one of the steadiest in the league: 10-4 in 2022, 10-3 in 2023, 11-3 in 2024 and 9-4 in 2025 [S3]. That's four straight winning seasons stacked like good masonry. Saturday is the last Saturday home game at Peden this year, with a Senior Day celebration before kickoff and Heroes Day honoring military members and first responders [S9]. Bring a flag and a thank-you.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

John Hauser is in his first season as head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 26, 2025 [S3]. His Bobcats run it with purpose: 207 rushing yards a game, 24th in FBS [S5], 1,449 yards on 289 carries [S3]. The passing game is a supporting wall, 164.3 yards a game (126th) [S5]. The defense allows 22.1 points (57th) and 337.1 yards (51st) [S5]. One crack to fill: opponents convert 42.1% of third downs, 106th [S5]. And we play clean, 42.6 penalty yards a game, 18th-fewest [S5]. A tidy wall stands longer.
The season, brick by brick: we opened at Nebraska and lost 49-21, then beat Jacksonville State 29-27 [S3]. A 41-36 loss at South Alabama followed, and since then it's been four straight wins: Stonehill 35-7, at Kent State 13-10, Central Michigan 31-14 and at Sacramento State 48-7 [S3]. The Kent State game was a grinder, the kind you win with defense and patience [S3]. The Central Michigan game was the template: run the ball, avoid mistakes, and let the fourth quarter come to you [S3]. Turnovers have been even-ish, eight lost and five gained [S3], and the pass rush has 13 sacks while allowing 12 [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Nick Poulos: 38 of 68, 503 yards, 5 TD, no interceptions [S4][S5]. Last week he went 11 of 14 for 165 and a touchdown, and ran five times for 48 yards [S5].
• RB Duncan Brune: 330 yards on 73 carries, 3 TD [S4][S5]. Irving Brown ran eight times for 87 yards and a score at Sacramento State [S5].
• WR Riley Neer: 32 catches, 441 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5]. Preston Bowman caught three for 94 and a touchdown last week [S5].
• LB Michael Molnar: a team-high 52 tackles and an interception [S4]. DE Ike Ackerman: 4.5 sacks [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Ohio is 5-2 and 3-0 in the MAC, and 3-0 at home [S3]. The losses were at Nebraska and at South Alabama, both outside the league [S3]. In the MAC we've beaten Kent State 13-10, Central Michigan 31-14 and Sacramento State 48-7 [S3]. Eastern Michigan comes in 3-1 in the league [S2], so this is a real conference test. Next is a trip to Akron on Nov. 3 [S5].

6. This Week: Eastern Michigan (4-4) at Ohio (5-2)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 4 p.m. ET · Peden Stadium · ESPNU [S1][S5][S9]. Senior Day and Heroes Day [S9].

report.title: "I Brought a Pen": Hen Lofland Opens a New Chapter in the First State
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Good evening, and please lower your voices; this is a library. Kidding. Shout all you like. I'm Henrietta Lofland, but my friends and the circulation desk call me Hen, and I'm your Delaware insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Newark native, a librarian by day and a wing-T devotee by night. I have opinions about the buck sweep that I've been asked not to share at dinner parties.

Delaware is the First State, and our Blue Hens are writing a brand-new chapter at the FBS level. I'm here to annotate it carefully. You'll get footnotes, because every fact I give you will have a source. You'll get honesty, because if we stumble I'll say so, kindly. You'll also get a librarian's promise: if I don't know something, I'll go look it up before I say it. I brought a pen. A blue one, naturally. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Delaware plays in Conference USA at the FBS level [S6]. The school announced its move to Conference USA and FBS in 2023, ahead of the 2025 season [S6]. Before that, the Blue Hens were an FCS power. They claim six national titles, in 1946, 1963, 1971, 1972, 1979 and 2003 [S6], and they reached the FCS title game again in 2007 and 2010 [S6]. Delaware has produced quarterbacks Rich Gannon and Joe Flacco, among others [S6]. From 1999 to 2010, it was the only FCS program to average more than 20,000 fans at every regular-season home game [S6].

Home is Tubby Raymond Field at Delaware Stadium in Newark [S6]. The stadium dates to 1952 per CFBD [S1]. Capacity is conflicting: CFBD lists 22,000 [S1], while Wikipedia says 18,500 seats [S6]. The last five seasons: 5-6, 8-5, 9-4, 9-2 and 7-6 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Ryan Carty has led the program since the 2022 season [S8]. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 10, 2021 [S1]. This is his fifth season.

In 2026 the Blue Hens lean on the pass. They average 271.0 passing yards per game (29th in FBS) but just 94.0 rushing yards (135th) [S3], and 3.12 yards per carry [S1]. My wing-T heart aches a little. Total offense is 365.0 yards per game, and scoring is 22.8 points per game [S3]. The bright spot is the pass rush: 18 sacks in six games [S1]. The defense allows 390.7 yards per game, with 259.2 through the air (125th) [S3]. Turnovers are even, eight lost and eight forced [S1].

4. Players to Know

• QB Nick Minicucci: the season passing leader, at 838 yards, 5 TD, 3 INT, 57.3% [S3]. AP reported he missed the Middle Tennessee game, his second straight game out [S4]. I haven't found an update on his status for Tuesday, so it's unknown.
• QB Tyler Bell: started in Minicucci's place at Middle Tennessee and threw for 306 yards and two touchdowns on 22 of 36 [S3][S4]. He also caught a 15-yard touchdown pass from Bryson Graves [S9]. Versatile young man.
• RB Jo'Nathan Silver: 230 yards on 58 carries, 1 TD [S3].
• WR Sean Wilson: 25 catches, 339 yards, 3 TD [S3]. Donovan Lewis caught six passes for 83 yards against MTSU [S3].
• LB Blake Matthews: 4.5 sacks [S2]. LB Colin Gallagher: a team-high 42 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

Delaware is 2-4 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA [S1]. The Blue Hens are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The losses: at Vanderbilt (35-26), at Virginia (42-3), Liberty at home (30-14), and at Middle Tennessee (33-30) [S1]. Tuesday is a chance at the first league win of the season, at home, on national television.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Missouri State (2-4) at Delaware (2-4) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Delaware Stadium, Newark · ESPNU [S3][S10]

Last time out. Delaware led 30-26 with 9:57 left at Middle Tennessee after Bell's 23-yard touchdown pass to Kaderris Roberts. Then the Blue Raiders went 93 yards to win 33-30 [S4]. Missouri State beat Kennesaw State 24-21 the next night on Yousef Obeid's 20-yard field goal as time expired [S5]. It was the Bears' first FBS win under Casey Woods [S5].

Delaware's offense vs. Missouri State's defense. This one looks promising on paper. The Bears allow 430.8 yards per game (127th), including 254.3 passing (120th) and 176.5 rushing (108th) [S3]. They give up 30.5 points per game [S3], and opponents convert 44.4% of third downs (120th) [S3]. If our run game, at 94.0 yards per game [S3], can find even modest room, Bell or Minicucci gets to throw on schedule.

Missouri State's offense vs. Delaware's defense. Here is my worry. The Bears average 224.7 passing yards per game [S3], and Isaiah Myers has 554 receiving yards and five touchdowns [S3]. Henry Belin IV threw for a career-high 300 yards in the last game, with two touchdowns to Myers [S5]. Our pass defense ranks 125th [S3]. Our 18 sacks [S1] are the best counterargument I have.

Series. I found no Delaware-Missouri State meeting in CFBD's 2016-2025 list of most frequent opponents [S1], and I haven't confirmed the all-time series. Not found, so not stated.

Availability. No official conference availability report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S10]. The one confirmed item is that Minicucci missed the Oct. 13 game, his second straight [S4]. His status for Tuesday is unknown.

Missouri State also debuts an insider this week. I'm told she guides float trips. I'll lend her a library card. Fair trade.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Who plays quarterback for Delaware, and does it matter as much as protection does [S4]?
2. Can the Blue Hens' pass defense slow Myers [S3]?
3. Can Delaware's pass rush, with 18 sacks [S1], finish drives the way MTSU's offense finished ours?

7. Local Flavor

I'm keeping my best-loved Newark spots in my card catalog until I can confirm them. Not an ad.

report.title: "Right Down the Street": Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate Brings the 305 Heart to Tuesday Night
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

¡Hola, Panther people! Welcome to The Cover Window. I'm Lourdes Ibarguen-Tate, and I grew up in Sweetwater, five minutes from campus, at a kitchen table where my abuela taught me football with cafecito and dominoes. The dominoes were the players. The sugar packets were the defense. To this day I can't watch a fourth-down stop without craving a colada.

Here's what I am: the loudest, warmest, most bilingual hype machine FIU has ever had, and I will never, ever let anybody sleep on this program. Here's what I'm not: a person who makes things up. Every week I'll bring you the real numbers, the real schedule, and an honest, kind look at whoever we're playing. If I don't know something, I'll say "no sé" and go find out. Miami has a lot of teams, but only one is right down the street from my abuela's house. ¡Vamos, Panthers! (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

FIU plays in Conference USA at the FBS level, and home is Pitbull Stadium in Miami [S9][S2]. The stadium opened in 1995, and CFBD lists its capacity at 20,000 [S1], which matches Wikipedia's figure [S9]. The program's trophy case includes a share of the 2010 Sun Belt championship and three bowl appearances [S9]. Last season was a big one: under first-year coach Willie Simmons, the Panthers went 7-6 [S1] and made their first bowl trip since 2019 [S8].

Look at the last five seasons and you'll see why that mattered so much to my family: 1-11 in 2021, then three straight 4-8 years, then 7-6 in 2025 [S1]. The Panthers also play Florida Atlantic every year in the Shula Bowl [S8].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Willie Simmons is in Year Two [S8]. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 7, 2024 [S1]. Before FIU, he was head coach at Florida A&M from 2018 to 2023, winning a black college national championship and a SWAC title in 2023, and at Prairie View A&M from 2015 to 2017 [S11]. He played quarterback at Clemson and The Citadel [S11].

What do the 2026 numbers say? This team wins with defense. FIU allows 14.7 points per game [S4], and opponents average just 3.21 yards per carry [S1]. The Panthers have 14 sacks in six games [S1]. The offense is perfectly balanced in volume, with 214 rushing attempts and 214 pass attempts [S1], but it averages only 19.7 points per game [S4] and 3.36 yards per carry [S1]. Ball security needs work: nine giveaways against eight takeaways [S1].

4. Players to Know

• QB JJ Kohl: 116 of 199 for 1,458 yards, 7 TD, 7 INT [S2][S3]. He threw for 278 yards and two touchdowns in the loss at Jax State [S6].
• RB Devonte Lyons: 268 yards on 65 carries, 1 TD [S2]. He ran for 78 yards on 14 carries against New Mexico State [S7].
• WR Maguire Anderson: 33 catches, 534 yards, 4 TD, the team's top receiver [S2][S4].
• DL DeeJay Holmes Jr.: 5 sacks [S2], plus 6 tackles for loss [S3].
• DB DeAndre Boykins: a team-high 37 tackles [S2].
• K Robert Czeremcha: made a career-high five field goals against New Mexico State, tying the program record [S7]. He missed from 38 and 49 at Jax State [S6], and I know he wants Tuesday badly.

5. The Conference Picture

FIU is 3-3 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA [S1]. Here's the fun part: the Panthers are 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1], and after the New Mexico State win AP noted the Panthers had won five straight home games dating to last season [S7]. All three losses came by 10 points or fewer: at USF (19-9), at Florida Atlantic (16-10) and at Jax State (27-24) [S1]. FIU is not ranked [S1]. A home win Tuesday gets the Panthers back above .500 in league play.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Middle Tennessee (3-3) at FIU (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Pitbull Stadium, Miami · CBS Sports Network [S8][S2]

Last time out. FIU lost 27-24 at Jax State on Oct. 13, when Garrison Rippa kicked a 26-yard field goal with 44 seconds left [S6]. Middle Tennessee rallied past Delaware 33-30 the same night. Roman Gagliano threw for 291 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another, and led a 10-play, 93-yard drive that ended with a 14-yard touchdown pass to Neo Clifton with 3:06 to go [S5].

FIU's defense vs. MTSU's offense. This is the matchup I'm watching with my cafecito. The Blue Raiders score 22.8 points per game and throw for 200.7 yards a game [S4]. Gagliano is efficient: 110 of 188, 1,204 yards, 11 touchdowns and only two interceptions [S2]. Antonio Martin Jr. has 433 rushing yards [S2], and Cam'ron Lacy has 35 catches for 369 yards [S2]. But FIU allows only 166.0 passing yards and 100.0 rushing yards per game [S4]. Holmes against MTSU's protection could decide a lot of drives.

FIU's offense vs. MTSU's defense. The Blue Raiders allow 28.3 points per game [S4] and 5.21 yards per carry [S1]. They gave up 55 points at Kansas [S1]. If Lyons and the run game can get going, Kohl gets manageable third downs. MTSU's defense does have a playmaker in linebacker Korey Smith, who leads his team with 56 tackles [S2].

Series. Middle Tennessee leads the all-time series 14-7 [S3], and CFBD shows MTSU winning seven of 10 meetings from 2016 to 2025 [S1]. But FIU has won the last two: 35-24 in 2024 and 56-30 in Murfreesboro in 2025 [S3]. That 2025 win started a 4-0 finish to the regular season [S8].

Availability. No official conference availability report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed FIU or MTSU injury news in the sources above, so every status is unknown to me until game notes come out.

Middle Tennessee debuts its own insider this week too. Welcome, neighbor.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can FIU's pass rush rattle Gagliano, who has thrown just two interceptions all year [S2]?
2. Can the Panthers finish drives with touchdowns instead of leaning on Czeremcha [S6][S7]?
3. Does the 3-0 home magic hold one more Tuesday [S1]?

7. Local Flavor

I'm not listing restaurants until I can confirm them for you. For now: bring your family, bring your voice, and get to Pitbull Stadium early. Not an ad.

report.title: "Writing It Live": Ximena Holcombe-Reyes Opens a New Chapter Against Liberty
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Hey, Owl Nation! I'm Ximena Holcombe-Reyes, your Kennesaw State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Marietta native with a computer science degree, and I've cheered this program since its very first season. I was there for version 1.0. I still have the T-shirt. It no longer fits. That's growth.

Here's my operating system. I'm a builder. I love that some programs have a hundred years of history while Kennesaw State gets to write ours right now, live, in front of us. I'm keeping the notes. Every number I share is sourced and debugged. Every opponent gets respect. When I don't know something, I'll log it as "unknown" instead of guessing. Bugs happen. We patch them, and we ship again. Let's go, Owls. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Kennesaw State football began play in 2015 as an FCS member of the Big South Conference [S6]. In 2022 the Owls moved to the ASUN's new FCS football league, and after that season they began the transition to FBS ahead of joining Conference USA in 2024 [S6]. That's an entire program history in about a decade. Speedrun.

Home is Fifth Third Stadium, just outside the Kennesaw city limits [S6]. The game feed lists it as Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium [S9], and CFBD lists it as built in 2010 with a capacity of 11,040 [S1]. The last five seasons: 11-2, 5-6, 3-6, 2-10, and then a big jump to 10-4 in 2025 [S1]. Last year the Owls finished the regular season 9-3 and 7-1 in Conference USA [S8].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jerry Mack is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 1, 2024 [S1], so this is his second season. He was head coach at North Carolina Central from 2014 to 2017, going 31-15 [S7], and was later offensive coordinator and associate head coach at Rice [S7]. He played wide receiver at Jackson State and Arkansas State [S7].

The 2026 numbers show a balanced offense, with 193 rushes and 198 passes [S1]. It averages 223.7 passing and 143.7 rushing yards per game, and scores 22.3 points [S3]. Yards per carry is 4.47 [S1]. The defense allows 376.3 yards (94th) and 23.5 points (66th) per game [S3]. Two things to patch: penalties, at 77.8 yards per game (129th) [S3], and red-zone defense, where opponents score on 95.5% of trips (132nd) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Rickie Collins: completing 70.1% of his passes [S3]. Season yardage is conflicting: AP lists 1,287 [S3] and ESPN lists 1,302 [S2], both with 4 TD and 3 INT. He also leads the team in rushing, with 271 yards and 5 TD on 64 carries [S3]. Against Missouri State he threw for 260 yards and ran for a touchdown [S3][S5].
• WR Javon Rogers: 18 catches, 308 yards, 1 TD [S3].
• WR Dylan Gary: 10 catches for 135 yards and a touchdown at Missouri State [S3][S5].
• RB Alan Woods III: 47 rushing yards and a touchdown on 13 carries at Missouri State, plus six catches [S3].
• DL Ugonna Nwoha: 3 sacks [S2]. LB Tywon Christopher: a team-high 48 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

Kennesaw State is 1-5 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA [S1]. The Owls are 1-2 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. They've lost five straight since a 47-0 win over West Georgia in the opener [S5]. But look closer at the commit history: the losses to Arkansas State (17-14), Jacksonville State (27-26) and Missouri State (24-21) were all by three points or fewer [S1]. The code is close to compiling. A home win Thursday would be the first league win of 2026.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Liberty (5-1) at Kennesaw State (1-5) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw, Ga. · CBS Sports Network [S3][S9]

Last time out. The Owls took a halftime lead at Missouri State on a 10-yard Collins-to-Gary touchdown pass, but lost 24-21 on a field goal as time expired [S5]. Liberty beat Sam Houston 35-3 on Oct. 8 [S4], its fifth straight win [S4].

KSU's offense vs. Liberty's defense. I'll be straight with you: this is a tough draw. Liberty allows 15.3 points per game (15th), 167.5 passing yards (15th) [S3], and just 28.4% on third down (8th) [S3]. Our path is Collins's efficiency and his legs. Staying on schedule, and converting the 40.3% of third downs we've managed so far (74th) [S3], decides whether drives keep running.

Liberty's offense vs. KSU's defense. The Flames run for 223.0 yards per game (15th) [S3]. Kam Davis has 524 yards [S3], and quarterback Deshawn Purdie hasn't thrown an interception all season [S3]. Our run defense allows 143.0 yards per game (74th) [S3]. Makai Jackson averages more than 23 yards a catch [S3], so the deep ball is a threat too. Liberty is heavily penalized, at 85.8 yards per game (137th) [S3], so our defense can't give back the yards it gets for free.

report.title: "Somebody's Son": Gideon Fairweather Brings Joy (and a Five-Game Streak) to Kennesaw
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, praise the Lord and pass the program! I'm Gideon Fairweather, your Liberty insider at The Cover Window. I grew up in Lynchburg, and I'm a youth pastor who coaches middle-school football on the side. That means I've given a halftime speech about perseverance to eleven 12-year-olds who were mostly worried about Gatorade flavors. I'm ready for anything.

You'll hear a big laugh from me, and a lot of encouragement. When I look at a roster, I see a hundred-some young men who are each somebody's son, and I'll write about them that way. I'll also tell you the truth. Every number here is sourced. If we play poorly, I'll say so gently. If I don't know something, I'll admit it. Lynchburg on game day feels like a family reunion with a marching band. Our guys play hard, play fair, and you can see the joy on their faces. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Liberty University is a private Christian university in Lynchburg, Virginia [S6]. Its football program announced the move from FCS to FBS in July 2017, became a provisional FBS member in 2018, and became a full member with bowl eligibility in 2019 [S6]. In 2020 the Flames entered the AP poll for the first time, at No. 25 [S6]. They joined Conference USA for the 2023 season [S6].

Home is Williams Stadium, which CFBD lists as built in 1989 with a capacity of 25,000 [S1]. The last five seasons: 8-5, 8-5, a magnificent 13-1 in 2023, 8-4, and then a humbling 4-8 in 2025 [S1]. That makes a 5-1 start this year [S1] a joyful sight.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jamey Chadwell has led Liberty since the 2023 season [S7]. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 4, 2022 [S1]. Before Lynchburg, he was head coach at North Greenville (2009-11), Delta State (2012), Charleston Southern (2013-16) and Coastal Carolina, first as interim in 2017 and then from 2019 to 2022 [S7]. He played quarterback at East Tennessee State [S7]. (One AP recap credited Liberty's record to a different coach. CFBD and Wikipedia both list Chadwell, so I treat that as an error [S4].)

The 2026 Flames run the ball and play defense. They average 223.0 rushing yards per game (15th in FBS) [S3] at 5.27 yards per carry [S1], and they have 254 rushing attempts to 129 passes [S1]. The defense allows 291.7 yards (19th) and 15.3 points (15th) per game [S3], and opponents convert just 28.4% of third downs (8th) [S3]. The area for growth is penalties, at 85.8 yards per game, 137th in FBS [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Deshawn Purdie: 1,050 yards, 8 TD, 0 INT, 61.4% [S3]. Zero interceptions! Against Sam Houston he went 10 of 14 for 114 yards and a touchdown, and ran seven times for 57 yards [S4].
• RB Kam Davis: 524 yards on 74 carries, 4 TD [S3].
• RB Jaylon Coleman: 92 yards on just seven carries against Sam Houston [S4]. Ethan Vasko scored two rushing touchdowns in that game [S4].
• WR Makai Jackson: 22 catches, 515 yards, 5 TD [S3]. That's more than 23 yards a catch.
• DB Brenton Williams: 2.5 sacks [S2]. LB Derrell Farrar: a team-high 33 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

Liberty is 5-1 overall and 2-0 in Conference USA [S1]. The Flames are 3-0 at home and 2-1 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The only loss was the opener at James Madison, 20-13 [S1]. Liberty has won five straight [S4], including road wins at Coastal Carolina and Delaware [S1]. A win Thursday would make the Flames 3-0 in league play [S1].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Liberty (5-1) at Kennesaw State (1-5) · Thursday, Oct. 22, 7:00 p.m. ET · Walens Family Field at Fifth Third Stadium, Kennesaw, Ga. · CBS Sports Network [S3][S9]

Last time out. Liberty beat Sam Houston 35-3 on Oct. 8, piling up 297 rushing yards [S4]. Kennesaw State lost 24-21 at Missouri State on Oct. 14 on a field goal as time expired [S5]. That's the Owls' fifth straight loss since a 47-0 opening win over West Georgia [S5].

Liberty's offense vs. KSU's defense. The Owls allow 143.0 rushing yards per game (74th) and 376.3 total yards (94th) [S3]. Our ground game is the plan, with Davis, Coleman and Purdie's legs. Kennesaw State ranks 132nd in red-zone defense, allowing scores on 95.5% of trips [S3], and our red-zone offense scores 88.5% of the time (45th) [S3]. Jackson against a pass defense allowing 233.3 yards per game (102nd) [S3] could produce a big play or two.

KSU's offense vs. Liberty's defense. Rickie Collins is a dual threat. He's completed 70.1% of his passes [S3] and leads the Owls in rushing, with 271 yards and five touchdowns [S3]. Against Missouri State, Dylan Gary caught 10 passes for 135 yards [S5]. Our defense allows 167.5 passing yards per game (15th) [S3], and slowing Collins on third down, where KSU converts 40.3% (74th) [S3], is the job.

Series. I won't sugarcoat it. Kennesaw State has won the last three meetings, including 48-42 in double overtime in Lynchburg on Nov. 29, 2025 [S8]. A search summary of the schools' records puts KSU ahead 3-2 all-time [S8], and CFBD shows the Owls 3-1 against us from 2016 to 2025 [S1]. My youth group calls this a "growth opportunity."

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S9]. I found no confirmed injury news for either team, so all statuses are unknown.

Kennesaw State is debuting its own insider, and I hear she's keeping notes on a young program's story. I'll pray for her keyboard, and for our tackling.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Liberty clean up the penalties (85.8 yards a game) on the road [S3]?
2. Can the Flames contain Collins as a passer and runner [S3]?
3. Can the run game control the clock the way it has all year, with a 33:26 average possession time (12th) [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

I'll share Kennesaw spots once I've confirmed them. Our youth group's packing PB&Js anyway. Not an ad.

report.title: "Sit With Us": Opal Stonebriar Packs a Cooler for Miami
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Well, hey there, sugar. Come in, sit down, and have a biscuit. I'm Opal Stonebriar, your Middle Tennessee insider here at The Cover Window. I'm a Rutherford County girl and a church choir director, raised on Friday-night lights and Saturday Blue Raiders. Folks call me the front-row grandma of Murfreesboro. I'm 34. It's a spiritual title.

Here's how this works. I will feed you, I will love on these boys like they're my own, and if you say something about my team that isn't true, I will correct you sweetly and with a citation. I don't make up numbers, I don't make up injuries, and when I don't know something I'll say, "Honey, I don't know yet." Murfreesboro is a city that grew up fast, and so did our program. Come sit with us, and you'll leave a Blue Raider. I promise. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Middle Tennessee plays FBS football in Conference USA, out of Murfreesboro, Tennessee [S10]. The Blue Raiders have played in 14 bowl games and seven I-AA playoffs [S10]. Home is Johnny "Red" Floyd Stadium, which opened in 1933 [S1]. The sources disagree on its size. CFBD lists a capacity of 30,788 [S1], and Wikipedia lists 27,303 [S10]. I'm noting both until I check the media guide.

The last five seasons have been a climb and then a dip: 7-6 in 2021, 8-5 in 2022, 4-8 in 2023, and 3-9 in both 2024 and 2025 [S1]. So a 3-3 start in 2026 [S1] already beats last year's win total by midseason, and in my kitchen that calls for a pound cake.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Derek Mason was hired on Dec. 6, 2023, as the 15th head coach in program history [S10][S1]. Before Murfreesboro, he was head coach at Vanderbilt from 2014 to 2020 [S11]. This is his third season [S1].

Here's what the 2026 numbers show. The offense averages 22.8 points per game, with 200.7 passing yards and 120.8 rushing yards per game [S4]. It runs efficiently, at 4.74 yards per carry [S1], and it takes care of the football: only four giveaways all season, against eight takeaways [S1]. Defense is the worry. Opponents average 28.3 points per game [S4] and 5.21 yards per carry [S1]. FOX Sports lists the Blue Raiders' 11 tackles for loss as the second-fewest in FBS [S4]. That's not a scheme label, just the numbers.

4. Players to Know

• QB Roman Gagliano: 110 of 188, 1,204 yards, 11 TD, just 2 INT [S2][S3]. Against Delaware he threw for 291 yards and three touchdowns, ran for another, and led the game-winning 93-yard drive [S5]. Sweet as tea and twice as cool.
• RB Antonio Martin Jr.: 433 yards on 83 carries, 1 TD [S2][S3].
• WR Cam'ron Lacy: 35 catches, 369 yards, 4 TD [S2].
• WR Neo Clifton and WR Koraun Perdue: against Delaware, Clifton caught four passes for 64 yards and two touchdowns, including the winner. Perdue caught four for 103 yards and an 80-yard score [S5].
• LB Korey Smith: leads the team in tackles. ESPN lists 56 [S2] and FOX lists 55 [S4], so the count is conflicting by one.
• Sacks: the sources disagree on the team leader. ESPN lists Kaven Call (1) [S2], while FOX and Sports-Reference list Ashton Taylor (2 per FOX, 1 per Sports-Reference) [S4][S3]. Conflicting, so I'm showing all of it.

5. The Conference Picture

Middle Tennessee is 3-3 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA [S1]. The Blue Raiders are 3-0 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1], with road losses at Marshall (28-26), Jax State (23-13) and Kansas (55-0) [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. A road win Tuesday would put them over .500 in the league and break that road skid. That's a big "if," and a beautiful one.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

Middle Tennessee (3-3) at FIU (3-3) · Tuesday, Oct. 20, 7:00 p.m. ET · Pitbull Stadium, Miami · CBS Sports Network [S8][S2]

Last time out. We rallied! Down 30-26 in the fourth quarter against Delaware on Oct. 13, Gagliano led a 10-play, 93-yard drive and hit Clifton for a 14-yard touchdown with 3:06 left. Final: 33-30 [S5]. FIU lost 27-24 at Jax State that same night on a field goal with 44 seconds left [S6].

MTSU's offense vs. FIU's defense. I won't sugarcoat it: this FIU defense is stingy. The Panthers allow 14.7 points, 166.0 passing yards and 100.0 rushing yards per game [S4]. DeeJay Holmes Jr. has five sacks and six tackles for loss [S2][S3]. Our answer is protecting the football. Gagliano's two interceptions in 188 attempts [S2] mean FIU will have to earn every stop.

FIU's offense vs. MTSU's defense. FIU scores 19.7 points per game [S4] and averages 3.36 yards per carry [S1]. JJ Kohl has 1,458 passing yards with seven touchdowns and seven interceptions [S2], and Maguire Anderson has 534 receiving yards [S2]. Our defense allows 216.5 passing yards per game [S4], so keeping Anderson in front of us matters. FIU has also turned it over nine times [S1], and our defense has eight takeaways [S1].

Series. Middle Tennessee leads the all-time series 14-7 [S3]. From 2016 to 2025, CFBD shows us winning seven of 10 [S1]. I'll be honest, though: FIU won the last two, 35-24 in 2024 and 56-30 in Murfreesboro in 2025 [S3]. Bless it. We remember.

Availability. No official conference availability report for this game as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S12]. I found no confirmed injury news for either team in these sources, so I'm treating every status as unknown until game notes are released.

FIU is introducing its own insider this week, and I've heard she makes a mean cafecito. I'll bring the biscuits, and we'll call it even.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Gagliano keep his turnover-free ways against a defense allowing 14.7 points a game [S2][S4]?
2. Can our run defense, at 5.21 yards per carry allowed [S1], keep FIU off schedule?
3. Can we finally win on the road after an 0-3 start away from home [S1]?

7. Local Flavor

I'm not naming spots until I can confirm them. Pack a cooler for the drive, sugar. Not an ad.

report.title: "Pack a Snack": Clementine Bilyeu Floats the Bears to Newark
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Howdy from the Ozarks! I'm Clementine Bilyeu, your Missouri State insider here at The Cover Window. I'm a Springfield native and a float-trip guide, and I've been maroon since the day I was born. Mama swears my first word was "Bears." It was probably "boat," but I've chosen my story and I'm sticking with it.

I take a practical view of football, the same way I take a river. Read the current, respect the rocks, and keep everybody in the canoe. Missouri State is on a brand-new ride as an FBS program, and I'm thrilled to be your guide. I'll give you real numbers, honest takes, and kind words for every opponent. If I don't know something, I'll tell you, and then I'll paddle off and find out. Springfield is the heart of the Ozarks, and our Bears are taking the whole region along. Pack a snack. It's going to be a fun float. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Missouri State University is in Springfield, Missouri, and its first football team took the field in 1909 [S7]. Until 2005, the school was known as Southwest Missouri State [S7]. The Bears were a founding member of the Gateway Football Conference in 1985, which later became the Missouri Valley Football Conference [S7]. They joined Conference USA in 2025 and became a full FBS member in 2026 [S7]. Wikipedia lists an all-time record of 492-532-39 and 10 conference championships [S7].

Home is Plaster Sports Complex, which CFBD lists with a capacity of 17,337 and a 1941 construction year [S1]. The last five seasons: 8-4, 5-6, 4-7, 8-4 and 7-6 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Casey Woods is in his first season as head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 19, 2025 [S1]. He was previously offensive coordinator at SMU and played wide receiver at Tennessee [S8].

The 2026 offense is fairly balanced, with 202 rushing attempts and 183 pass attempts [S1]. It averages 359.5 yards per game, 224.7 passing and 134.8 rushing, and scores 22.2 points per game [S3]. Yards per carry sits at 4.00 [S1]. The defense is the stretch of river with rocks in it. It allows 430.8 yards (127th in FBS) and 30.5 points per game (116th) [S3]. The Bears have seven sacks [S1], seven giveaways and six takeaways [S1]. Penalties have been a drag, at 394 yards in six games [S1].

4. Players to Know

• QB Henry Belin IV: threw for a career-high 300 yards on 28 of 39 against Kennesaw State, with two touchdowns [S5][S3]. He also ran nine times for 24 yards [S3].
• QB Skyler Locklear: the season passing leader, at 788 yards, 4 TD, 2 INT, 65.7% [S3][S2]. AP's preview doesn't say who will start Tuesday, so I'm calling the starter unconfirmed.
• WR Isaiah Myers: 27 catches, 554 yards, 5 TD [S3]. He had seven catches for 135 yards and both touchdowns against KSU, tying the game twice in the second half [S5]. That boy can run a rapid.
• Rushing leader: conflicting. AP lists Jambres Dubar (233 yards on 42 carries, 2 TD) [S3], and ESPN lists Ramone Green Jr. (227 yards on 51 carries, 2 TD) [S2]. Connor Lair carried 14 times for 65 yards against KSU [S3].
• LB Jared Lloyd: a team-high 71 tackles [S2].
• K Yousef Obeid: made the 20-yard game-winner as time expired, plus two earlier field goals [S5].

5. The Conference Picture

Missouri State is 2-4 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA [S1]. The Bears are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The Kennesaw State win was their first FBS victory under Woods [S5]. Their earlier win came over FCS member Lindenwood [S5]. Their losses were at Texas A&M, to Marshall at home (30-24), at SMU (34-24) and at Western Kentucky (34-13) [S1]. A road win in Newark would make them 2-1 in league play [S1], and I'd like that very much.

report.title: "Turn Up the Heat": Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya Roasts Up a Wednesday in Huntsville
report.byline: Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya · New Mexico State Insider
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

¡Buenas noches, Aggies! I'm Esperanza Lujan-Tafoya, your New Mexico State insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Las Cruces native, a chile farmer's daughter and an ag-science grad. That means I can tell you the soil pH of the practice field and how much Scoville heat a fourth-down stop packs. (A lot. A fourth-down stop is Christmas-style, red and green.)

Everything gets a chile rating from me. A routine first down? Mild. A 40-yard run? Hatch hot. But I don't heat up the facts. Every number I give you is real and sourced. Every opponent gets respect. If I don't know something, I'll say so, and then I'll go find out. In the Mesilla Valley, fall smells like roasting chile and fresh-cut grass. Our Aggies play with that same heat, and the Organ Mountains watch every snap. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

New Mexico State plays FBS football in Conference USA [S7]. The road here was winding. The Aggies were independent in 2013, a football-only Sun Belt member from 2014 to 2017, and independent again from 2018 [S7]. They announced in November 2021 that they would join Conference USA in all sports starting in 2023 [S7]. Home is Aggie Memorial Stadium in Las Cruces, which CFBD lists as built in 1978 with a capacity of 28,853 [S1].

Here's the honest part: Wikipedia notes that NMSU has one of the longest AP poll droughts in FBS, with its last ranking in 1960 [S7]. The recent highs are real, though. The Aggies went 10-5 in 2023 [S1]. The last five seasons: 2-10, 7-6, 10-5, 3-9 and 4-8 [S1].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Tony Sanchez is the head coach. CFBD lists his hire date as Dec. 23, 2023 [S1]. He's an NMSU alum and a former Aggie wide receiver [S8]. He was head coach at UNLV from 2014 to 2019, and before that at Bishop Gorman High School in Las Vegas [S8].

The 2026 numbers say run first. NMSU averages 142.7 rushing yards per game [S3] at 4.53 yards per carry [S1], plus 230.5 passing yards [S3]. Scoring is 23.7 points per game (97th) [S3]. The defense is sturdier against the run. It allows 125.5 rushing yards (47th) and 3.50 yards per carry [S3][S1], and it has 15 sacks [S1]. The red-pepper warnings: a -5 turnover margin (122nd) [S3], 92.9% red-zone scoring allowed (118th) [S3], and a 27:08 time of possession (127th) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• RB James Jones: 599 yards on 92 carries, 3 TD [S3]. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game, then ran for 89 there [S5]. Chile rating: Hatch hot.
• QB Trey Hedden: the season passing leader, at 906 yards, 5 TD, 6 INT, 52.4% [S3]. He started the first four games [S5].
• QB Adam Damante: started at FIU, going 9 of 22 for 104 yards with an interception [S3][S5]. Wednesday's starter isn't confirmed in my sources.
• WR Tyler "TK" King: 20 catches, 286 yards, 3 TD [S3][S2]. Terrione Graves caught two passes for 39 yards at FIU [S3].
• DE Gabe Peterson: 4.5 sacks [S2]. S Nick Session: a team-high 50 tackles [S2].

5. The Conference Picture

New Mexico State is 2-4 overall and 1-1 in Conference USA [S1]. The Aggies are 2-1 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The highlight so far is a 34-13 win over Western Kentucky [S1], the same WKU team that beat Sam Houston 16-3 last week [S4]. A road win Wednesday would make NMSU 2-1 in the league and earn its first road win of 2026 [S1].

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

New Mexico State (2-4) at Sam Houston (1-5) · Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET · Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville, Texas · ESPN2 [S3]

Last time out. FIU beat us 22-3 in Miami on Oct. 7. Their kicker made five field goals, and we threw two interceptions [S5]. Sam Houston lost 16-3 to Western Kentucky on Oct. 14 and managed just 177 total yards [S4]. Both teams have had a week to cool off. Time to fire up the roaster again.

NMSU's offense vs. Sam Houston's defense. This is the matchup I'm roasting over an open flame. The Bearkats allow 200.3 rushing yards per game (129th) [S3]. Jones against that front is my top storyline. Sam Houston's pass defense, though, allows just 137.8 yards per game (4th in FBS) [S3], so I expect the Aggies to stay on the ground. One more thing: the Bearkats hold opponents to 32.1% on third down (24th) [S3]. Staying ahead of the chains is the key.

Sam Houston's offense vs. NMSU's defense. Landyn Locke has 1,418 passing yards and 11 touchdowns [S2][S3] in Phil Longo's offense, which Wikipedia calls air raid [S8]. The Bearkats run for just 95.0 yards per game (134th) [S3], so they'll lean on Locke. Our pass defense allows 222.3 yards per game (90th) [S3], and our 15 sacks [S1] are the answer. Peterson needs a big night.

Series. New Mexico State leads 2-1, per a search summary of school records: NMSU won 27-13 in 2023, Sam Houston won 31-11 in 2024, and NMSU won 37-10 on Oct. 2, 2025 [S9]. I'm marking that thin until I confirm it on the media guide.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S10]. Our quarterback situation is unconfirmed: Hedden started four games and Damante started the last one [S5]. I found no other confirmed injury news.

Sam Houston debuts a storyteller insider this week too, a history teacher. I'll bring the green chile stew if he brings the campfire.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can Jones and the run game feast on a defense allowing 200.3 rushing yards a game [S3]?
2. Can the Aggies stop giving the ball away (-5 margin) [S3]?
3. Can our defense pressure Locke into mistakes [S1][S3]?

7. Local Flavor

I'm not naming Huntsville spots I haven't checked. I'm packing my own chile, thanks. Not an ad.

report.title: "Pull Up a Stump": Lem Coxwell Tells the Bearkats' Tale Under the Wednesday Lights
report.text:
1. Meet Your Insider

Evenin', folks. Pull up a stump. I'm Lemuel Coxwell, but everybody from here to the Trinity River calls me Lem, and I'm your Sam Houston insider at The Cover Window. I'm a Walker County native and a high-school history teacher, and I collect Texas folklore the way some folks collect bottle caps. My students say I can turn a fire drill into a three-part saga. They're not wrong.

Here's how I'll tell it. I'll be patient, because seasons are long and young men grow. I'll be proud, because Huntsville is a small Texas town with a big Texas name, and our Bearkats play like they're carrying it. Most of all, I'll be honest. A good storyteller never needs to stretch the truth. Every number I give you will be real. If I don't know something, I'll say so plain, then go dig through the archives. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Sam Houston State fielded its first football team in 1912 [S7]. Home is Elliott T. Bowers Stadium in Huntsville, which seats 14,000 [S7][S1]; CFBD lists it as built in 1986 [S1]. In 2021 the Bearkats left the Southland Conference for the WAC's FCS football league, and in November 2021 they accepted an invitation to join Conference USA at the FBS level starting in 2023-24 [S7].

The last five seasons tell a tale with some hills in it: 11-1 in 2021, 5-4 in 2022, 3-9 in 2023, 10-3 in 2024 and 2-10 in 2025 [S1]. That 10-3 year was the high mark of the FBS era so far [S1]. Every good story has a hard chapter before a good one.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Phil Longo was named Sam Houston's 16th head coach on Dec. 18, 2024 [S7][S1], so this is his second season. Wikipedia describes him as a practitioner of the air raid offense [S8]. He was previously offensive coordinator at Wisconsin, and before that offensive coordinator and quarterbacks coach at North Carolina, Ole Miss and Sam Houston [S8].

The 2026 numbers match that reputation through the air but not on the ground. The Bearkats throw for 247.0 yards per game (51st in FBS) and run for 95.0 (134th) [S3], at 3.15 yards per carry [S1]. Scoring sits at 19.5 points per game (123rd) [S3]. The defense is split. It allows just 137.8 passing yards per game (4th in FBS) but 200.3 rushing yards (129th) [S3], and opponents convert only 32.1% of third downs (24th) [S3]. The Bearkats have 12 sacks [S1] and a +1 turnover margin (61st) [S3].

4. Players to Know

• QB Landyn Locke: 129 of 205, 1,418 yards, 11 TD, 4 INT, 62.9% [S2][S3]. He was 13 of 30 for 112 yards against Western Kentucky [S3].
• RB Alton McCaskill: 211 yards on 53 carries, 1 TD [S2][S3]. M.J. Dowdy ran 14 times for 55 yards against WKU [S3].
• WR Chris Reed: 17 catches, 289 yards, 3 TD [S3], including three catches for 51 yards against WKU [S3].
• LB Dean Ford: a team-high 38 tackles [S2]. LB Elijah Groves: 2.5 sacks [S2].
• K Sam Carpenter: made a 42-yard field goal against WKU and a 36-yarder at Liberty [S4][S6].

5. The Conference Picture

Sam Houston is 1-5 overall and 0-2 in Conference USA [S1]. The Bearkats are 1-2 at home and 0-3 on the road [S1]. They are not ranked [S1]. The two close losses came early, 24-21 at Troy and 23-17 to Tulsa [S1]. Since then it's been a steep climb: 49-14 at Texas Tech, 35-3 at Liberty and 16-3 to Western Kentucky [S1]. The lone win was 59-0 over Nicholls [S1]. A home win Wednesday would be the first league win of the season. In a long story, that's the chapter where the hero stands back up.

6. This Week: Game Preview from Both Sides

New Mexico State (2-4) at Sam Houston (1-5) · Wednesday, Oct. 21, 8:00 p.m. ET · Elliott T. Bowers Stadium, Huntsville · ESPN2 [S3]

Last time out. Western Kentucky won 16-3 in Huntsville on Oct. 14. Sam Houston was held to 177 total yards and 12 first downs [S4]. WKU is now 4-1 against Sam Houston and perfect since the Bearkats joined CUSA in 2023 [S4]. New Mexico State lost 22-3 at FIU on Oct. 7 [S3]. FIU's kicker made five field goals, and NMSU threw two interceptions [S5].

Sam Houston's offense vs. New Mexico State's defense. The Aggies allow 347.8 yards per game (61st) and are tougher against the run (125.5 yards, 47th) than the pass (222.3, 90th) [S3]. So Locke's arm is our best path. NMSU has 15 sacks [S1], with Gabe Peterson at 4.5 [S2], so protection matters. The Aggies rank 118th in red-zone defense, allowing scores on 92.9% of trips [S3]. Get there, and good things tend to happen.

New Mexico State's offense vs. Sam Houston's defense. The Aggies will want to run, and James Jones is the reason: 599 yards on 92 carries and three touchdowns [S3]. He entered the FIU game leading Conference USA at 102.0 rushing yards per game [S5]. Our run defense allows 200.3 yards a game [S3]. That's the whole ballgame in one sentence. Our pass defense, fourth in FBS [S3], should make the Aggies one-dimensional if we can slow Jones.

Series. New Mexico State leads 2-1. NMSU won 27-13 in 2023, Sam Houston won 31-11 in 2024, and NMSU won 37-10 on Oct. 2, 2025 [S9]. Those series details come from a search summary of the schools' pages, so I'm marking them thin.

Availability. No official conference availability report as of Oct. 18, 2026 [S10]. I found no confirmed Sam Houston injury news. On the New Mexico State side, Adam Damante started at FIU after Trey Hedden started the first four games [S5]. Who starts Wednesday hasn't been confirmed.

New Mexico State brings its own debut insider, a chile-roasting storyteller from Las Cruces. Two storytellers, one ballgame. Somebody's tale gets a happy ending.

Three questions that decide it:
1. Can the Bearkats slow Jones and the NMSU run game [S3]?
2. Can Sam Houston's offense get into the red zone against a defense that rarely stops anyone there [S3]?
3. Can the Bearkats keep winning the turnover battle (+1) against an NMSU team at -5 [S3]?

7. Local Flavor

I'll tell you about my Huntsville haunts once I've confirmed them. Bring a lawn chair and a story. Not an ad.

report.title: "Paint It Blue": Thatcher Bluestem Takes the Blue Turf Spirit to Pullman
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Paint it blue! Howdy, friends, I'm Thatcher Bluestem, and yes, my car is blue, my pancakes are blue and my opinions are the bluest you'll ever hear. I travel with the Broncos and I live with the Broncos, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, loud and sunny and endlessly proud. Visitors always ask me if the field really looks that blue in person. Friend, it looks bluer. Bring sunglasses and an open mind. Here's the thing about me: no matter how good this team gets, I carry myself like we're the scrappy kids from the foothills nobody invited to the party. Old habits. We earned every seat at the table, and I'll never take one of them for granted. Smurf Turf, baby, show some respect. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Boise State was established in 1933 and now plays in the Pac-12 [S6]. The Broncos have won 23 conference championships and six division titles in the Mountain West's Mountain Division [S6]. Home is Albertsons Stadium, on campus in Boise, listed at 36,387 seats [S6][S2], and yes, that's where the famous blue turf lives. The last five years: 7-5, 10-4, 8-6, a glorious 12-2 in 2024 and 9-5 in 2025, all in the Mountain West [S2]. This is our first ride through the new Pac-12, and so far we're 2-0 in league play [S2]. Blue all the way down.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Spencer Danielson is the head coach [S6]; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 3, 2023 [S2]. Danielson's Broncos run the ball and keep it: 234.5 rushing yards a game (9th in FBS), 35 points a game (37th) and 450.5 total yards (27th) [S5]. Friends, we lead the entire country in time of possession at 36:41 a game [S5]. We convert 50.6% of third downs, 16th in FBS [S5]. And we take care of the football: only 3 turnovers in six games [S2], a plus-3 margin [S5]. The defense stops the run, 106.8 yards allowed a game (29th) [S5], and its red zone defense ranks 30th [S5]. Where we need work: the pass defense allows 261.3 yards a game, 126th in FBS [S5]. I'm loud, not blind.

4. Players to Know

• QB Maddux Madsen: 110 of 166 for 1,296 yards, 13 touchdowns and zero interceptions [S4][S5]. Zero! That's bluer than a cloudless October sky.
• RB Dylan Riley: 835 yards on 127 carries, 6 TD [S4][S5]. At Fresno State he ran 19 times for 150 yards and a touchdown and caught four passes for 64 yards and another score [S5].
• WR Rasean Jones: 23 catches, 359 yards, 1 TD [S4][S5]. Matt Wagner had five catches for 46 yards at Fresno [S5].
• LB Boen Phelps: team-high 35 tackles [S4]. LB Max Stege: 2.5 sacks [S4]. DB Travis Anderson: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Boise State is 5-1, 2-0 in the Pac-12, and ranked No. 21 by the AP and No. 22 in the coaches poll [S2][S5]. We opened with a 34-27 loss at Oregon, then rolled: Memphis 38-20, South Dakota 38-24, at Western Michigan 32-7, Utah State 37-18 and at Fresno State 38-31 [S2]. Then we had a week off to rest [S2]. After Pullman, Texas State comes to the blue turf on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing standings math, friends, but an unbeaten league record keeps the dream bright and blue.

report.title: "Thin Air, Thick Defense": Ansel Rimrock Welcomes the Aztecs to Fort Collins
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Thin air, thick defense. Hello, friends, I'm Ansel Rimrock. Most mornings you'll find me on a trail in the foothills west of town, and on fall Saturdays you'll find me with the Rams. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. I'm a calm guy, but don't mistake calm for quiet: I'm competitive right down to my trail shoes. I think football is just a long trail run with blocking. You pace yourself, you climb, you don't panic on the switchbacks, and you finish strong. Fort Collins on a fall Saturday is green and gold from the foothills to the stadium. Visiting teams breathe a little harder up here, and our kids love it. Ram tough, trail ready. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Colorado State Rams compete in the Pac-12 [S7]. Our big rivalries are with Colorado, Wyoming and Air Force [S7]. We've played at Canvas Stadium since 2017; before that, the Rams spent 49 seasons, 1968 to 2016, at Sonny Lubick Field at Hughes Stadium [S7]. CFBD lists Canvas at 36,500 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were a steep climb: 3-9, 3-9, 5-7, a nice 8-5 in 2024 and then 2-10 in 2025 [S3]. Every trail has a hard stretch. We're climbing out of one.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Jim Mora was hired on Nov. 26, 2025, and this is his first season [S7]. The offense can move: 445.3 yards a game (34th), 35.7 points (29th) and 274.7 passing yards (26th) [S5]. And we take care of the ball. We've turned it over only 4 times [S3] and taken it away 12 times [S3], good for a plus-8 margin, 6th in FBS [S5]. We play disciplined, 42.3 penalty yards a game (17th) [S5]. Now the hard switchback, friends. The defense is allowing 530.3 yards a game, 274.3 rushing yards and 43.2 points, all 138th in FBS [S5]. I said thick defense. I'm still waiting for the thick part. It'll come.

4. Players to Know

• QB K'saan Farrar: 89 of 144 for 931 yards, 5 TD, 2 INT [S4][S5]. At Texas State he went 26 of 41 for 282 yards, two touchdowns and no interceptions [S5].
• RB Brown: 431 yards on just 47 carries, 3 TD. That's more than nine yards a carry [S4][S5]. Heads-up: ESPN lists him as Mel Brown and AP as Jayden Brown; I'm showing both [S4][S5].
• WR Reginald "RJ" Vick Jr.: 24 catches, 367 yards, 4 TD [S4][S5]. WR Jackson Harper: five catches for 91 yards at Texas State [S5].
• LB Oumar Diomande: team-high 54 tackles [S4]. DL Jack Moran: 1.5 sacks [S4]. CB CJ Blocker: 3 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Colorado State is 2-4 and 0-2 in the Pac-12 [S3]. The season started fast: Wyoming 35-13 in the rivalry, then Southern Utah 58-24 [S3]. Then a tough climb: BYU 41-23, a 59-45 shootout at UTSA, Oregon State 56-26 and at Texas State 66-27 [S3]. After San Diego State, we visit Utah State on Oct. 31 [S5]. I don't do standings math on a trail. I just look at the next switchback.
Season so far, in trail terms: the first two miles were downhill and fast. Then came four straight climbs against BYU, UTSA, Oregon State and Texas State, and the legs got heavy [S3]. Every trail runner knows that feeling. You don't quit at mile four. You drink some water, shorten your stride and keep going.
The good news: beating Wyoming is never a small thing up here [S3]. And scoring 45 at UTSA shows how fast this offense can move [S3].

6. This Week: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6:30 p.m. ET (4:30 p.m. Mountain) · Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins · The CW [S1][S5][S8].

Their offense vs. our defense: San Diego State averages 292.9 yards (133rd) and converts only 29.3% of third downs (135th) [S5]. But it runs it, 144.4 yards a game, and Lucky Sutton ran for 110 last week [S5]. Our run defense has to win this climb.
Ball control: San Diego State's average time of possession is 24:47, 138th in FBS [S5]. We'll have the ball plenty.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].

What decides it: (1) Our run defense against Kinnard and Sutton. (2) Farrar against a 131st-ranked pass defense. (3) Our plus-8 turnover habit [S5].
To Kai Delgado-Sorensen, San Diego State's insider: holding your breath under a wave is one thing. Try running a mile at 5,000 feet. I'll lend you a water bottle.

Why I Love This Team

I love that this team keeps hold of the football [S3]. I love that Brown averages more than nine yards a carry [S4]. I love that this is a first-year staff building something [S7]. And I love Fort Collins in late October, when the foothills turn and the stadium fills up. Ram tough, trail ready.
