report.title: "Gnarly": Kai Delgado-Sorensen Paddles Out to Fort Collins
report.byline: Kai Delgado-Sorensen · San Diego State Insider
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Gnarly. Hey, dudes and dudettes, I'm Kai Delgado-Sorensen. I'm out in the water at Ocean Beach most mornings before the sun's all the way up, and I'm at every Aztecs game when it goes down. I travel with this team and I live with this team, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines. Fair warning: I rate defenses by swell size. A soft defense is ankle-high mush. A great one is a ten-foot wall, totally gnarly. Don't let the surfer drawl fool you, though. I've watched every snap this season, some of them twice, with a notebook full of salt stains. When we win, I yell "Gnarly!" and mime catching a wave. When we lose, it's "Wipeout, dude," and I paddle right back out. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

The Aztecs represent San Diego State University and began playing football in 1921 [S6]. We went to our first bowl game in 1948 and won our first major bowl in 1969 [S6]. The Aztecs have won 21 conference championships and are 10-10 all-time in bowl games [S6]. Now we play in the Pac-12, at Snapdragon Stadium, which opened in 2022 and seats 35,000 [S6][S2]. The last five seasons had some big waves and some flat days: 12-2 in 2021, 7-6, 4-8, 3-9 and then a 9-4 bounce back last year [S2].

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Sean Lewis is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Nov. 29, 2023 [S2]. Real talk, dudes: the offense has been flat water this year. We average 292.9 yards (133rd in FBS) and 23.3 points (101st) [S5]. The passing game is 148.4 yards a game (132nd) [S5], and we convert 29.3% of third downs (135th) [S5]. Our run game, 144.4 a game, is 87th [S5]. The defense has given up 449 yards a game (133rd) and 33.3 points (127th) [S5]. But here's the thing: the pass rush is real. We have 16 sacks [S2], and linebacker Djibril Rahman has 4 [S4]. And the Aztecs have found ways to win close ones: 31-29 over Texas State and 26-23 over Fresno State [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Jayden Denegal: 83 of 151, about 900 yards (ESPN says 899, AP says 896), 7 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. Against Fresno he was efficient, 7 of 10 for 112 and a score [S5].
• RB Javion Kinnard: 432 yards on 81 carries, 1 TD [S4][S5].
• RB Lucky Sutton: 110 rushing yards on 18 carries against Fresno State [S5]. That's a set wave, dude.
• WR Nathan Acevedo: 17 catches, 181 yards, 2 TD [S4][S5]. WR Jaylon Hawkins: six catches for 84 yards and a touchdown against Fresno [S5].
• LB Sione Hala: team-high 67 tackles [S4]. LB Djibril Rahman: 4 sacks [S4]. CB Mike Lindsay: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

San Diego State is 3-4 and 2-1 in the Pac-12 [S2]. We're 3-1 at home and 0-3 on the road [S2]. The season: a 53-20 win over Portland State, losses at UCLA 28-10, to James Madison 26-13 and at Toledo 41-16, a 31-29 win over Texas State, a rough 66-14 loss at Oregon State, and then a 26-23 win over Fresno State [S2]. After Fort Collins, we host Washington State on Oct. 31 [S5]. Not doing table math, dude. But a winning league record is a nice place to be standing up on the board.
The road thing: we haven't won away from home yet [S2]. Every surfer knows a new break takes some figuring out. This is the one to figure out.
Why I love this team: it keeps paddling back out. After the Oregon State wipeout, these dudes came home and beat Fresno State by three [S2]. Sione Hala leads the team with 67 tackles and seems to be in on every play [S4]. That's a surfer who never gets out of the water.

6. This Week: San Diego State (3-4) at Colorado State (2-4)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6:30 p.m. ET · Canvas Stadium, Fort Collins · The CW [S1][S5][S8].
Last week: we beat Fresno State 26-23 on Oct. 17 [S5]. Colorado State lost 66-27 at Texas State on Oct. 15 [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Colorado State gives up 530.3 yards a game (138th) and 274.3 rushing yards (138th) [S5]. Opponents convert 43.7% of third downs against them (133rd) [S5]. Dudes, that's knee-high mush. Kinnard and Sutton should be paddling in.
Their offense vs. our defense: this is a real swell. Colorado State scores 35.7 points (29th) and throws for 274.7 yards a game (26th) [S5]. Quarterback K'saan Farrar threw for 282 yards last week [S5]. And the Rams have a plus-8 turnover margin, 6th in FBS, while we're minus-2 [S5]. Our 131st-ranked pass defense has to show up [S5].
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Our run game against the 138th-ranked run defense. (2) Slowing Farrar and receiver Reginald Vick Jr. (3) Holding onto the ball against a team that takes it away [S5].
To Ansel Rimrock, Colorado State's insider: thin air? Brah, I hold my breath under a six-foot set every morning. We'll be fine. Respect, though.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

Back in San Diego? Eureka! on La Jolla Village Drive makes a solid burger after a dawn patrol.

report.title: "Go With the Flow": Yesenia Calderwood Floats the Bobcats Into Week 8

Eat 'em up, Cats! Hey, y'all, I'm Yesenia Calderwood, and if you can't find me at a Bobcats game, I'm probably floating down the San Marcos River on an inner tube with a sun hat and a radio. I travel with the Bobcats and I live with the Bobcats, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, sunny and laid-back but fiercely proud. San Marcos has a clear, cold river and a hot, rising football team. Grab a tube, grab a seat, and enjoy the ride with us. My motto for life and football: go with the flow, then run it up the middle. When we win, I'm floating on air. When we lose, I let the river carry it away and get ready for next week. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Texas State football began in 1904 and has an overall winning record [S7]. The program has 14 conference titles, nine of them outright [S7]. As of 2026, the Bobcats play in the Pac-12 [S7]. Texas State is now the fourth-largest university in Texas [S7]. And the recent current is strong: 4-8, 4-8, then 8-5, 8-5 and 7-6 [S3]. That's a river rising.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

We run for 303.5 a game, 3rd in the country, and score 40 points a game, 9th [S5]. We convert 56.1% of third downs, 4th [S5]. That's going with the flow, then running it up the middle, over and over. The defense is where the water gets choppy: 297.3 passing yards allowed a game, 137th, and 32.2 points (122nd) [S5]. And our turnover margin is minus-5 [S5]. Here's the thing, though: when an offense moves like this, every possession is a chance to put points on the board. We hold the ball 31:30 a game, 37th in FBS [S5]. Keep the defense rested, keep the river flowing, and good things happen.

4. Players to Know

• QB Brad Jackson: 106 of 157 for 1,439 yards, 14 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. Against Colorado State he went 14 of 19 for 213 yards and a touchdown, and ran 13 times for 181 yards and three more scores [S5]. Whoa, that's a waterfall.

Just know a home win keeps us floating.
The close ones: five points against UTSA and two points at San Diego State [S3]. A couple of bounces, and this record looks a lot different.
Season so far, from the tube: the Texas game was cold water, a shock to the system [S3]. Since then, this offense has scored 26, 49, 63, 29 and 66 [S3]. That's a river that keeps rising, and it's the most treasured part of my fall.

report.title: "Udderly Dominant": Hyrum Tolleson Brings Cache Valley Heart to San Marcos
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Go Aggies! Well, hello there, neighbors. I'm Hyrum Tolleson, and I've spent most of my life on a dairy up in Cache Valley, which is a fancy way of saying I've been up before the sun since I was eight years old. I travel with the Aggies and I live with the Aggies, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, slow and steady, the way you'd tell a story over the fence. I'm a patient man. It takes a lot to get me riled, and a lot less to get me laughing. Logan sits in a valley so pretty it almost feels unfair. Our Aggies play with that small-town heart, and afterward, everybody goes for ice cream. I always order a double scoop of Aggie Ice Cream, win or lose. When we play well, that's udderly dominant. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Utah State football was established in 1892, which makes it one of the oldest programs in the western United States [S6]. We play in the Pac-12 now [S6]. Home since 1968 has been Merlin Olsen Field at Maverik Stadium in Logan [S6], listed at 25,513 seats [S2]. The field is named for Merlin Olsen, a Pro Football Hall of Famer who played here [S6]. The Aggies have won 13 conference championships across four different leagues, most recently in 2021 [S6], the year we went 11-3 [S2]. Since then: 6-7, 6-7, 4-8 and 6-7 [S2]. Steady folks. We'll get the herd back to the top.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Bronco Mendenhall is the head coach; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 6, 2024 [S2]. Now, I'll be straight with you, neighbors, because that's the dairy way. The offense has had a hard time: 310 yards a game (129th in FBS) and 14.5 points (136th) [S5]. We've allowed 19 sacks [S2] and turned it over 12 times [S2], a minus-6 margin [S5]. The defense is the steady cow in the barn: 23.5 points allowed (66th) and 140.8 rushing yards allowed (68th) [S5]. It's kept us close. Four of our six games were decided by 12 points or fewer, including a 16-14 loss at Washington and a 17-16 win over Washington State [S2].

4. Players to Know

• QB Grady Brosterhous: 78 of 142 for 914 yards, 7 TD, 6 INT [S4][S5]. Against Washington State he threw for 150 yards and a touchdown [S5].
• RB Javen Jacobs: 393 yards on 70 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5]. He ran for 62 yards and a touchdown against Washington State [S5].
• WR Eli Wood: 36 catches, 472 yards, 5 TD [S4][S5]. Six catches for 84 yards and a touchdown last time out [S5]. Now that's a fine young man.
• S Brevin Hamblin: team-high 50 tackles and an interception [S4]. LB Jordan Pendleton: 2.5 sacks [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Utah State is 2-4 and 1-1 in the Pac-12 [S2]. The season: a 29-17 loss to Idaho State, a 16-14 loss at Washington, 33-0 at Utah, a 21-10 win over Troy, a 37-18 loss at Boise State and a 17-16 win over Washington State [S2]. We had last week off [S2]. After San Marcos, Colorado State comes to Logan on Oct. 31 [S5]. I won't do standings math, neighbors. I'll just say a .500 league record keeps the barn lights on.
On the road: we're 0-3 away from home this year [S2], and three of those trips were to Washington, Utah and Boise State. Tough barns.
Season so far: the Washington game still sticks with me. Two points, on the road, against a Big Ten team [S2]. That told me plenty about this team's heart. And the 17-16 win over Washington State? I had ice cream for dinner that night.

6. This Week: Utah State (2-4) at Texas State (3-3)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 7:30 p.m. ET (5:30 p.m. Mountain) · San Marcos, Texas · CBS Sports Network [S1][S5][S8]. CFBD calls the venue Bobcat Stadium; Wikipedia calls it UFCU Stadium [S3][S7].
Last time out: we beat Washington State 17-16 on Oct. 9 [S5]. Texas State beat Colorado State 66-27 on Oct. 15 [S5].
Their offense vs. our defense: here's the challenge, neighbors. Texas State leads the entire country in total offense, 562.3 yards a game, and runs for 303.5 a game (3rd) [S5]. They convert 56.1% of third downs (4th) [S5]. Running back Torrance Burgess Jr. has 838 yards [S5], and quarterback Brad Jackson ran for 181 yards and three touchdowns last game [S5]. That's a stampede. Our defense has to tackle.
Our offense vs. their defense: Texas State allows 297.3 passing yards a game, 137th in FBS [S5]. Brosterhous and Eli Wood should have a chance to make plays.
One more: Texas State scores on only 71% of its red zone trips (128th) [S5]. If we bend, we must not break.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S10].
Availability: no official availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S9].
What decides it: (1) Tackling the run game. (2) Our passing game against the 137th-ranked pass defense. (3) Holding onto the ball; both teams are below even in turnovers [S5].
To Yesenia Calderwood, Texas State's insider: a river float sounds lovely. Come see Logan sometime, and the ice cream's on me.

Why I Love This Team

I love that this team keeps showing up, even when the scoreboard is rough. I love Eli Wood's hands [S4]. I love that Utah State has been playing football since 1892 [S6]. And I love that after every game, win or lose, Logan goes out for ice cream. Go Aggies!

report.title: "Wave the Flag": Hank Palouse Welcomes the Broncos to the Palouse
report.text:
THE FANATIC EDITION

1. Meet Your Insider

Wave the flag. Howdy, neighbors, I'm Hank Palouse. I drive a combine for a living out in the wheat country, and I haven't missed a game in Pullman since cassette tapes. And yes, I still have the tapes. A whole shoebox of them, labeled by year, in the cab of my pickup. I travel with the Cougars and I live with the Cougars, and every week I'll bring you the players, the matchups, the history and the storylines, with a little dry Palouse humor and a lot of love for Ol' Crimson, the flag that shows up at every big game in the country. When we win, I wave Ol' Crimson right here in the studio. When we lose, I say "Cougs never quit," and then I tell you a 20-minute story about harvest. You've been warned. (Fictional character.)

2. The School in 60 Seconds

Washington State University is in Pullman, and the first Cougar football team took the field in 1894 [S7]. We play in the Pac-12 [S7]. Home is Martin Stadium, which opened in 1972; the ground there dates back to 1892, when it was called Soldier Field [S7]. CFBD lists the venue as Gesa Field, 32,952 seats [S3]. The last five seasons were 7-6, 7-6, 5-7, 8-5 and 7-6 [S3]. Steady folks out here, like the wheat: some years are a bumper crop, some years you pray for rain, but you always plant again.

3. The Coach and the Scheme

Kirby Moore is in his first season; CFBD dates his hire to Dec. 12, 2025 [S3]. I'll be honest, neighbors, because that's how we do it out here: it's been a hard first year. The offense averages 308.3 yards (130th in FBS) and 20.1 points (120th) [S5]. We've allowed 22 sacks [S3] and turned it over 12 times [S3], and our turnover margin is minus-7, 131st [S5]. The defense allows 383.1 yards a game (102nd) and 27.1 points (101st) [S5]. One bright spot: we hold opponents to 37% on third down, 66th in FBS [S5]. And here's the big bright spot. Last week we found a quarterback.

4. Players to Know

• QB Owen Eshelman: the redshirt freshman made his first career start at Oregon State and threw for 289 yards and two touchdowns, ran for 136 yards on 15 carries and a touchdown, and led three straight touchdown drives late [S9]. AP says our 30 points were the most we've scored against an FBS team this season [S9]. That's a foot of fresh topsoil on a dry field, neighbors.
• QB Caden Pinnick: the season passing leader, 110 of 178 for 952 yards, 3 TD, 5 INT [S4][S5]. Who starts this week? I haven't seen it announced [S10].
• WR Branden Ganashamoorthy: 26 catches, 343 yards, 3 TD, and 11 catches for 147 yards and a score last week [S4][S5].
• RB Kirby Vorhees: 267 yards on 54 carries, 2 TD [S4][S5].
• LB Keith Brown: team-high 51 tackles [S4]. DT Jirah Leaupepetele: 2.5 sacks [S4]. S Jaylen Thomas: 2 interceptions [S4].

5. The Conference Picture

Washington State is 1-6 and 0-3 in the Pac-12 [S3]. The schedule has been a grind: at Washington 24-10, at Kansas State 34-7, a 48-7 win over Duquesne, then Arizona 34-24, Fresno State 26-6, a one-point heartbreaker at Utah State 17-16 and at Oregon State 48-30 [S3]. Four of those were on the road [S3]. Next up after Boise, we head to San Diego State on Oct. 31 [S5]. I'm not doing math on the standings, neighbors. I'm doing math on how loud Pullman gets for a ranked visitor.
That one-point game in Logan still sits with me like hail on a ripe field [S3]. But Cougs never quit.
Why I still love this team: because in the fourth quarter at Corvallis, down big, a redshirt freshman in his first start led three straight touchdown drives [S9]. Nobody quit. Nobody ever does out here. That's a tape I'll be labeling and keeping, right next to the good ones from the old days.

6. This Week: No. 21 Boise State (5-1) at Washington State (1-6)

Saturday, Oct. 24 · 6 p.m. ET (3 p.m. Pacific) · Martin Stadium / Gesa Field, Pullman · USA Network [S1][S3][S5][S7][S8].
Their offense vs. our defense: Boise State runs for 234.5 yards a game (9th) and holds the ball 36:41 a game, first in the country [S5]. Dylan Riley has 835 rushing yards [S5]. And Maddux Madsen has 13 touchdown passes with zero interceptions [S5]. If we're going to win, the defense has to get them off the field on third down, and Boise converts 50.6%, 16th in FBS [S5].
Our offense vs. their defense: Boise State's pass defense allows 261.3 yards a game, 126th [S5]. Eshelman just threw for 289 [S9]. Now that's a crop I'd like to harvest.
Series: I couldn't find an all-time series record in a free source [S11].
Availability: no injury or availability report found for either team as of Oct. 18 [S10].
What decides it: (1) Slowing Riley and getting Boise off the field. (2) Eshelman's arm and legs against the 126th-ranked pass defense. (3) Holding onto the football [S5].
To Thatcher Bluestem, Boise State's insider: blue pancakes? Out here we eat our pancakes the color the Lord made them. Come on over and I'll prove it.

7. Local Flavor (unsponsored, not an ad)

In Pullman for the game? Birch & Barley on Southeast Bishop Boulevard is a good sit-down supper, and Shiki on East Main Street does sushi.
